packets.title: Central locked-id allocation for the leap (edge_category 35-36, cell_type 19-25) + six code-domain module slots
packets.rationale: Every new id the leap uses, collected from all eleven final group files and verifier summaries (search of implementation / entry_points / acceptance / fixtures for node_kind / edge_category / cell_type and the ranges node 50-53, edge 35-38, cell 19-28): edge_category 35 NAVIGATES_TO (LA.6a; read by LA.6b-e, LG.11), 38 CO_CHANGES (LF.5b; read by LF.5c/LF.5d, LG.11, LF.2a rejects it by name); cell_type 19 DOC_TAGS (LA.8; LG.12), 20 ROLE (LB.3a; LB.3b, LA.6a, LA.21a/b), 21 EVIDENCE (LC.3a; LC.3b-d, LC.10b, LE.4b/c, LE.5), 25 ACCESS_MODE (LE.4a; LE.4d), 26 SCHEMA_FIELDS (LE.10a/LE.10b; LE.10c), 27 COVERAGE (LF.6c), 28 ENTRYPOINT (LF.3b). No collisions (each group drew from its own sub-range) and no out-of-range use; node_kind 50-53 are unused (LA.3 reuses ATTRIBUTE + HAS_ATTRIBUTE for Rust enum variants and PACKAGE for inline mods; LE/LA-cov1/LD report none). The proposed numbers cannot be allocated as written: the W0.3 guard `registry_ids_are_unique_and_contiguous` (code-domain/src/lib.rs:2183) requires every ALL table to be exactly 1..=len, and cells 22-24 / edges 36-37 would be holes. CLAUDE.md's rule is 'take the next free value'. So the allocation is compacted (W0.3 precedent: A5.3 proposed GRPC_SERVER=45 and got 47). ACCESS_MODE keeps 25 on purpose: every stale number left in a packet's text (26, 27, 28, 38) then names an UNREGISTERED id, which decodes as UNKNOWN and trips the guard test below, instead of silently naming a different registered cell. HEAD state (read at 7a4883b, code = 5280cee): pinned counts 49 / 34 / 18 in the registry test; reserved_ids_decode (:2604) asserts NodeKindId(50), EdgeCategoryId(35), CellTypeId(19) are UNKNOWN (:2618-2620); grade.py raises `unknown category 'NAVIGATES_TO'` / `'CO_CHANGES'` on HEAD (LA-cov2 and LF verifiers). Module slots: code-domain/src/lib.rs is claimed by 20 packets; six of them (A13.1, LC.3a, LD.14a, LF.1a, LF.2a, LF.5a) touch it only to add one `pub mod x;` line next to `pub mod walk_gating;` (:21) / `pub mod project_roots;` (:25). Declaring those six modules here (empty files, doc comment only) lets them edit only their own file; measured with the wave simulator this is worth one wave. The other 14 claimants edit existing code (the inline `pub mod endpoint` - LB.4a, LB.5, A14.6; LocalModuleIndex - A6.8, LA.1b; CodeNav - A6.2a; di_stats - A14.4; registry doc comments - LD.14b, LE.3a, LE.4a, LE.4b; UnresolvedRef/CallSite - LC.2, LC.3b; LD.11a), so this file is NOT split, per the integrator rule. projection-text/src/lib.rs:613 cell_label matches raw cell numbers; LF.3b and LF.6c plan arms `28 => "entry"` and `27 => "coverage"`. packets.rationale: engine/src/lib.rs is claimed by 37 packets (LA.6e, LA.13, LA.14, LB.4a, LC.7, LC.8, LC.9, LC.10b, LD.1, LD.3b, LD.4a, LD.4b, LD.5, LD.6, LD.7c, LD.8a, LD.8b, LD.11a, LD.13, LD.14a, LE.1b, LE.2, LE.3b, LE.4d, LE.5, LE.6b, LE.7a, LE.8, LE.9b, LE.10c, LF.1a, LF.2b, LF.2c, LF.4b, LF.5c, LG.1a, LG.3a). Every one except LD.11a touches it only to add a `mod x;` line and/or names to a `pub use` list (their FACADE notes say so). Under the file-disjoint scheduler that is a 37-wave floor on its own - the same failure W0.1 fixed for the pre-split 44-packet lib.rs. Wave simulation (all leap packets + Batch C, deps patch applied): 63 waves with no wave-0 split, 38 with L0.1-L0.6, 51 with every split except this one. Glob parity verified at HEAD by comparing `grep '^pub ' <module>` with the facade lists (engine/src/lib.rs:31-47): answers.rs has 16 pub items and the list has the same 16; build.rs 6/6; coverage.rs 3/3; extract.rs 2/2. So `pub use m::*` for those four changes no public path. arch.rs and cache.rs are `pub mod` with partial flat lists (arch::FLOW_MECHANISMS and cache::content_hash are not flat) and stay explicit. An empty module cannot be glob re-exported warning-free (rustc 1.95: `unused import` plus `glob import doesn't reexport anything`, measured on a scratch crate), while an empty `pub mod x;` or private `mod x;` compiles clean - hence public module slots rather than pre-declared re-exports. graph query: repo-graph find build_graphs_for_repo -> engine/src/build.rs:460; impact backward depth 1 -> generate_one_inner / generate_many_inner (both flagged dead: the LA.1 full-crate-path blind spot).

Each slot file holds only `//! <purpose>. CONVENTION (written into CLAUDE.md 'Module layout', replacing 'the public API is exactly what the facade re-exports'): (1) the HEAD API stays flat; answers / build / coverage / extract are glob re-exported, so a `pub` item in them IS public API - cross-module helpers stay `pub(crate)`, never `pub`; (2) every new leap primitive is a public module (`repo_graph_engine::delta::graph_delta_vs_rev`, `::persist::load_layout`, `::profile::CODE_PROFILE`), so no later packet edits lib.rs; (3) a packet whose spec says 'FACADE: pub use x::{..}' or 'mod x;' skips that step and its cli/py call sites use the module path. packets.rationale: py/src/lib.rs (783 lines) is claimed by 36 packets and the planned snapshot py/api_surface.txt by 22, py/tests/test_surface.py by 9: nearly every LD / LE / LF surface packet adds a PyGraph method or a module function there. With pyo3's default single `#[pymethods]` block per class and one `#[pymodule]` registration list, a file split alone cannot help - every new method would still edit the one impl block. pyo3 0.28 (py/Cargo.toml:16) has the `multiple-pymethods` feature (pyo3-0.28.3/Cargo.toml:157, needs the `inventory` crate; inventory-0.3.24 is in the local cargo registry cache, so no network). Simulated: removing this split alone moves the leap from 38 to 52 waves. graph query: repo-graph find PyGraph -> 27 nodes (the struct + 26 members, py/src/lib.rs:21-453), matching the LG-h verifier's surface count (11 module functions, 26 PyGraph members). HEAD tests in this crate: 3 (py/src/lib.rs:707, :724, :747), all pyo3-free helpers because a unit test naming a #[pyclass] fails to link under extension-module (py/src/lib.rs:33-38).

packets.implementation:
MECHANISM. (1) pyo3 `multiple-pymethods`: each module carries its own `#[pymethods] impl PyGraph { .. }`; the class is declared once in graph.rs. (2) Module functions self-register: py/src/registry.rs defines `pub(crate) struct ModuleFns { pub name: &'static str, pub add: fn(&Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> }` and `inventory::collect!(ModuleFns);`; every module that owns #[pyfunction]s ends with `fn register(m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> { m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(f, m)?)?; .. Ok(()) }` and `inventory::submit! { ModuleFns { name: "<module>", add: register } }`. lib.rs: `let mut fns: Vec<&ModuleFns> = inventory::iter::<ModuleFns>.into_iter().collect(); fns.sort_by_key(|f| f.name); for f in fns { (f.add)(m)?; } m.add_class::<graph::PyGraph>()?;`. Alternatives weighed: per-area register() calls listed in lib.rs (8 new areas would edit lib.rs again - rejected); declarative `#[pymodule] mod` with #[pymodule_export] (still one list - rejected); keep one file (36-wave floor - rejected). inventory is what multiple-pymethods itself uses, so the mechanism adds no new class of dependency.
MODULES (verbatim moves, imports adjusted, private `mod` in lib.rs): py/src/graph.rs - the #[pyclass] PyGraph struct (fields become pub(crate)) + #[pymethods] parse_errors (getter), node_count, edge_count, cross_edge_count, node_cells, save_to, save_to_default; py/src/convert.rs - escape_json (LD.2 adds the serde_json::Value -> Python converter here); py/src/build.rs - #[pyfunction] generate, generate_many, parse_file_to_json + register(); py/src/layout.rs - #[pyfunction] load_from_gmap, default_gmap_dir, is_stale + register(); py/src/registry.rs - #[pyfunction] kind_names, category_names, cell_type_names, version, build_stamp + register() + the ModuleFns inventory type + test build_stamp_is_the_release_plus_the_parser_stamp; py/src/text.rs - #[pymethods] dense_text, dense_text_full, dense_text_subset, prose, activate; py/src/records.rs - #[pymethods] nodes_json, edges_json; py/src/traversal.rs - #[pymethods] neighbours; py/src/blast.rs - #[pymethods] blast_radius; py/src/trace.rs - #[pymethods] cross_stack_trace; py/src/find.rs - #[pymethods] resolve, find_node, resolve_signal, find_nodes_by_qname; py/src/docs.rs - #[pymethods] governing_docs; py/src/arch.rs - #[pymethods] coverage, project_roots, service_map + service_map_json (and its link-reason doc comment) + test service_map_returns_the_documented_json_object; py/src/contracts.rs - #[pymethods] contracts + contracts_json + test contracts_returns_the_documented_json_array. packets.title: Rust calls inside macro arguments: scan macro token trees for call-shaped token runs (run!/println!/assert_eq!/vec!/format!)
packets.area: LA.2 - Rust call extraction inside macro invocations (parser)
packets.rationale: tree-sitter-rust does not parse macro arguments as expressions: a `macro_invocation` holds a flat `token_tree` (node-types.json of tree-sitter-rust 0.24.2: token_tree children are _literal / identifier / self / super / crate / metavariable / token_tree plus anonymous punctuation), so collect_calls_in (parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs), which only matches `call_expression`, never sees a call written inside one. repo-graph `impact parsers::code::extractors::src::queues::extract_queue_consumer_nodes` (backward, depth 1) at HEAD: "No backward nodes found" - its only caller is `run_with_edges!(queues::extract_queue_consumer_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo))` in engine/src/extract.rs apply_cross_cutting_extractors, one of 24 run!/run_counted!/run_marked!/run_with_edges! invocations there; 39 of the 65 `extract_*` FUNCTIONs in parsers/code/extractors have no CALLS in on the self-graph. Probe fixture below: CALLS 1/4 - only the control call outside any macro resolves; helper() inside run!/println!/assert_eq!/vec!, fmt_id() nested in println!, and self.name() inside format! are all invisible. The same gap drops `println!("{}", greet())` in fixtures/rust-axum-imports and `assert_eq!(add(2, 3), 5)` in matrix/rust/tests.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN. (a) Re-parse the token tree's text as an expression list wrapped in a synthetic `fn __m() { __f(<args>); }` - REJECTED: a second tree-sitter parse per macro, every position has to be re-offset (LC.3 wants call-site positions), and DSL macros whose arguments are not expressions (`select!` arms, `matches!` patterns, `html!`) either fail to parse or parse into wrong calls. (b) Scan the token tree for call-shaped token runs - CHOSEN: no second parse, real positions, and it degrades to 'no call found' on any shape it does not recognise.

NEW fn in parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs (~110 LOC + tests):
```rust
/// Calls written inside a macro invocation's arguments. Returns the number of CallSites pushed.
fn collect_macro_calls(invocation: TsNode, src: &[u8], from: NodeId, acc: &mut Acc) -> usize
fn scan_token_tree(tt: TsNode, src: &[u8], from: NodeId, pattern_tail: bool, depth: usize, acc: &mut Acc) -> usize
```
Collect ALL children of the token_tree (named and anonymous - `::`, `.`, `!`, `,` are anonymous) into a Vec and walk an index i:
- PATH CALL: tok[i] is identifier | self | super | crate (text not starting with `$`), followed by zero or more (`::`, identifier) pairs ending at j; if tok[j] is a token_tree whose first child is `(` -> one CallSite: a single segment -> Bare(name) unless name is in the keyword stop-list; several -> Attribute{base: segments[..n-1].join("::"), name: last} (same shape classify_call gives a scoped_identifier). Then scan tok[j] recursively.
- NESTED MACRO: path followed by `!` and a token_tree -> no CallSite for the macro name; recurse into that token_tree.
- METHOD CALL: tok[i] is `.`, tok[i+1] identifier, tok[i+2] token_tree starting `(` -> receiver = tok[i-1]: `self` -> SelfMethod(name); a lone identifier -> Attribute{base, name}; anything else -> ComplexReceiver{receiver: text, name}.
- every other token_tree -> recurse; depth cap 32; literals are single tokens, so text inside a string (`"fmt_id(1)"`) can never match.
PATTERN MACROS: when the invocation's macro name (last path segment) is `matches`, `assert_matches` or `debug_assert_matches`, scan only the tokens before the first top-level `,` - the rest is a pattern, where `Some(Wrap(_))` is not a call. Keyword stop-list for Bare names: as async await break const continue dyn else enum extern false fn for if impl in let loop match mod move mut pub ref return static struct trait true type unsafe use where while yield (defensive: tree-sitter may lex a keyword inside a token tree as an identifier).
collect_calls_in: `if n.kind() == "macro_invocation" { collect_macro_calls(n, src, from, acc); }` - its token_tree children contain no call_expression, so the existing stack walk needs no other change. CallSites are per site like ordinary calls (no dedup).
Path-shaped sites (`util::scaled(3)`, `queues::extract_queue_consumer_nodes(..)`) produce Attribute CallSites exactly like a non-macro path call; they turn into edges through LA.1a/LA.1b. This packet's own gate asserts the CallSite shape for them and the resolved edge only for bare and self calls, so it has no ordering dependency.
MARKER: one `static RUST_DEBUG: OnceLock<bool>` reading GLIA_RUST_DEBUG; when set and a file produced >= 1 macro call site, `eprintln!("[rust-macro-calls] {file_rel}: {n} call site(s) in {m} macro invocation(s)")` at the end of parse_file (the A2.1 `[queues] scan` precedent: a per-file line is too noisy to be always on for a feature that fires in most Rust files).
UNIT TESTS (parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs tests mod): macro_arg_calls_are_extracted (the fixture's entry(): CallSites include Bare(helper) x4, Bare(fmt_id), Bare(total), and for `vec![util::scaled(3)]` Attribute{base:"util", name:"scaled"}); string_literal_in_macro_is_not_a_call; matches_pattern_is_not_a_call (`matches!(w, Some(Wrap(_)))` yields no Bare(Wrap)); self_method_inside_format (SelfMethod("name")); nested_macro_recurses (`vec![format!("{}", f(1))]` -> Bare(f), no CallSite named vec or format).

packets.rationale: parse_file (parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs) makes two passes over `root.named_children` only, and neither pass has a `mod_item` arm, so an inline module is not a node AND nothing inside it is either: repo-graph `find url_to_path` (kind=symbol) -> "No nodes matched" and `find code-domain::src::lib::endpoint` -> "No nodes matched", although `pub mod endpoint { pub fn url_to_path .. }` (code-domain/src/lib.rs) is used by a dozen parsers; `node_kind`, `edge_category`, `cell_type`, `infra` and `di_stats` are inline mods too. glia holds 111 inline `mod x {` blocks, 95 of them `mod tests` (verifier: `git ls-files '*.rs' | xargs grep -hE '^\s*(pub(\([^)]*\))? )?mod \w+\s*\{'`), so its 997 in-source #[test] fns (outside tests/ dirs) are absent. Enum variants are never walked: `find MatchTier` returns the ENUM and its method `ceiling`, no variant. Probe fixture below at HEAD: 0/9 nodes, CONTAINS 0/1, HAS_ATTRIBUTE 0/1, USES 0/4, CALLS 0/4 (the fns inside `mod endpoint` and `mod tests` do not exist, so nothing can call them or be called from them). Also measured: an `impl MatchTier { fn rank(&self) { self.weight() } }` self-call is unresolved because graph::calls::enclosing_class_or_struct accepts CLASS/STRUCT only; the same walk fails for every method of an impl block whose type is defined in another file (visit_impl parents those methods to the MODULE). Kind choice: Python's parser already emits Enum members as ATTRIBUTE + HAS_ATTRIBUTE (probe: `class Color(Enum): RED = 1` -> ATTRIBUTE colors::Color::RED), so Rust variants reuse ATTRIBUTE and the reserved node_kind 50 is NOT taken; inline mods reuse PACKAGE, the kind C#/PHP/Ruby/C++/Elixir already give an in-file namespace (joined to its file MODULE by CONTAINS). VERIFIER FINDING (precision): graph::calls::resolve_calls resolves a Bare call against the FILE MODULE's symbols before the enclosing PACKAGE's (the Elixir order, graph/src/calls.rs:37-51), so once inline mods exist, `mod endpoint { fn url_to_path() { helper() } fn helper() {} }` beside a file-level `fn helper()` would bind the call to the FILE's helper - a wrong edge, and the hook cannot fix it because it only runs after a generic hit/miss. Rust scoping is innermost-first; this packet resolves inline-mod Bare calls through the PACKAGE chain before the generic pass (fixture guard below).

packets.implementation:
PARSER (parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs, ~200 LOC):
```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Scope { qname: String, id: NodeId }   // the file MODULE, or an inline-mod PACKAGE
fn visit_items(container: TsNode /* source_file | declaration_list */, scope: &Scope, file_rel: &str, repo: RepoId, src: &[u8], acc: &mut Acc)
```
visit_items does, per container: pass 1 = struct_item / enum_item / trait_item -> nodes as today (qname `<scope.qname>::<Name>`, DEFINES scope -> type, nav parent scope.id) into a LOCAL `type_ids` map; pass 2 = function_item / impl_item / const_item / static_item / use_declaration / attribute_item exactly as today but with `scope`, plus `mod_item`: when it has a `body` (declaration_list) -> PACKAGE node qname `<scope.qname>::<name>`, nav.record(id, name, qname, PACKAGE, Some(scope.id)), edge scope.id --CONTAINS--> id, cells POSITION + DOC only (no CODE: a module block's text is every child's CODE again), then recurse visit_items(body, &Scope{qname, id}); `mod x;` (no body) emits nothing - the file module exists on its own. USE INSIDE AN INLINE MOD: collect_use records it with from_module = the PACKAGE qname. graph::imports::resolve_imports_python looks from_module up in module_by_qname (MODULEs only) and skips it, so until LA.1b a `use` inside `mod tests` binds NOTHING - deliberately: recording it against the file module would leak a test-only import into file-level resolution. `self` inside an inline mod means the innermost PACKAGE, `super` its nav parent (file MODULE or outer PACKAGE) - LA.1a's resolve_path rules (2)/(3) read nav parents, so this holds once PACKAGEs exist.
parse_file keeps emitting the file MODULE first (engine/src/build.rs apply_rpc_needles pairs a parse to its file by `fp.nodes.first()`), then calls visit_items(root, &file_scope). Items inside a PACKAGE get DEFINES from the PACKAGE (the Elixir defmodule precedent), so graph::build_symbol_table indexes them under the PACKAGE (it already indexes PACKAGE children) and graph::calls::enclosing_module still walks up to the file MODULE, which is why a bare call from a `mod tests` fn to a parent-file fn resolves with no new resolver code (`use super::*` in effect).
ENUM VARIANTS: for each enum_item, every `enum_variant` in body -> ATTRIBUTE node qname `<enum qname>::<Variant>`, cells = entity_cells (CODE + POSITION + DOC), edge ENUM --HAS_ATTRIBUTE--> variant, nav parent ENUM. Tuple, struct and unit variants alike; the discriminant `value` is part of CODE.
VARIANT REFERENCES (inside collect_calls_in, per fn/method): (1) a `scoped_identifier` whose `name` and the last segment of its `path` both start with an ASCII uppercase letter, in value or pattern position; (2) a call_expression whose `function` is such a scoped_identifier (tuple-variant construction `MatchTier::Suffix(3)`) - emit the USES ref and NO CallSite; (3) tuple_struct_pattern `type`, struct_expression / struct_pattern `name` that are scoped. Each -> UnresolvedRef{from: fn id, from_module: file MODULE id, qualifier: Attribute{base: path text, name}, category: USES}, deduped per (from, base, name) inside one fn so a 40-arm match is one edge per variant. Associated consts that pass the case test (`Self::MAX`) simply stay unresolved.

GRAPH (graph/src/rust_paths.rs + build.rs, ~110 LOC):
INLINE-MOD BARE PRE-PASS (the precision fix): build_rust partitions all_calls, preserving order, into (a) Bare sites whose `from` has at least one PACKAGE ancestor in nav.parent_of and (b) the rest. For (a), `RustIndex::resolve_scoped_bare(g, site)` walks the PACKAGE ancestors innermost-first and returns the first `g.symbols.module_symbols[pkg][name]` hit (build_symbol_table already indexes PACKAGE children); a hit -> push_edge(CALLS) directly; a miss joins (b) at its original position. Then `resolve_calls(&mut g, &rest, hook)` as LA.1a wrote it - so a miss still reaches the file MODULE's symbols (the `use super::*` case, e.g. a test fn calling its parent file's fn). Non-Rust graphs never run this; Rust sites outside inline mods are untouched. RustIndex's member map adds, for every ENUM id, its nav children (ATTRIBUTE and METHOD) by name, sorted by qname. resolve_call: for SelfMethod(name) (generic enclosing_class_or_struct already missed) walk nav parents to the first ENUM/STRUCT/CLASS and look the member up; when the caller METHOD's parent is a MODULE (visit_impl parents a method to its module when the impl'd type lives in another file - e.g. graph/src/blast.rs `impl MergedGraph` over the struct in merged.rs, where `self.all_edges()` and `self.activate(..)` are unresolved today) take the type segment of the caller's own qname, find that type crate-locally (unique STRUCT/ENUM of that name) and look the member up there, else in LA.1a's impl_elsewhere index. New `pub(crate) fn resolve_leftover_refs(&self, g: &mut RepoGraph)`: drain g.unresolved_refs, for each ref with category USES and an Attribute qualifier call resolve_path(r.from, base, name); hits push_edge(r.from, target, USES), misses go back to unresolved_refs in their original order. build_rust calls it right after resolve_refs.
MARKER (build_rust, once per Rust graph): `[rust-items] inline_mods=N fns_in_inline_mods=F enum_variants=V variant_uses=R/T enum_self_calls=S mod_scoped_calls=M` (M = pre-pass hits) - counted off the built graph (PACKAGE nodes whose file is .rs, ATTRIBUTE children of ENUMs, resolved/total USES refs), so cache-served files count too.

TESTS: parser unit tests inline_mod_items_are_nodes (PACKAGE + fn inside + nested mod qnames + CONTAINS), mod_without_body_emits_nothing, enum_variants_are_attributes (4 ATTRIBUTE with HAS_ATTRIBUTE), variant_refs_are_uses_refs (tier/mk/named/classify refs; no CallSite for `MatchTier::Suffix(3)`), and the existing enums_and_traits keeps its ENUM/INTERFACE counts. engine/tests/rust_inline_items.rs (tempfile + generate_one over the fixture source) asserts every expect_edges row of the fixture by qname, plus the three forbids (the shadowing one proves the pre-pass runs before the generic Bare order).

packets.risks: (1) The visitor refactor must preserve every existing node's qname and order within a file for top-level items - diff a Rust fixture's node list before/after as part of the gate. (2) The file MODULE must stay `fp.nodes[0]` (apply_rpc_needles relies on it). (3) Graph growth on glia itself (~+1,100 FUNCTION nodes, Weak) - measure node/edge counts before/after and report them; PPR and dense-text budgets absorb it, but say so. (4) Uppercase heuristics: `Type::CONST` refs stay unresolved (harmless); a CamelCase associated fn would be misread as a variant ref only if someone names a fn in CamelCase. (5) Test fns are not entrypoints (is_entrypoint keys on the name `test*`, not #[test]) - LD.6 owns entry kinds; noted as a cross-group item. (6) Must not widen graph::calls::enclosing_class_or_struct or reorder the generic Bare lookup (calls.rs) - both are shared by every language; the Rust pre-pass is the only place inline-mod scoping lives. (7) LocalModuleIndex (code-domain) adds every PACKAGE qname's segments to its local-path set, so an external crate that shares a name with an inline mod (e.g. a crate `tests`) would be filtered from the IMPORTS cell - acceptable, noted for LA.1b. (8) The pre-pass is lookup-only over sorted/keyed maps; never choose a candidate by HashMap iteration.

packets.title: Rust `use` trees resolved as Rust paths: workspace-crate uses, `pub use` re-exports, aliases, globs and fn-body uses bind; external crates reach the IMPORTS cell
packets.area: LA.1 - Rust call resolution (use-tree extraction + resolve_imports_rust)
packets.rationale: LA.1a resolves calls that spell a path; most Rust calls are bare names bound by a `use`. collect_use (parsers/code/rust/src/lib.rs) only emits `use crate::..` and `use super::..`, strips `crate::`, and drops every other form with the comment "External crate imports (std::, etc.) - skip": a workspace crate (`use repo_graph_engine::{generate_one, ..}` at the top of cli/src/main.rs), a child module (`pub use arch::{service_map, ..}` - every engine/graph facade line), a glob (`use super::*`), and any `use` inside a fn body (engine/src/extract.rs apply_cross_cutting_extractors opens with `use repo_graph_code_extractors::{anchor, angular, cli, .., queues, ..};`) are all lost. The same drop empties the Rust IMPORTS cell: library_name (code-domain) is written for raw paths (it drops crate/self/super/std/core/alloc) but never sees `serde` or `tokio`. Probe fixture below: CALLS 0/4, IMPORTS 0/1, IMPORTS-cell 0/1 at HEAD. Rust imports currently ride resolve_imports_python, which only works because the parser pre-strips `crate::` and the tail fallback binds by unique name.

packets.implementation:
ENCODING (no type change - ImportStmt / ImportTarget are rkyv-archived and shared by 16 parsers). Paths keep their first segment verbatim (`crate`, `self`, `super`, a crate or module name):
- `use a::b::c;` -> Symbol{module:"a::b", name:"c", alias:None, level:0}; `use a::b::c as d;` -> alias Some("d")
- `use a::b::{self, c};` -> Module{path:"a::b", alias:None} + Symbol{module:"a::b", name:"c"}; nested groups flatten with the prefix joined
- `use a::b::*;` -> Symbol{module:"a::b", name:"*"} (the glob marker)
- `use a;` / `use a as b;` -> Module{path:"a", alias}
from_module = the qname of the innermost scope: the file module, an inline-mod PACKAGE (LA.3), or the fn/method whose body holds the `use`.

RESOLVER graph/src/rust_paths.rs `pub(crate) fn resolve_imports_rust(g: &mut RepoGraph, imports: &[ImportStmt], idx: &RustIndex) -> RustBindings` (~140 LOC). Scope lookup: module_by_qname for MODULE, a nav qname index for PACKAGE / FUNCTION / METHOD. Each stmt resolves LAZILY on first demand with a memo and a visiting set (re-export chains are order-independent; a cycle or > 8 hops -> unresolved): Module -> resolve_path to a MODULE/PACKAGE/type or a crate root; Symbol -> resolve `module` to a module M, then `name` in M (module_symbols, else M's own bindings = re-export following), else a child module named `name`; glob -> M. Bound name = alias or last segment. Storage: scope is MODULE/PACKAGE -> g.symbols.module_import_bindings[scope] (so the generic resolver benefits); scope is a fn -> RustBindings.fn_scoped[fn] (owned by the hook, NOT persisted - module_import_bindings is written to the .gmap by store::SymbolTableStore, fn-scoped bindings must not be); globs -> RustBindings.globs[scope]. IMPORTS edges: scope's file MODULE -> the MODULE/PACKAGE the path names (Symbol: its module part; Module: the target when it is a module), deduped per (from, to), emitted in statement order. A Symbol import that resolves to nothing falls back to HEAD's tail rule (unique_global_function by name) so loose-file fixtures (rust-axum-imports' `use crate::util::greet` with no Cargo.toml; matrix/rust/tests' `use crate::calc::add`) behave exactly as today. External crates stay unresolved (no edge), which is correct.
SCOPE ORDER (Rust shadowing, innermost first): the generic resolver checks the FILE module's bindings and symbols first, so a name bound only in a narrower scope must be tried BEFORE it. LA.3's pre-pass (resolve_scoped_bare) is widened to every Bare site that has fn-scoped bindings or a PACKAGE ancestor: fn_scoped[from] -> for each PACKAGE ancestor innermost-first: its symbols, its bindings, its globs -> miss falls through to the generic pass (file MODULE bindings + symbols) -> HOOK after a generic miss: the file module's globs. Attribute first segments consult the same chain before LA.1a's rules 6-8. build_rust: `let bindings = resolve_imports_rust(&mut g, &all_imports, &idx);` replaces resolve_imports_python and the index/hook take `&bindings`.

IMPORTS CELL: with raw paths, code-domain library_name("rust") now yields real crates (serde, tokio). Workspace crates must not count (A16.4 rule: intra-repo names are not dependencies): `LocalModuleIndex::add_local_crate(&mut self, name)` inserts the ident into `paths`; engine/src/build.rs filter_imports_cells takes `&[RustCrate]` (already built for build_rust) and adds each name before filtering. A child-module `pub use arch::..` is already dropped by is_local_path (arch is a declared module segment).
COVERAGE ROW (engine/src/coverage.rs): CoverageCaveat{language:"rust", edge_category:"CALLS", note:"method calls on a local variable or field (`x.m()`) resolve only when the receiver is `self`/`Self` or a module/type path; typed-receiver inference is not implemented", verify:"grep the method name"} - so `glia coverage` states the gap that remains after LA.1-LA.3.
MARKER (build_rust): `[rust-uses] scopes=S bindings=B (reexport_hops=H alias=A fn_scoped=F glob=G) unresolved=U imports_edges=E`.
TESTS: engine/tests/rust_crate_paths.rs also gains `fn_scoped_use_shadows_file_item` (a file-level `fn gm()` and a fn whose body does `use lib::generate_many as gm; gm()` -> CALLS to generate_many, none to the file-level gm). Parser `use_imports` updated (the `use std::io::Read` line is now emitted: 4 -> 5 imports) plus `use_tree_forms` (group + self + alias + glob + nested group + fn-body scope); engine/tests/rust_crate_paths.rs gains `use_reexport_alias_glob_and_fn_scope` over the fixture shape (the four CALLS edges, IMPORTS app::src::main -> lib::src::lib, the forbid) and `imports_cell_lists_external_crates_only` (app::src::main's IMPORTS cell == ["serde"] exactly - no "reexp_lib").

packets.rationale: `glia arch /home/ivy/Code/quokka-stack` at HEAD lists `quokka_android/android/app` as a service with 1 file, 1 node and no language: the file is the Flutter-generated android/app/src/main/kotlin/.../MainActivity.kt, and android/ + android/app are Gradle roots that code-domain/src/project_roots.rs detects under the Dart app root quokka_android (pubspec.yaml). packets.title: Correct the substrate-gap harness claim: a single-dir build DOES pair HTTP / gRPC / RPC / queue / GraphQL / WS / EventBus; only the SHARES_* resolvers need two RepoIds
packets.area: LA.10 - substrate-gap authoring docs + a harness test that pins the fact
packets.rationale: AUTHORING.md's decision table says `A single-repo run only ever has one RepoId, so a cross-repo resolver has nothing to pair against and its edge can never appear`; matrix_vocab.py's docstring, scaffold.py's docstring, matrix/README.md and a grade.py comment repeat it. Measured on HEAD's installed wheel (script: every fixture and matrix probe with >= 2 dirs built once with rg.generate_many(dirs) and once with rg.generate(fixture_dir), cross-category edge counts compared; re-run twice, identical): 99 fixtures SAME, 18 DIFF. The stack resolvers pair inside ONE repo - HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, RPC_CALLS, QUEUE_FLOWS, GRAPHQL_CALLS, WS_CONNECTS, EVENT_FLOWS, CLI_INVOKES, HANDLED_BY all appear single-dir (e.g. xstack-go-http, xcut-grpc-grpc_calls, xcut-trpc, xcut-websocket-ws_connects, xcut-eventbus-spring). Every DIFF is one of two explained kinds: (a) the pairwise SHARES_* resolvers skip same-repo pairs (graph/src/resolvers/mod.rs emit_cross_repo_pairs `if refs[i].1 == refs[j].1 { continue; }` and the equivalent in config/cron/iac/package/shared_schema) - SHARES_SCHEMA, SHARES_DATA_ENTITY, SHARES_DATA_SOURCE, SHARES_CONFIG, SHARES_INFRA_REF only appear with two dirs; (b) one RepoId changes COUNTS, not presence: same-qname markers from two dirs merge into one node (matrix/python/amqp and matrix/csharp/amqp: QUEUE_FLOWS 2 -> 1, the `queue_declare` in both files mints one shared queue node) and HTTP host narrowing keys owners by repo (fixtures/xstack-host-pairing: HTTP_CALLS 2 with two dirs, 4 in one - less precise). fixtures/arch-monorepo-flows and arch-monorepo-http already assert WS/GraphQL/gRPC/EVENT/HTTP edges from a single dir. The harness assumption built on the claim: a single-dir fixture was treated as unable to show a cross-service edge, i.e. as a free negative control.

bench/substrate-gap/matrix_vocab.py:14-23 - module docstring `cross_repo` paragraph ('a single-repo run only ever has one RepoId ... can never appear'); new module-level REPO_PAIRWISE_CATEGORIES

packets.implementation:
DOCS. Replace the claim everywhere with the measured rule: 'Every cross-graph resolver runs in both generate() and generate_many(). The stack resolvers (HTTP, gRPC, RPC, queue, GraphQL, WebSocket, EventBus, CLI) pair across the per-language graphs of ONE repo, so a single-dir fixture shows their edges. Only the pairwise SHARES_* resolvers require two distinct RepoIds. Two dirs stay the default for cross-service columns because (1) it is the realistic client/server shape, (2) one RepoId merges same-qname markers from both sides into one node, changing edge counts, and (3) HTTP host narrowing is keyed per repo, so a single-dir build can over-pair (xstack-host-pairing: 4 HTTP_CALLS vs 2). Consequence: a single-dir fixture is NOT a negative control for a cross-service edge - use a forbid.' AUTHORING.md gets that as the row text plus a 5-line measured table (category -> single-dir pairs? -> example fixture). The other files get a one-sentence version pointing at AUTHORING.md.
matrix_vocab.py: `REPO_PAIRWISE_CATEGORIES = frozenset({"SHARES_SCHEMA", "SHARES_DATA_ENTITY", "SHARES_DATA_SOURCE", "SHARES_CONFIG", "SHARES_INFRA_REF", "SHARES_DEPENDENCY", "SHARES_CRON_SCHEDULE"})` - module level, NOT a MECHANISMS field, so the vocabulary digest does not move. `cross_repo` keeps its meaning for scaffold.py (two dirs by default) with the docstring saying what it now means: 'the column is about a cross-service flow', not 'a single dir cannot show it'.
HARNESS TEST test_matrix.py `test_single_dir_pairing_matches_the_vocabulary` (~40 LOC): for a fixed list of two-dir fixtures - xcut-proto-shared (SHARES_SCHEMA), xdata-source-shares (SHARES_DATA_SOURCE), xiac-terraform-k8s (SHARES_INFRA_REF), xstack-go-http (HTTP_CALLS), xcut-grpc-grpc_calls (GRPC_CALLS), xcut-trpc (RPC_CALLS), xcut-queue-queue_flows (QUEUE_FLOWS), xcut-websocket-ws_connects (WS_CONNECTS), xcut-graphql-graphql_calls (GRAPHQL_CALLS), xcut-eventbus-spring (EVENT_FLOWS) - build with rg.generate_many(dirs) and rg.generate(fixture_dir, False) under GLIA_NO_PERSIST, and for each CROSS-GRAPH category present in the two-dir build (the probe's set: HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, RPC_CALLS, QUEUE_FLOWS, GRAPHQL_CALLS, WS_CONNECTS, EVENT_FLOWS, CLI_INVOKES and the seven SHARES_*; intra-graph categories such as IMPORTS are excluded because single-dir qnames carry the dir prefix) assert: present single-dir  <=>  category not in REPO_PAIRWISE_CATEGORIES. 20 small builds; it fails the day a stack resolver starts requiring distinct RepoIds, or a SHARES_* resolver starts pairing inside one repo.

(2) `grep -rn "can never appear\|one RepoId\|two distinct\|distinct RepoIds" bench/substrate-gap/*.md bench/substrate-gap/*.py bench/substrate-gap/matrix/README.md` finds no remaining statement of the old claim. packets.title: Go package = directory: an import binds the package by its directory, and calls resolve across all of the package's files
packets.rationale: GAP FOUND WHILE SPECCING LA.13 (no item covers it; nearest item is LA.13, so it is a letter packet of it). The engine passes path_to_qname(path) as the Go `package_qname`, so Go module qnames are PER FILE (internal/store/store.go -> `internal::store::store`), while a Go package is a directory. graph/src/imports.rs resolve_imports_go therefore misses on the exact qname (`internal::store`) for every internal import and binds only through the tail fallback (unique_global_module of the last segment) to ONE file. Measured with the HEAD debug CLI on a one-go.mod fixture (below): `store.Save()` resolves because Save sits in store.go, but `store.Load()` (defined in the package's other file, load.go) does not, and the same-package BARE call `helper()` from store.go into load.go does not either - CALLS 1/3. Every real Go package has several files, so cross-file calls inside a package and into imported packages are dropped repo-wide (the go/calls matrix cell reads full only because its fixture is one file per package). LA.13's multi-module fix cannot show an edge without this: with two go.mods, the tail `store` is ambiguous and binds nothing.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN. (a) Change Go module qnames to the package directory so the files of a package share one MODULE node - REJECTED: a qname/node-id change on every Go node (LB-class identity break) and the per-file POSITION/CODE cells would stack onto one node. (b) Union every package's symbols into each file's module_symbols - REJECTED: module_symbols is persisted (store::SymbolTableStore), so a 50-file package would store its symbol table 50 times. (c) A package-directory index used only at resolution time - CHOSEN: no persisted or identity change, and it rides the existing extra_hook seam, so every edge that resolves today is untouched.

graph/src/build.rs (~90 LOC): `struct GoPackages { by_dir: HashMap<String, Vec<NodeId>>, dir_of: HashMap<NodeId, String> }` built from g.symbols.module_by_qname (dir = qname minus its last segment; each member list sorted by qname). build_go: `let pk = GoPackages::build(&g); resolve_calls(&mut g, &all_calls, |g, site| pk.resolve(g, site));` where resolve handles (1) Bare(name): the caller's enclosing module M (graph::calls::enclosing_module) -> every OTHER module in M's dir -> module_symbols[..][name]; exactly one hit binds (Go forbids duplicate top-level names in a package, `init` excepted - skip `init`); (2) Attribute{base, name} whose base is bound (module_import_bindings of M) to a MODULE B: search every module in B's dir for `name`, exactly one hit binds. Anything else -> None. Counters in Cell<usize>.
graph/src/imports.rs resolve_imports_go (~25 LOC): after `g.symbols.module_by_qname.get(path)` misses, collect the modules whose qname minus its last segment == path (the package dir), sorted by qname; if non-empty bind to the member whose last segment equals the package's last segment (Go convention `store/store.go`), else the first; only then the tail fallback. One IMPORTS edge as today (to that representative) - the call-level hook reaches the rest of the package.
MARKER (build_go, once per Go graph): `[go-package] dirs=D multi_file=M dir_bound_imports=I sibling_calls=S`.
TEST graph/tests/go_package_dir.rs (graph already depends on repo-graph-parser-go; the go_smoke_graph.rs pattern): parse the fixture's three files with repo_graph_parser_go::parse_file(src, rel, &path_to_qname-equivalent, "example.com/app", repo) and build_go; assert CALLS main -> internal::store::load::Load, internal::store::store::Save -> internal::store::load::helper, the control main -> Save, and that a package whose two files both define `init` produces no CALLS to either `init`.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN - extraction records, the engine resolves. Alternatives weighed: (a) hand the repo ConstTable to the per-file queue extractor - REJECTED: that output is cached by the file's own content hash, so editing topics.ts would leave publish.ts serving a stale topic (constants.rs cache rule). (b) record the unresolved expression on the sentinel node's CODE cell and fold it later - REJECTED: the sentinel is only emitted when NO site of a needle named a topic, so in a file with `send('audit')` and `send(ORDERS_TOPIC)` the constant site has no carrier and stays lost. (c) CHOSEN: post-cache, re-run the text-only queue scan (cheap - no tree-sitter) for files that already hold a queue node, with a resolver closure, and swap that file's queue nodes only when at least one site folded. Every node, cell (POSITION, CODE {framework,family,sites}, A12.1 MESSAGE_TYPE) and CONTAINS edge comes from the same emit path as the first scan, so a folded node is shaped exactly like a literal one; a file where nothing folds is untouched (endpoint_fold's zero-change guarantee).
1. queue_topic.rs (~60 LOC). `TopicHit { topic, form, offset, expr: Option<String> }`. `scan` sets `expr` only when `topic` is None and the rule is ArgLiteral / ArgIndex(n) / Keyed / KeyedOrArg (never NoIdentity or the four A2.5 identity rules). New private `arg_expr(region, n)` reads the same slot `arg_literal` reads (split_args arg n); `keyed_expr(region, keys)` the value after `<key><sep>` exactly where `keyed_literal` looks, or the key itself for an ES6 shorthand whose key is followed by `,` or `}` (`{ topic, messages }`). Accept only an identifier chain after trim: first byte [A-Za-z_$@], then only [A-Za-z0-9_$.:>?!-], optional trailing `()`, at most 128 bytes; anything with a quote, whitespace, `+`, `[`, `{` or an inner `(` is None. Slice only through `clip` / `get`.
2. constants.rs (~25 LOC). `pub fn resolve_identity(&self, expr: &str) -> Option<&str>`: normalise_expr; if the key is constant-shaped (dotted or SCREAMING_CASE) return the strict exact binding (never an ambiguous key - `alternatives` check, as resolve_expr_strict); else if the key is dotted and its LAST segment is SCREAMING_CASE, that segment strictly (Java `Topics.ORDERS` where the table bound bare `ORDERS` inside `class Topics`). The programme text said `resolve_expr`; the lenient form takes first-binding-wins even for an ambiguous key, and resolve_expr_strict's own doc gives the reason not to: 'A wrong topic manufactures a false cross-service edge; no topic does not.'
3. queues.rs (~120 LOC). `emit_queue_nodes(.., resolve: Option<&dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>>, counts: &mut ConstFoldCounts)`. A hit with topic None, expr Some(e), a rule that is not identity/NoIdentity, on a row that is NOT `is_generic_verb_row` (generic verbs keep their `literal_leads` guard) becomes a site when `resolve(e)` returns a value AND `queue_topic::fold_topic(value)` accepts it (a constant holding an SQS URL / SNS ARN folds exactly as the literal would); Confidence::Medium; `counts.folded += 1`, else `counts.unresolved += 1`. The sentinel fallback rule is unchanged (only when no site of the needle named a topic). The two existing pub fns pass None - byte-identical output, every existing test (incl. `servicebus_trigger_attr`'s constant case) unchanged. New pub API: `pub struct ConstFoldCounts { pub folded: usize, pub unresolved: usize }`; `pub struct ConstFold { pub consumers: QueueNodes, pub producers: QueueNodes, pub counts: ConstFoldCounts }`; `pub fn extract_queue_nodes_with_consts(source, path, module_id, repo, resolve: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> ConstFold`; `pub fn replace_queue_nodes(fp: &mut FileParse, module_id: NodeId, lang: &str, fold: ConstFold)`: removes every node whose nav kind is QUEUE_PRODUCER / QUEUE_CONSUMER (only queues.rs mints those kinds - grep-verified), the CONTAINS edges from module_id to them, their name/qname/kind/parent_of entries and their ids from children_of[module_id] (retain), then appends consumers then producers (nodes, edges, nav via the same extend + map merge), the order apply_cross_cutting_extractors uses. IMPORTS CELL (verifier addition): the router attached the raw G15 IMPORTS cell (code-domain attach_imports_cell, engine/src/route.rs parse_repo_files) to EVERY node of a language-parser parse before the cache stored it, so the removed queue nodes carried one and the re-emitted ones would not. `replace_queue_nodes` therefore takes `lang: &str` and, after appending, gives exactly the new nodes that cell the way engine/src/build.rs graft_rpc_markers does: split the new nodes off into a temporary `FileParse { nodes, imports: fp.imports.clone(), ..Default::default() }`, call `repo_graph_code_domain::attach_imports_cell(&mut tmp, lang)`, extend them back. apply_queue_const_topics runs before filter_imports_cells in build_graphs_for_repo, so the A16.4 rewrite then treats them like every other node. Unit test `replace_queue_nodes_keeps_the_imports_cell` (a folded node carries exactly one IMPORTS cell, last, like a literal one).
4. engine/src/build.rs (~60 LOC). `fn apply_queue_const_topics(parses_by_lang: &mut HashMap<&'static str, Vec<FileParse>>, files: &[(String, String)], repo: RepoId, consts: &ConstTable, parse_errors: &mut Vec<String>) -> QueueConstStats { files, folded, unresolved }`, called right after the endpoint fold (cached parses are folded too; the cache keeps the pre-fold parse, the endpoint_fold precedent). Iterate `files` (walk-sorted, so process-independent); detect_language; find the FileParse by MODULE id exactly as apply_rpc_needles; skip unless `fp.nav.kind_by_id` holds a QUEUE_* kind; `let local = ConstTable::scan_file(source, lang);` resolver `|e| local.resolve_expr_strict(e).or_else(|| consts.resolve_identity(e)).map(str::to_string)` - a SAME-FILE binding resolves at any shape (Go `const SubjectOrders`, a TS class field read as `this.topic`), a cross-file one only when constant-shaped, both only when unambiguous. Run under catch_unwind (`{path}: PANIC (queue const fold)` into parse_errors); call replace_queue_nodes only when counts.folded > 0. Print the marker once per repo when folded + unresolved > 0.
5. engine/src/coverage.rs: first QUEUE_FLOWS caveat note becomes 'topics passed as parameters, runtime variables or env vars - and constants that are ambiguous, or lower-case bindings in another file - are extracted as an unresolved framework tag and never paired; literal constants the repo table resolves are folded' (verify text unchanged).
6. Tests. queue_topic.rs `expr_is_captured_only_for_identifier_slots` (ORDERS_TOPIC, Topics.PAYMENTS, `{ topic, messages }`, this.topic -> Some; `'t' + x`, `getTopic(a)`, a template literal -> None). queues.rs `const_resolver_folds_keyed_positional_and_annotation_sites` (kafkajs keyed, Spring send(TOPIC, ..), @KafkaListener(topics = Topics.ORDERS), Go nc.Publish(SubjectOrders, ..)), `mixed_literal_and_constant_sites_in_one_file` (send('audit') + send(ORDERS_TOPIC) -> both topics, no sentinel), `generic_verb_rows_never_resolve`, `unresolvable_expr_keeps_the_sentinel`, `replace_queue_nodes_swaps_nodes_edges_and_nav`, `replace_queue_nodes_keeps_the_imports_cell`. constants.rs `resolve_identity_gates_shape_and_ambiguity`. engine/tests/queue_const_topics.rs (new) - see acceptance.

packets.implementation:
OUTPUT SHAPE. An annotation op is the A10.1 contract op: DOC_SECTION (42, no new id) + CODE / POSITION / ORIGIN{provenance:contract}, built by contracts::push_op (now pub(crate)). ORIGIN carries `method` + `path` (+ `raw_path`), so link_contract_routes pairs it UNCHANGED and `glia docs-for <route>` / governing_docs answer with it (merged.all_edges includes the DOCUMENTS cross-edge). `ContractNodes.source` stays None, so route.rs ContractCounts never double-counts it.
WHERE METHOD + PATH COME FROM - weighed: (a) recompose class + method paths from annotation text for every framework - REJECTED for Java/C#: the parsers already compose them (A4.x) and emit ROUTE -HANDLED_BY-> METHOD as a per-file Edge; a second composer would drift. (b) CHOSEN: Java/C# read the ROUTE the annotated method handles out of the FileParse (this runs after the language parser, so fp has both); NestJS composes, because ts_routes emits `route:/users/:id` without HANDLED_BY - reusing ts_routes' own decorator helpers so the two cannot disagree.
openapi_annot.rs (~230 LOC + ~110 test LOC). `pub fn extract_annotated_ops(source: &str, path: &str, lang: &str, fp: &FileParse, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId) -> ContractNodes`. Returns empty unless lang is java / csharp / typescript-family AND the framework gate is in the file.
Blocks: maximal runs of lines whose trimmed text starts with `@` (Java, TS) or `[` (C#), continued while paren/bracket depth > 0 (multi-line `@ApiOperation({` ... `})`); strings and `//` comments respected; every slice via get().
Frameworks (gate -> needles -> fields): springdoc (`io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations`): `@Operation(` summary= / operationId= (a block with `hidden = true` is skipped), `@ApiResponse(` responseCode = "NNN", `@ApiResponses(`. springfox (`io.swagger.annotations`): `@ApiOperation(` value= / nickname=, `@ApiResponse(` code = NNN. swashbuckle (`Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.Annotations`): `[SwaggerOperation(` Summary= / OperationId=, `[SwaggerResponse(` NNN. aspnet-apiexplorer (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc`, used when the block has `[ProducesResponseType(` but no Swagger* attribute): status = first integer 100-599 in the args or the NNN of `StatusCodes.StatusNNN...`; type from `typeof(T)` / `Type = typeof(T)`. nestjs (`@nestjs/swagger`): `@ApiOperation({ summary, operationId })`, `@ApiResponse({ status: NNN, type: T })`, and `@ApiOkResponse` / `@ApiCreatedResponse` / `@ApiNoContentResponse` / `@ApiBadRequestResponse` / `@ApiUnauthorizedResponse` / `@ApiForbiddenResponse` / `@ApiNotFoundResponse` mapped to 200/201/204/400/401/403/404.
Owner + key. Java/C#: owner = anchor::owner_of_line(&anchor::build_owner_index(&fp.nodes, &fp.nav), first block line) (METHOD spans include annotations - measured). Key = every ROUTE r with an Edge{from: r, to: owner, category: HANDLED_BY} in fp.edges, qname split `<METHOD> <path>` (the shape Java/C# emit; a `route:<path>` ROUTE is read with its ROUTE_METHOD cells); a non-verb method (ANY) is not keyed. NestJS: owner not needed; key = the block's own `@Get|@Post|@Put|@Patch|@Delete|@Head|@Options(` decorator suffix (ts_routes::extract_decorator_string) joined to the nearest preceding `@Controller(` prefix by ts_routes::combine_nest_paths; `@All(` is not keyed. A block with no key emits nothing and counts `unkeyed` - never a guessed path.
Emission per (method, path): qname `contract::<file stem>::<METHOD>:<path>`, name `<METHOD> <path>`, POSITION = the block's first line (0-indexed), ORIGIN JSON in this key order: {"provenance":"contract","source":"<springdoc|springfox|swashbuckle|aspnet-apiexplorer|nestjs>","method":M,"path":P,"raw_path":P[,"operation_id":..][,"summary":..][,"responses":["200","404"]][,"response_types":{"200":"UserDto"}]} - optional keys omitted when empty, never null; responses in declaration order, deduped; all strings via esc(). Two blocks keyed to one (method, path) in one file merge (first block's POSITION, responses unioned). Confidence is push_op's Strong, as for spec-file ops (the DOCUMENTS edge confidence is set by link_contract_routes from the matcher tier and the ROUTE, unchanged).
Marker, one line per file per framework that emitted or skipped a block (the [java-routes] per-file precedent).
extract.rs: `let ops = openapi_annot::extract_annotated_ops(source, path, lang, fp, module_id, repo); fp.nodes.extend(ops.nodes); merge_nav(&mut fp.nav, ops.nav);` placed before anchor::attach (DOC_SECTION is not a marker kind, attach ignores it). The result is a function of the file alone, so it is safe to cache with the FileParse.
Unit tests (openapi_annot.rs): springdoc_block_keys_on_handled_by_route, springdoc_hidden_operation_is_skipped, springfox_code_attr_is_a_response, swashbuckle_typeof_and_statuscodes_forms, producesresponsetype_alone_is_aspnet_apiexplorer, nestjs_composes_controller_and_verb_decorator, unannotated_handler_emits_nothing, block_without_route_counts_unkeyed, gate_absent_emits_nothing (an `@Operation` from an unrelated package).

packets.implementation:
Both readers are text scanners inside openapi_annot.rs; no fp lookups (method + path are declared), no engine change (LA.15a already wired the call for every language). swaggo (~70 LOC): lang == go and the file contains `// @Router`. A block = a run of consecutive lines whose trimmed text starts with `//`. Inside a block: each `@Router []` line (several allowed; verb case-insensitive, must be an OpenAPI verb) is one op; `@ID ` -> operation_id; `@Summary ` -> summary; `@Success|@Failure {} ` -> responses + response_types. A file-level `// @BasePath

` anywhere in the SAME file is joined onto every path (path = join(base, router), raw_path = the router path - the servers-base fold contracts.rs applies to spec files, so link_contract_routes' raw_path retry still pairs when routes are registered un-prefixed); a @BasePath in another file (usually main.go) is not followed and the matcher's prefix tiers carry it. POSITION = the @Router line. source "swaggo". rswag (~80 LOC): lang == ruby, the file contains `path '` or `path "`, and one of `swagger_helper`, `openapi_helper`, `rswag` (gate). Indentation-scoped scan: `path '

' do` opens a path scope; inside it `get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options '

' do` opens an op scope (summary from the literal); inside that `operationId ''` and `response ''` / `response ""` lines fill the ORIGIN. A scope closes at the first later non-blank line whose indent is <= its opener's indent. POSITION = the verb line. source "rswag". The spec file lives under spec/, and passes.rs tag_synthetic_provenance skips any node that already has an ORIGIN cell, so the contract ORIGIN is never replaced by test_fixture. Marker lines reuse LA.15a's per-file format with framework=swaggo / framework=rswag. packets.implementation:
WHERE THE SNIFF LIVES - the item says 'in the contract admission gate'. The gate is walk_dir's call; the sniff itself goes in schemas.rs (the MESSAGE_TYPE owner) rather than as a ContractSource variant, because a JSON Schema declares a type, not operations, and contracts.rs is LA.15a's file. walk.rs ORs the two sniffs; route.rs dispatches.
1. schemas.rs `sniff_json_schema(text) -> bool` (~30 LOC, no parse): BOM-trimmed body starts with `{`; within the first 8 KiB, either a `"$schema"` KEY whose string value contains `json-schema.org`, or a `"type"` KEY whose value is `"object"` AND a `"properties"` KEY (key position = quoted key followed by optional whitespace and `:`, the contracts::key_pos rule re-implemented locally in ~10 LOC; char-boundary-safe cut). It is only a gate: nested look-alikes are admitted and rejected by step 2 at the cost of one parse, never a wrong node.
2. `extract_json_schema_types(source, path, module_id, repo) -> SchemaNodes` (~110 LOC): serde_json validity check first (the extract_avro_records precedent), then JsonReader for 0-indexed object spans. The ROOT is a type when it is an object with `"type":"object"` or an object-valued `"properties"`; each member of `$defs` / `definitions` that is itself such an object is a type (one level; at most 256 types per file). Root name: `title` when it matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}; else the last path segment of `$id` with `.schema.json` / `.json` stripped; else the file stem with a trailing `.schema` stripped. qnames `message:jsonschema:<root>` and `message:jsonschema:<root>.<def>`. Node shape identical to extract_avro_records: Confidence::Strong, POSITION = the object's own braces, ORIGIN {"provenance":"contract","source":"jsonschema","decl":"object"|"def"[,"id":"<$id>"]}; the root DEFINES each def (Edge, Strong) and is its nav parent; a def whose root is not a type is parented to the module; module_cells = whole-file POSITION; message_count counts roots, def_count defs. First declaration wins on a repeated qname (the avro rule).
3. walk.rs walk_dir: `&& (sniff_json_contract(&text).is_some() || schemas::sniff_json_schema(&text))` - same JSON_CONTRACT_CAP, same json.sniffed / json.admitted counters.
4. route.rs parse_repo_files json branch: `if contracts::sniff_json_contract(source).is_none() && schemas::sniff_json_schema(source)` -> extract_json_schema_types, counters jsonschema_files / types / defs, `stash_synthetic_parse("json", path, module_id, repo, vec![recs.nodes], vec![recs.edges], vec![recs.nav], recs.module_cells, ..)` when non-empty (the existing "json" group: no new per-language shard); otherwise the existing contract path unchanged. After the loop, beside `[avro]`: print the marker when jsonschema_files > 0.
No resolver change: MessageSchemaResolver already pairs same-qname MESSAGE_TYPE nodes across repos with SHARES_SCHEMA and prints `[schema-link]`.
Tests: schemas.rs sniff_json_schema_accepts_draft_and_object_shapes (draft-07 and 2020-12 $schema; type object + properties) and rejects openapi.json / tsconfig.json / package-lock.json / a JSON array / a substrate key.json; json_schema_root_and_defs_are_message_types (qnames, DEFINES, POSITION lines, ORIGIN); title_id_stem_naming_precedence; nested_lookalike_yields_nothing; malformed_json_yields_nothing_and_does_not_panic. walk.rs new walk_admits_json_schema_and_rejects_lookalike_data (the existing walk_admits_only_sniffed_contract_json stays unchanged and green). engine/tests/json_schema_types.rs - see acceptance.

packets.implementation:
MODEL - weighed: (a) widen the gRPC family (GRPC_CLIENT / GRPC_SERVER, service-level GRPC_CALLS) - REJECTED: service-level only, and Twirp is not gRPC (the fixture forbids a GRPC_SERVER leak). (b) CHOSEN, as the item and rpc.rs specify: method-level RPC_PROCEDURE (48) / RPC_CALL (49) paired by the UNCHANGED RpcStackResolver on an exact path (RPC_CALLS 34 is already a blast carry edge). No new id. Overlap kept, declared: a connect-go client still also matches the legacy `ServiceClient(` suffix and keeps its service-level grpc_client:<Svc> -> GRPC_CALLS; removing it would be an edge removal with no gain.
QNAME: `rpc:<proto package>.<Service>.<Method>` / `rpc_call:<proto package>.<Service>.<Method>` (package from ProtoServiceRef.package, omitted when the .proto declares none; Method = the proto rpc name). Package-qualified because Connect's own procedure path is /<package>.<Service>/<Method> and the gRPC pass already needed package evidence (fixture xcut-grpc-package-collision). A service name matching two known services in different packages is skipped and counted ambiguous, never guessed.
WHY POST-CACHE: the procedure list comes from the build's .proto set (RpcContext, A5.2), not the file itself, so this runs in apply_rpc_needles exactly like the data-driven gRPC client and server-impl passes; incremental == clean.
1. grpc.rs (~200 LOC + ~90 test LOC). `pub struct ProtoRpcCounts { pub connect_procedures, pub connect_calls, pub twirp_procedures, pub twirp_calls, pub ambiguous, pub unowned: usize }`; `pub struct ProtoRpcNodes { pub nodes: Vec<Node>, pub edges: Vec<Edge>, pub nav: CodeNav, pub counts: ProtoRpcCounts }`; `pub fn may_hold_proto_rpc(source: &str, twirp_repo: bool) -> bool` (connect import strings, or twirp_repo and `ProtobufClient(` / `JSONClient(` / `Server(`); `pub fn extract_proto_rpc_nodes(source: &str, path: &str, lang: &str, module_id: NodeId, repo: RepoId, known: &[ProtoServiceRef], nodes: &[Node], nav: &CodeNav, twirp_repo: bool) -> ProtoRpcNodes`. Skip a file carrying a GENERATED_BANNERS line and any needle after a declaration keyword (`func NewElizaServiceClient(` in *.connect.go). Gates: Go connect - `connectrpc.com/connect` or `github.com/bufbuild/connect-go` in the file; Go twirp - `twirp_repo` (Twirp client files import only the generated package - measured - so the gate is repo-level); TS connect-es - `@connectrpc/connect` or `@bufbuild/connect`. SERVERS: Go `.New<Svc>Handler(` (connect) and `.New<Svc>Server(` (twirp; package-qualified call only, so a hand-written `NewGreeterServer()` constructor in a gRPC repo never hits), Svc a known service. Impl type T = arg #0 (`&T{`, `T{`). For each rpc R of Svc one RPC_PROCEDURE (Confidence::Medium): when this file has a METHOD named R whose nav parent is a STRUCT named T, a HANDLED_BY Edge procedure -> method and a POSITION copied from the method's span; otherwise a one-line POSITION at the registration line and a module CONTAINS edge, NO owner edge (an rpc served by the Unimplemented embed must never read as HANDLED_BY main), counts.unowned += 1. CLIENTS: Go `.New<Svc>Client(` (connect), `.New<Svc>ProtobufClient(` / `.New<Svc>JSONClient(` (twirp); TS `createClient(<Svc>`, `createPromiseClient(<Svc>`, `createCallbackClient(<Svc>`. Binding = the identifier assigned on the needle's line (`client :=`, `client =`, `const client =`, `s.client =` -> `client`); every `<binding>.<m>(` in the file (identifier boundary before the binding; TS lowerCamel m -> UpperCamel) whose name is an rpc of Svc is a call site, and a chained `New<Svc>Client(..).<M>(` counts too; `client.Close()` and other non-rpc methods mint nothing. One RPC_CALL per (Svc, rpc) per file, Confidence::Medium, POSITION at the first site, and per site a USES Edge from the innermost METHOD / FUNCTION holding it - anchor::build_owner_index + anchor::owner_of_line used as a library, NOT anchor::attach, so anchor.rs's marker kinds and the `[marker-anchor]` census (and tRPC) are untouched - or a module CONTAINS edge when no function holds it. nav.record(id, name = "<Svc>.<Method>", qname, kind, Some(module_id)).
2. engine/src/build.rs (~45 LOC). In build_graphs_for_repo compute `twirp_repo = files.iter().any(|(p, s)| (p.ends_with("go.mod") && s.contains("github.com/twitchtv/twirp")) || p.ends_with(".twirp.go"))`; pass it to apply_rpc_needles; the per-file gate becomes `grpc::may_hold_grpc_server(source) || grpc::may_hold_proto_rpc(source, twirp_repo)` (the existing gRPC calls keep their own inner gates); for lang go and the TS family call extract_proto_rpc_nodes under catch_unwind (`{path}: PANIC (proto rpc needles)`), graft nodes / edges / nav into the matched FileParse (cells and edges arrive finished - no anchors) through a new `graft_proto_rpc(fp, out, lang) -> usize` beside graft_rpc_markers that, like it, gives the new nodes the router's raw G15 IMPORTS cell (split_off + attach_imports_cell on a temporary FileParse with fp.imports) so they match every other node of a language-parser parse before filter_imports_cells rewrites them, accumulate counts; print the marker once per repo when any count > 0.
3. engine/src/arch.rs: FLOW_MECHANISMS gains edge_category::RPC_CALLS so `glia arch` shows Connect / Twirp / tRPC links by default (cli/src/main.rs drop_non_flow_links reads the table; no CLI code change).

packets.rationale: The programme left ws as the only net-negative mechanism (wave-plan section 7: A5.6/A5.8 were precision-only). What websocket.rs has at HEAD (read in full, 194 lines): 12 HANDLER_PATTERNS and 8 CLIENT_PATTERNS, each matched with `source.find` - FIRST occurrence only; the name is a quoted literal immediately after the needle, else the fallback `ws` / `default`. No Python, Java, C#/SignalR or nhooyr needle; `gorilla/websocket` (an import line) and `websocket.Upgrader` (a package var) are HANDLER needles, so the handler is never anchored inside the upgrading function; `io(` has no word boundary. PROBES ON HEAD 7a4883b: FastAPI `@app.websocket("/ws/chat")` + `("/ws/admin")` -> no WS_HANDLER (matrix/python/ws graded: WS_HANDLER 0/2, WS_CONNECTS 0/1, cell none); JSR-356 `@ServerEndpoint`, Spring `registry.addHandler(h, "/echo")` -> nothing; SignalR `app.MapHub<ChatHub>("/hubs/chat")` + TS `HubConnectionBuilder().withUrl("/hubs/chat")` -> nothing; nhooyr `websocket.Accept(` -> nothing; TS `new WebSocket("ws://" + location.host + "/ws/chat")` -> `ws_client:ws://` (garbage) and a second `new WebSocket(` in the same file is never read; Dart `Dio()` in fixtures/http-absolute-url-client/client-dart mints `ws_client:ws` through the `io(` needle. Graph: `find extract_ws_handler_nodes` -> websocket.rs:39; `impact` backward on it returns no callers (the run_marked! macro call in engine/src/extract.rs:203 is invisible - LA.2). VERIFIER RE-MEASURE 2026-09-18 on HEAD fe23c8d (code identical to 7a4883b; only dev-notes/next-leap-0.5.0.md changed): every fixture key below was re-graded with grade.py (installed wheel = HEAD) from scratch copies; the rows match the baseline stated here. packets.implementation:
SCANNER (~150 LOC). Each row: `struct WsRow { needle: &'static str, gate: &'static [&'static str] /* any-of substrings of the file, empty = none */, read: PathRead, anchor: AnchorAt, framework: &'static str }`. Every occurrence of every row whose gate holds is examined (cap 32 per row per file, as queue_topic::MAX_HITS_PER_NEEDLE). A needle starting with an identifier byte must not be preceded by one (word boundary - kills Dart `Dio()` -> `io(`). PathRead: Generic (name `ws`), Default (`default`), Arg(n) (first quoted literal of positional arg n of the call region), KeyedOrArg(keys) (`path: '/x'`, `value = "/x"`, else arg 0), AfterAngle (`MapHub<T>("/x")` - the `(` after the matching `>`), Client(n) (the client path reader on arg n). A readable name is kept verbatim for servers (`/chat/{room}` stays templated for LA.18b); an unreadable one falls back to `ws` exactly as today. AnchorAt: Needle, or NextDef for Python decorators - the first `def ` / `async def ` line within 5 lines after, because Python FUNCTION spans start at the def line, not the decorator (measured: app::chat starts at its def). Every site of a name is anchored (the name is per-site, so every site is meaningful - anchor.rs density rule), so attach gives each owning function its HANDLED_BY / USES edge. The arg-region reader is a local ~40 LOC bracket/quote-aware walker (depth counter, ', ", ` quoting, \ escapes, 2048-byte cap, char-boundary clip via queue_topic::clip). It is NOT shared with queue_topic.rs's private arg_region/split_args, which belong to LA.4's file set - same rule A2.8 followed for escape_json; follow-up: one shared call-argument reader.
CLIENT PATH READER (~50 LOC): split arg n into top-level `+` pieces; a string literal is static, a template literal is static text with each `${...}` span a dynamic piece, anything else is dynamic. Concatenate with a marker for every dynamic piece; take the text after the LAST marker if it starts with `/`, else the whole text when there is no marker; strip `ws://` / `wss://` / `http://` / `https://` + authority (normalise_ws_path widened from ws(s) to http(s) for SignalR `withUrl("https://h/hubs/chat")`); accept only a result starting with `/`. So `"ws://" + location.host + "/ws/chat"` -> `/ws/chat`, `` `${base}/ws/admin` `` -> `/ws/admin`, `"wss://api.example.com/echo"` -> `/echo`, `new WebSocket(url)` -> unreadable -> `ws_client:ws` (unchanged fallback).
ROWS - server: keep `ws.on("connection"` / `ws.on('connection'` (Generic), `@WebSocketGateway` (Default), `ws.handleUpgrade` (Generic); `WebSocketServer` becomes `new WebSocketServer(` / `new WebSocket.Server(` KeyedOrArg(["path"]) (an import line no longer mints a handler); REMOVE `websocket.Upgrader` and `gorilla/websocket` as needles (a package var / import is not a handler - gorilla/websocket becomes a gate); ADD go gorilla `.Upgrade(` gate [gorilla/websocket] Generic, go nhooyr `websocket.Accept(` gate [nhooyr.io/websocket, github.com/coder/websocket] Generic (both anchored at the call inside the handler function, so LA.18b can give them their route paths); python `.websocket(` gate [fastapi, starlette] Arg(0) NextDef, `WebSocketRoute(` gate [starlette] Arg(0), `.add_websocket_route(` gate [fastapi, starlette] Arg(0); java `@ServerEndpoint(` gate [javax.websocket, jakarta.websocket] KeyedOrArg(["value"]), `.addHandler(` gate [WebSocketHandlerRegistry] Arg(1), `.addEndpoint(` gate [StompEndpointRegistry] Arg(0); csharp `MapHub<` gate [SignalR] AfterAngle, `AcceptWebSocketAsync(` Generic. The Phoenix / ActionCable rows (`channel "`, `channel '`, `socket "`, `Phoenix.Channel`, `ActionCable`) are left as they are for LA.18c. ROWS - client: `new WebSocket(`, `useWebSocket(`, `io(`, `io.connect(`, `ws.connect(`, `WebSocketSubject(`, `connectWebSocket(` -> Client(0); `socket.io-client` unchanged (Generic); SignalR `.withUrl(` gate [@microsoft/signalr] Client(0) and `.WithUrl(` gate [Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client] Client(0); Go `DefaultDialer.Dial(` gate [gorilla/websocket] Client(0), `DefaultDialer.DialContext(` Client(1), nhooyr `websocket.Dial(` gate [nhooyr.io/websocket, github.com/coder/websocket] Client(1); python `websockets.connect(` Client(0).
Nodes keep today's shape (qname `ws:<name>` / `ws_client:<name>`, Confidence::Medium, cells filled by anchor::attach); one node per distinct name per file. Signatures become `(source, path, module_id, repo)`; extract.rs passes `path`. Marker per file per framework with >= 1 node.

packets.implementation:
Alternatives weighed: (a) HANDLED_BY the enclosing function (main) - REJECTED: main registers every route and calls everything, so every route would inherit every callee (the fixture forbids route:/health -> main::main); (b) HANDLED_BY the MODULE (the C# lambda rule) - REJECTED: a module carries no CALLS, so the callee stays unreachable; (c) CHOSEN: the literal's own direct callees, which is what actually runs for that route.
WHY THE CALLEE FILTER MATTERS (verifier correction). The draft said external calls 'stay unresolved under the builder's normal rules'. They do not: graph/src/calls.rs resolve_refs falls back, for HANDLED_BY only, to unique_global_function(name) for a Bare ref and unique_global_method(name) for an Attribute ref - any uniquely named function / method anywhere in the repo. So `log.Println(..)` would bind to a repo's own unique `Println` method, `json.NewEncoder(w)` to a unique `NewEncoder`, and a builtin such as `len(x)` to a repo function named `len`. The filter therefore has to be applied in the parser, where the import table is known.
emit_route_from_call, handler_arg match: new arm `Some(h) if h.kind() == "func_literal"`: collect the literal's parameter names (its parameter_list identifiers: w, r, c, ctx, ...); walk its body in source order, NOT descending into nested func_literal nodes; for each call_expression: (1) `function` is an identifier -> CallQualifier::Bare(name), unless the name is a Go builtin or predeclared conversion (append cap clear close complex copy delete imag len make max min new panic print println real recover, and the predeclared types bool byte complex64 complex128 error float32 float64 int int8 int16 int32 int64 rune string uint uint8 uint16 uint32 uint64 uintptr any); (2) `function` is a selector_expression whose operand is an identifier -> CallQualifier::Attribute { base, name } ONLY when the operand is neither one of the literal's parameters (so `c.JSON(..)`, `w.Write(..)` never become refs) NOR the local name of an EXTERNAL import of this file (so `log.Println`, `http.Error`, `json.NewEncoder`, `fmt.Fprintf` never become refs); a repo-local package import (path under module_import_prefix, e.g. `handlers.ListUsers(c)`) and a captured variable (`h.ServeWS(w, r)`, `hub.register(..)`) are kept - the same shapes the identifier / selector arms already resolve. Acc gains `external_pkgs: HashSet<String>`, filled in the import handler (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs, the function that pushes ImportStmt ~:585-627, beside di_containers): the local name (alias, else the last path segment) of every import whose path does NOT start with module_import_prefix (all imports when the prefix is empty); `_` and `.` imports bind nothing. Go requires imports before other declarations, so the set is complete before any route is visited. Dedupe callees; at most 8 per literal; push UnresolvedRef { from: route_id, from_module: module_id, qualifier, category: HANDLED_BY } exactly as the identifier arm does. handler_display stays None (there is no single named handler), so the ROUTE_METHOD cell is unchanged. Acc gains `func_literal_handlers` / `func_literal_refs`; parse_file prints the marker when func_literal_handlers > 0 (the [java-routes] per-file precedent).
Unit tests in the go parser tests mod: func_literal_handler_refs_its_callees (`http.HandleFunc("/ws", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { serveWs(hub, w, r) })` -> exactly one HANDLED_BY ref Bare(serveWs)), gin_closure_skips_param_receiver_calls (`r.GET("/x", func(c *gin.Context) { c.JSON(200, build()) })` -> Bare(build) only), external_package_calls_are_not_refs (`import ("log"; "encoding/json")` + a literal calling `log.Println(..)`, `json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)`, `len(v)` and `writeHealth(w)` -> Bare(writeHealth) only), repo_local_package_call_is_a_ref (module prefix `example.com/app`, `import "example.com/app/handlers"`, literal calls `handlers.ListUsers(c)` -> Attribute{handlers, ListUsers}), nested_func_literal_calls_are_not_refs, identifier_handler_unchanged (the existing emits_handled_by_refs_for_identifier_and_selector_handlers stays green).

packets.implementation:
Parsers extract, the graph resolves: which route reaches an upgrade site is a cross-file join over HANDLED_BY / CALLS edges, so it lives in the resolver, not in websocket.rs (an extractor sees one file; the gochat route and upgrade are in different files).
1. http.rs (~15 LOC): `pub(crate) fn route_path(qname: &str) -> Option<&str>` = first `repo_graph_code_domain::split_owner(qname).0` (LB.4a's ` @<project>` owner suffix, a declared prerequisite - without it a nested-root route reads `/ws @services/chat` and never matches a client path), then `route:<path>` -> path, or `<METHOD> <path>` with path starting `/` -> path; index_route_node calls it. One reader of the ROUTE qname shape for both resolvers.
2. websocket.rs (~150 LOC + tests). (a) Generic test on the RAW key before segmenting: a key is generic iff it is exactly `ws` or `default` with no leading `/` (the extractor's fallback names; real paths always start with `/`). (b) Route inheritance, per RepoGraph g: `ws_owner: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<NodeId>>` from HANDLED_BY edges whose `from` is a WS_HANDLER (LA.18a's anchor edges); `route_paths: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<String>>` from ROUTE -HANDLED_BY-> fn with route_path over g.nav.qname_by_id; `callers: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<NodeId>>` from CALLS edges. Effective paths of a generic handler W = BTreeSet over owners F of paths(F) ∪ paths(G) for every G -CALLS-> F (ONE hop: the route handler that calls an upgrade helper; LA.18d makes func-literal routes HANDLED_BY their callees, which covers the gochat layout with zero hops). Maps are only looked up; output order comes from BTreeSet / graph order. (c) Pairing: a generic handler pairs ONLY against its effective paths (counted `inherited`), never by its fallback name; a generic handler with none, and every generic client, pairs nothing (counted `dropped-generic`) - this removes the coincidental `/ws` client <-> `ws` fallback pair. (d) Parameters: a segment `{x}`, `:x` or `<x>` on the handler side (and `{}` on the client side, from a template the extractor could not fold) matches exactly one non-empty segment; a path containing any parameter pairs only at equal length (no suffix tier), so /chat/lobby/feed never pairs /chat/{room}; counted `param`. The Exact / Suffix tiers are unchanged for literal paths. Marker line gains the new counters.
3. coverage.rs: row {language:"*", edge_category:"WS_CONNECTS", note:"a WebSocket upgrade whose route is registered more than one call away from the upgrading function, or through a router glia does not extract, stays unpaired; a client whose URL has no static path is not paired", verify:"grep the upgrade call and the route registration"}.
Unit tests (resolvers/websocket.rs): generic_handler_pairs_only_through_route_paths, generic_client_never_pairs, generic_handler_without_routes_is_dropped, inherits_one_call_hop_not_two, param_segment_matches_one_segment_only, templated_path_has_no_suffix_tier, raw_slash_ws_is_not_generic (client `/ws` vs fallback `ws`); exact_match_survives_slash_and_case, suffix_is_segment_aware_not_byte_wise and empty_path_never_pairs keep passing unchanged (ws_pair stays segment-level; the generic rule is applied to raw keys in resolve() before ws_pair is called); generic_names_no_longer_wildcard keeps its ws_pair assertion and its three is_generic_ws_path assertions move to is_generic_ws_key with the raw-key semantics: `ws` true, `default` true, `/api/ws` false, and `/default` now FALSE (a leading slash means a real path was read). http.rs: route_path_reads_both_qname_shapes.
