packets.implementation:
CLI: `glia merge [REPOS]... [--gmap DIR]... [--workspace FILE] [--layout OUT_DIR] [--out JSON|-] [--incremental]`. Positional REPOS alone keeps today's behaviour byte-for-byte. `--gmap` members are named by the dir's basename (a trailing `.glia/graph` is stripped: `api/.glia/graph` -> `api`); `--workspace` reads members via read_workspace (relative paths resolve against the file's directory). `--incremental` with --gmap/--workspace is rejected with exit 1 and a one-line error (Repo members already go through LC.8's load_or_rebuild, which is incremental). Errors from merge_layouts (RepoId collision, missing member, unreadable layout) exit 2 with the message. `--layout` -> persist_merge(&r, dir, "merge"); the `[merge] ...` marker is LC.10b's, printed by merge_layouts.
pyo3: merge_gmaps builds Gmap members (basename rule above), calls merge_layouts, persists to `out` when given (persist_merge, writer "py"), and returns a PyGraph through LC.7's from_result (labels, roots, errors carried). ValueError on any merge error.

packets.title: One line convention: every answer record is 1-based; a Locator builds the node index once and returns a named Located record
packets.rationale: Measured on HEAD 7a4883b with target/debug/glia on a 9-line app.py (`def helper` on 1-based line 4, `def main` on line 8; source inlined in the acceptance): `glia blast-radius <d> app::helper` prints `app.py:7` for app::main and --json `"line":7`; `glia trace <d> app::main --json` gives to_line 3 for app::helper; `glia resolve <d> app.py --kind diff --json` gives main 7 / helper 3 / module `app` 0. The installed HEAD wheel (build 0.4.18+p3d23e8828e7ba01a) returns the same 0-based values from blast_radius / cross_stack_trace / resolve, while nodes_json on the same graph returns start_line app 1 / helper 4 / main 8 (py/src/lib.rs PyGraph::nodes_json adds +1) - two conventions in one wheel. The repo-graph MCP shows it live in this session: `find locate_node` answers engine/src/answers.rs:344 (from nodes_json, correct) while `impact locate_node` (backward, depth 1) lists contract_side at answers.rs:815 and cross_stack_trace at :171 - both one line early (the fns start at :816 / :172). The wrapper's `_eloc` (/home/ivy/Code/repo-graph/repo_graph/server.py) prints the raw value and drops line 0 via `if line`, so every MODULE-level record also loses its line. Root cause is one function: engine/src/answers.rs locate_node documents `line` as the 0-indexed POSITION start_line, and all five answer builders (blast_radius_by_qname, cross_stack_trace, resolve_signal_located, governing_docs, contract_side via message_contracts) copy it; the five CLI format!("{f}:{l}") sites (cli/src/main.rs cmd_blast_radius, cmd_docs_for, cmd_contracts, cmd_trace, cmd_resolve) print it verbatim. dense_text / prose already add +1 (projection-text/src/lib.rs render path). Second defect in the same function (recorded by LD-x as unowned): locate_node does `g.nodes.iter().find(|n| n.id == id)` per call, so every located answer is O(rows x V) and apply_scope re-locates per item. CODE_RULES.md section 4 currently contradicts itself about POSITION's base (says 0-indexed, then 'as actually stored ... 1-indexed'); it is fixed here. Storage is NOT changed: POSITION cells stay 0-based rows (engram-export/src/lib.rs and neuropil position.rs / code_viewer.rs read them raw) and ENDPOINT_HIT / ROUTE_METHOD `line` stay 1-based; the convention is fixed once at the record boundary.

packets.implementation:
code-domain/src/project_roots.rs:
```rust
/// Human project name for `repo` (G18): the first manifest that yields a label, in priority order
/// Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, composer.json, go.mod (last `/` segment of the module path), else the directory name.
pub fn project_name(repo: &Path) -> Option<String>
```
Body: for base in that order, read_to_string(repo.join(base)).ok() then manifest_label(base, &text); for go.mod take the text after the last '/'; first Some wins; else repo.file_name(). manifest_label already rejects labels with '::' / '${' / control chars (clean_label) - a stricter superset of core's parsers; pyproject additionally accepts [tool.poetry] (superset). packets.title: MergedGraph traversal API over activation::algo: direction-aware neighbours, bfs, predecessors, reachable_by, shortest_path across cross_edges
packets.rationale: graph/src/traversal.rs exposes neighbours / bfs / predecessors / reachable_by only on RepoGraph (one repo x language graph): none of them sees MergedGraph.cross_edges, so a traversal from a client function can never cross HTTP_CALLS / QUEUE_FLOWS into another repo, and RepoGraph::neighbours is outgoing-only (repo-graph `find neighbours`: graph/src/traversal.rs:17 and py/src/lib.rs:178; `grep -rn '.neighbours('` over glia, neuropil and bench finds no Rust caller of RepoGraph::neighbours). pyo3 PyGraph::neighbours re-implements it as an outgoing-only scan. Measured on HEAD with the installed wheel over a 9-line app.py (main calls helper): `g.neighbours(<main id>)` -> [(helper, 4)] but `g.neighbours(<helper id>)` -> [] although main CALLS it. So the wrapper builds its own adjacency_out / adjacency_in and BFS in Python (/home/ivy/Code/repo-graph/repo_graph/graph.py _build_indices, _traverse, downstream, upstream, shortest_path - an undirected BFS over every edge). LD-x's LD.15a lands the domain-free CSR home (activation::algo: GraphSource impl for MergedGraph, Adjacency, CategorySet, Walk, reach::{bfs, reachable, reachable_by}, Reached {id, depth, via, parent}) and explicitly leaves the direction on neighbours and the merged exposure to this item. LE.5 (why) and LG.3a (feature flows) already consume MergedGraph::shortest_path / bfs with exactly the signatures below.

MATCH TIERS, first that applies wins; the tier NAME is what the record reports (no numeric score):
  exact_qname (qname == q) > exact_name (name == q) > exact_ci (case-insensitive equality on name or qname) > qname_suffix (lowercased qname ends with `::` + lowercased q, so `UserService::get_user` finds the method) > name_prefix (ci) > name_word (ci substring starting at a word boundary of name: after `_` `-` `.` `:` `/` ` `, or at a lower->Upper camel step) > name_substring (ci) > qname_substring (ci substring of qname only, e.g. via the module path) > subsequence (every char of lowercased q appears in order in lowercased name; skipped when q has < 3 chars).
Query normalisation: trim; `.` and `/` in q are also tried as `::` for the qname tiers (a Python dotted path or a file-ish path finds the qname).
TIE-BREAK inside a tier: exact_qname and exact_name use EXACTLY pick_primary's key (total degree desc, NodeId asc), so find(q, 1)'s top row equals node_id_by_qname / resolve_name whenever the match is exact - the single-node resolution LD.2 hands to the wrapper. Every other tier: total degree desc, qname length asc, qname asc, NodeId asc. Degree is computed once for the candidate set in one pass over all_edges into a HashMap used for lookups only (never MergedGraph::degree per candidate, which is O(E) each). Candidates are collected by iterating merged.graphs and g.nodes (Vec order) with nav lookups, then sorted by the full key - no HashMap order reaches the output. kinds filter before ranking; scope via the pub resolve_scope (once) + node_in_scope rule (keep-unlocatable, applied before top_k, same as A8.3). Records are located with LD.1's Locator (1-based line). Twin nodes that share a qname (CLASS + COMPONENT until LB.3) both appear, adjacent, ordered by degree.

[--scope S] [--json]`; table `| match | kind | qname | location |`; `--kind` takes kind NAMES (code_domain::node_kind::ALL lookup, unknown name = exit 2 listing the valid names). engine/src/absence.rs:
```rust
#[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] #[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Absence {
  pub tier: &'static str,            // always "FACT": a statement about the graph as built
  pub reason: &'static str,          // unknown_symbol | no_edges | no_match | no_signal_match | unserved_channel
  pub query: String,
  pub note: String,                  // one sentence, e.g. "no DOCUMENTS edge reaches `app::helper` in this graph"
  pub mechanisms: Vec<&'static str>, // edge categories the answer depended on
  pub caveats: Vec<CoverageNote>,    // coverage rows for those mechanisms, for the languages that matter
  pub suggestions: Vec<String>,      // nearest qnames from find_nodes (top 3), for unknown_symbol / no_match / unserved_channel
  pub nodes_searched: usize,
  pub unparsed_files: usize,         // filled by the surface from parse_errors (MergedGraph does not carry them; LC.7 persists them)
}
#[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] #[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Answer<T> { pub results: Vec<T>, pub absence: Option<Absence> }
pub(crate) fn unknown_symbol(merged: &MergedGraph, query: &str, mechanisms: &[&'static str]) -> Absence;
pub(crate) fn empty(merged: &MergedGraph, query: &str, reason: &'static str, note: String, mechanisms: &[&'static str], seed_file: Option<&str>) -> Absence;
pub(crate) fn mechanisms_for_kind(kind: NodeKindId, reach: Reach) -> &'static [&'static str];
```
Invariant: `absence.is_some()` iff `results.is_empty()` (a helper `Answer::from_results(results, || absence)` enforces it).
Caveat join: coverage::caveats_for keeps the COVERAGE_CAVEATS rows whose edge_category is in `mechanisms` and whose language is `*` or one of `languages` (the seed file's language via coverage::ext_to_language when the seed is located, else every language present - the same inference coverage_report uses); edges_found as today. mechanisms_for_kind is a static table (code knowledge in the code engine; LD.14 may absorb it into the profile): FUNCTION/METHOD -> CALLS; ROUTE/ENDPOINT -> HTTP_CALLS, HANDLED_BY; QUEUE_* -> QUEUE_FLOWS; GRPC_* / GRPC_SERVER -> GRPC_CALLS; RPC_* -> RPC_CALLS; GRAPHQL_* -> GRAPHQL_CALLS; WS_* -> WS_CONNECTS; EVENT_* -> EVENT_FLOWS; CLI_* -> CLI_INVOKES; CLASS/INTERFACE/STRUCT -> IMPLEMENTS, INHERITS_FROM, INJECTS; DATA_ENTITY/DATABASE/CACHE -> ACCESSES_DATA; CONFIG_KEY -> READS_CONFIG; DOC_SECTION -> DOCUMENTS; anything else -> CALLS. Suggestions call find_nodes(query, top_k 3) and keep qnames only.
Wrapped here: resolve_signal_located -> Answer<LocatedNode>: empty seeds -> reason no_signal_match, mechanisms [] (resolution is by POSITION file/line and symbol name, not by edges), note names how many frames/paths/symbols the signal held (count from the same sniffer the graph crate uses - merged.resolve_signal returns ids only, so the note counts input lines matching the stacktrace / diff header shapes; no graph change). governing_docs -> unknown qname = unknown_symbol (mechanisms [DOCUMENTS]); no DOCUMENTS edge = no_edges (mechanisms [DOCUMENTS], language of the target's file). find_nodes -> no candidate in any tier = no_match (suggestions empty: the subsequence tier already ran). Scope interplay: a scope that filters every result to nothing is reason no_match with note 'N results outside scope S' - never a silent empty.
Marker, once per absence built: `eprintln!("[absence] primitive={p} reason={r} mechanisms={m} caveats={c} suggestions={s}")`.
CLI: after the existing `_(no governing docs)_` / `_(nothing resolved)_` line print `> FACT: <note>` then one `> caveat (<lang>, <category>): <note> - verify: <verify>` per caveat and `> did you mean: a, b, c` when suggestions exist; --json prints the envelope object {results, absence}. pyo3: resolve / governing_docs return the envelope as a JSON string (LD.2 turns every answer native), with absence.unparsed_files = self.parse_errors.len().

THE CONVENTION (module docstring + py/README.md; every later pyo3 addition follows it - LE, LF and LG.3c finals already assume it): an ANSWER returns native Python objects (dict / list of dict), keys exactly the engine struct's serde fields; a method whose NAME ends in `_json` returns a JSON string (nodes_json, edges_json, parse_file_to_json stay - bulk dumps where json.loads is the fastest path); pair-shaped data stays tuples (activate, node_cells, kind_names, neighbours); node ids are Python ints (u64, never float). Alternatives weighed: (a) all JSON strings - consistent but forces a json.loads per call and is what lets `_jload` swallow shape errors silently; (b) the pythonize crate - a new dependency whose pyo3 0.28 compatibility is unverified; (c) CHOSEN: a ~40-line converter over serde_json::Value inside py/src/lib.rs: Null->None, Bool->bool, Number: as_u64 -> int, else as_i64 -> int, else as_f64 -> float, String->str, Array->list, Object->dict (insertion order = serde field order).
find(query, top_k=20, kinds=None, scope=None): kinds = list of kind NAMES (validated against node_kind::ALL; unknown -> ValueError listing valid names) -> engine find_nodes -> native Answer {results, absence}. Replaces find_node / find_nodes_by_qname: single-node resolution is `find(q, top_k=1)['results'][0]`, which equals node_id_by_qname / resolve_name for exact matches by LD.3b's pick_primary tie-break; scope here is a FILTER (find_nodes_by_qname's semantics). Seed resolution with scope as a PREFERENCE (LA.14's resolve_seed) stays inside the primitives that take a seed (blast_radius after LD.5).
generate / generate_many: one private build_graph(paths: &[String], incremental: bool) -> PyResult<PyGraph> (ending in LC.7's `from_result(GenerateResult) -> PyGraph`, which already carries repo_labels / repo_roots / parse_errors) used by both (generate passes one path; engine generate_one(_incremental) vs generate_many(_incremental) is chosen inside, preserving each path's HEAD graph). incremental=False is PURE: no cache read, no cache write, no purge. incremental=True loads + saves the per-repo sidecar (engine *_incremental). Neither persists a .gmap: persistence is save_to / save_to_default only (LC.9's persist_result stays the one writer behind them and behind LC.8's load_from_gmap rebuild). Both raise ValueError when every graph is empty and parse errors exist; both print `[parse] N file(s) failed`. pyo3 then no longer reads GLIA_NO_PERSIST (LC.8's load_or_rebuild keeps honouring it for its rebuild write; grade.py's setdefault stays harmless; update the py/README.md and generate docstring mentions). pub struct TracePath { pub rank: usize, pub hops: Vec<TraceHop>, pub cross_service_hops: usize,
```rust
                       pub mechanisms: Vec<&'static str>, pub length: usize, pub directed: bool }
#[derive(serde::Serialize)] #[non_exhaustive]
pub struct TraceAnswer { pub seed: Option<Located>, pub target: Option<Located>, pub resolved_by: &'static str,
                         pub hops: Vec<TraceHop>, pub paths: Vec<TracePath>, pub truncated: bool, pub absence: Option<Absence> }
pub fn cross_stack_trace(merged: &MergedGraph, feature: &str, opts: &TraceOptions) -> TraceAnswer;
```
TraceHop keeps every HEAD field and gains `cross_repo: bool` (HEAD's repo-boundary value, kept so no information is lost). `hops` keeps HEAD's BFS tree exactly (LD.15b's algo::reach::bfs discovery order over Adjacency::carry(merged, &CODE_PROFILE.tables)) so a consumer that only wants the set is unaffected apart from the envelope. `paths`: maximal simple paths from the seed by DFS over a successor map built once per call from all_edges filtered to carry categories (Vec per node in global edge order - deterministic); a path ends where no unvisited successor remains or at `depth`. Expansion budget 50_000 DFS steps -> `truncated = true` (and the marker says so). RANK KEY, no scores: (cross_service_hops desc, distinct mechanisms desc, length desc, the path's qname sequence asc); keep the first max_paths; rank = 1-based position. Each path's hops are full TraceHop records (located via one LD.1 Locator, 1-based, `to_live` from LD.6).
cross_service (the semantic change, declared): true when the repos differ (HEAD rule) OR when the arch keying is ServiceKeying::ProjectRoots and arch::service_of(file) differs between the two ends (default_keying(merged), empty labels map - only equality matters). TopLevelDir keying is NOT used for this flag (a heuristic that would call src/ -> lib/ cross-service in a plain app); a node with no file falls back to the repo comparison. So a manifest-rooted monorepo's web -> api hop is cross-service exactly when `glia arch` draws the link, and multi-repo answers are unchanged.
Two-node mode (`to` set): DFS for simple DIRECTED carry paths seed -> target within depth, same ranking, directed=true; if none, one fallback path from LD.3a MergedGraph::shortest_path(from, to, Reach::Both, None /* all categories: the wrapper's semantics */, depth) with directed=false and each hop's mechanism = the category it traversed. Unreachable -> absence no_edges.
Seed resolution (resolved_by): LA.14's resolve_seed(merged, q, None) - exact qname (`qname`) then exact name (`name`) - then LD.3b find_nodes' top hit if its tier is exact_ci / qname_suffix / name_prefix / name_word (`find`; never the substring or subsequence tiers), else absence unknown_symbol with suggestions. A resolved seed with no outgoing carry edge gives an answer with empty hops / paths and absence no_edges (HEAD printed '_(no outward flow)_'). packets.title: Interface-extends heritage: Java `interface A extends B` and TypeScript `interface A extends B` emit INHERITS_FROM refs
packets.area: LD-api - heritage extraction for the interfaces query
packets.rationale: 'Who implements X' must be transitive through interface inheritance, and two of the biggest languages drop that edge. Measured on HEAD by grading the probe fixtures with bench/substrate-gap/grade.py (installed HEAD wheel): java (Readable; Catalog extends Readable; PgCatalog implements Catalog) -> IMPLEMENTS PgCatalog -> Catalog 1/1, INHERITS_FROM Catalog -> Readable 0/1 (BLIND SPOT); typescript (same shape, one file) -> IMPLEMENTS 1/1, INHERITS_FROM 0/1. Cause, verified in source: parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs visit_type_decl reads the `superclass` and `interfaces` fields of a type declaration only; interface_declaration's `extends_interfaces` child is read only by emit_repository_access's scan. parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs visit_interface records the INTERFACE node and never reads its `extends_type_clause` child. Same sweep, other languages (measured with target/debug/glia, NOT fixed here; LD.7c adds caveat rows): PHP emits no IMPLEMENTS / INHERITS_FROM at all, Swift no protocol conformance, Rust no supertraits (impl-for IMPLEMENTS works); Scala and C# already work. TS interface method signatures are not METHOD nodes (grade: catalog::Readable::read missing) - recorded as a gap, not fixed (type-level implementors do not need them). No item owns interface heritage; it is a letter packet of LD.7 because the query is wrong without it.
entry_points: parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs visit_type_decl (after the `interfaces` field block) - for interface_declaration, each type in the `extends_interfaces` child's type_list -> emit_heritage_ref(.., INHERITS_FROM, ..)
parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs visit_interface - each `type` of an `extends_type_clause` child -> UnresolvedRef Bare(heritage_type_name) INHERITS_FROM (the post-A6.3 shape)
graph/src/calls.rs resolve_refs - count INHERITS_FROM refs whose `from` is an INTERFACE for the marker
bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/java-iface-extends/ + ts-iface-extends/ - NEW

TypeScript: in visit_interface, for a child of kind `extends_type_clause`, iterate children_by_field_name("type") and push `UnresolvedRef { from: iface_id, from_module: module_id, qualifier: Bare(heritage_type_name(ty)), category: INHERITS_FROM }` - the shape A6.3 gives class heritage, so resolve_refs' Bare global fallback (graph/src/calls.rs, which already admits INHERITS_FROM) binds same-file and cross-file targets alike. Direction interface -> super-interface, the same direction as class -> superclass. graph/src/calls.rs resolve_refs: two counters (bound / unresolved) for INHERITS_FROM refs whose `from` kind is INTERFACE; after the loop, if either > 0: `eprintln!("[heritage] interface-extends bound={} unresolved={}")`.

packets.title: Go implicit interfaces: interface method specs become METHOD nodes, embedded interfaces INHERITS_FROM, and a method-set pass emits IMPLEMENTS (Medium)
packets.rationale: next-leap-0.5.0.md: 'Go implicit interfaces are where search fails'. Measured on HEAD by grading the probe (store.go: `type Store interface { Get; Put }`, MemStore with both methods, ReadOnly with Get only, `func Use(s Store)`) with grade.py and the installed wheel: IMPLEMENTS 0/3 (BLIND SPOT), METHOD store::Store::Get / Put missing; `glia analyze` lists INTERFACE store::Store, STRUCT MemStore / ReadOnly and their METHOD nodes and only DEFINES edges.
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] #[non_exhaustive]
pub enum HierarchyDirection { Down /* implementors / subtypes */, Up /* supertypes */ }
#[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] #[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Implementor { pub id: u64, pub qname: String, pub name: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub file: Option<String>,
  pub line: Option<i64>, pub live: bool, pub relation: &'static str /* IMPLEMENTS | INHERITS_FROM of the entering edge */,
  pub depth: usize, pub via: Option<String> /* parent qname when depth > 1 */, pub tier: &'static str /* FACT | DERIVED | HEURISTIC */ }
pub fn implementors(merged: &MergedGraph, qname: &str, direction: HierarchyDirection, transitive: bool) -> Answer<Implementor>;
```
Walk: algo::reach::bfs over Adjacency::build(merged, &CategorySet::of(&[IMPLEMENTS, INHERITS_FROM])) from the resolved target, Walk::Backward for Down, Forward for Up, max_depth usize::MAX when transitive else 1. Target resolution: node_id_by_qname, else pick_primary over the nodes whose NAME equals q restricted to type / method kinds (CLASS, INTERFACE, STRUCT, ENUM, SERVICE, COMPONENT, METHOD) - a Java file MODULE shares its class's name and must never win - else absence unknown_symbol (LD.8a). A METHOD target walks the same categories, which for methods are A6.6's method-level IMPLEMENTS: implementors("Shop::IRepo::Get") lists the implementing methods. tier = weakest edge confidence on the path from the target (Strong -> FACT: declared in source; Medium -> DERIVED: inferred by a rule, e.g. LD.7b's Go method-set match; Weak -> HEURISTIC), computed during the walk from each Reached's parent (min over the parent's tier and the entering edge's confidence - edge confidence looked up once in a (from, to, category) -> confidence map built from all_edges, first occurrence wins). Rows: BFS discovery order, then located via LD.1's Locator, live via LD.6. Empty -> absence no_edges, mechanisms [IMPLEMENTS, INHERITS_FROM], caveats for the target's language.

```rust
#[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] #[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Server { pub id: u64, pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64>, pub live: bool,
  pub r#match: &'static str /* RouteMatch.tier for http; exact for queue */, pub confidence: &'static str, pub handlers: Vec<Located> }
pub fn serves(merged: &MergedGraph, channel: &str, mechanism: &str /* auto | http | queue */) -> Result<Answer<Server>, String>;
```
auto: a leading HTTP verb or '/' -> http, else queue. Err only for an unknown mechanism name.
http: parse `METHOD /path`; a bare `/path` means every verb: lookup under GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE in that order, results deduped by route id (the matcher's own ANY tier still finds method-agnostic routes under each verb). HttpRouteMatcher::new(&merged.graphs) is built once per call; lookup(method, path); r#match = RouteMatch.tier (new field), confidence = RouteMatch's. handlers = HANDLED_BY targets of the route (edge order), located (one LD.1 Locator). live from LD.6. Empty -> absence unserved_channel, mechanisms [HTTP_CALLS, HANDLED_BY], caveats (LD.8a), suggestions (up to 5, deduped, in this order): routes the same matcher returns for the same path under the other verbs [GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE] (the near miss an agent asks next), then routes returned for the parent path (last segment stripped) under any of those verbs - all through lookup, no private index access.
queue: QUEUE_CONSUMER nodes whose qname == `queue_consumer:<topic>` in any graph (dedup by id, graphs in Vec order), handlers = HANDLED_BY targets (present once the LE group's queue anchoring lands; reported honestly as handlers [] until then). A framework-tag topic (extractors::queues::is_framework_tag) is refused with absence note 'a framework tag is not a topic'. Wildcard subscriptions are not matched (QueueStackResolver's matcher is private) - the queue absence carries the universal QUEUE_FLOWS caveats plus the note 'wildcard subscribers are not matched by serves'. Empty -> unserved_channel, suggestions = producers of the topic (a producer with no consumer is the usual finding), then consumer topics differing only by case / separator.

Their order dependencies are implicit: demote_unmatched_http_nodes runs after downgrade_test_paths, link_contract_routes needs the HTTP resolver's cross edges, and the sort must run last (audit 2026-06-10 #6). Registering a resolver means editing build.rs (CLAUDE.md:131; memory 'Three places to wire a new resolver/extractor'). James: 'reachableby, is a good thing to add. same with pass composition.' MOVE, don't rewrite: the body moves verbatim into research/key_symbols.rs; only its inputs change. `pub struct KeySymbolsSynth { pub activated: Vec<(String, f64)>, pub class_seeds: Vec<String>, pub test_patch_facts: TestPatchFacts, pub issue_anchored_qnames: Vec<String>, pub issue: String, pub test_patch: String, pub chain_depths: HashMap<String, usize>, pub top_k: usize, pub aplus_scan: usize, pub chain_grounding_cap: usize, pub max_chars: usize }`. `activated` is seeds.json's list VERBATIM (order kept, unresolvable qnames kept): the ranking loop iterates it by qname and resolve_suffix matches against all of it, so rebuilding it from view.scores (resolved ids only) would change which suffix wins - the plan's scores are NOT this hook's ranking input (that ranking was computed by the `seeds` bin and is task-shaped driver data). synth(g, view): the A+ summaries = view.synth cells whose hook is one of {"summary", "access_path", "callsite_argflow"}, in view order, read as (key=qname, score, text=summary) and filtered by HEAD's own rule (key starts with `synth::AccessPath::`) - so no caller has to classify cells. Output: one SynthCell per SourceCell in rank order: hook "key_symbols", id = rank as u64, key = qname, anchor = Some(effective node id), text = source, score = the ranked score, attrs = [("file",..), ("rank",..), ("reason",..), ("start_line",..), ("end_line",..)]. The max_chars cut becomes a char-boundary clip (largest i <= max_chars with src.is_char_boundary(i)) - byte-identical for ASCII, no panic otherwise. The local SummaryEntry struct and its #[allow(dead_code)] id are deleted (the hook reads SynthCells). `[keysym]` stderr diagnostics keep their text.

Thin bin: every flag and default unchanged (bench/latent/out/run_instance.py, gitignored, invokes it by name); builds KeySymbolsSynth from --issue / --test-patch / seeds.json fields / --chain exactly as main does today; loads EVERY --summaries entry {id, qname, score, summary} as SynthCell { hook: "summary", id, key: qname, score, text: summary } (id is now read, not suppressed); runs ActivationPlan::new(ActivationConfig::default()).synth(&hook).synthesize(&graph, &mut view) over ActivatedView::from_ranked(vec![]) + those cells; maps the key_symbols cells back to SourceCell {qname, file, source, rank, reason, start_line, end_line}; writes the same pretty JSON; prints `[synth] plan hooks=[key_symbols] cells=N`.

packets.title: toy-domain: a test-only second domain ('toy-reel') proving the seam end to end - own registry, header registries, a container section, a profile, passes; built, written, read back, activated
packets.rationale: 0.5.0 is 'prep for cross domain' (James, dev-notes/next-leap-0.5.0.md section 0) and the seam must be proven without shipping a domain (section 3: 'test-only toy second domain ... proves the seam'). The 2026-04-17 design (dev-notes/glia-memory/project_050_domain_agnostic.md) says 'New domains add types through the registries. No core changes required', that navigation lives in 'domain-owned indices stored in the container', and names the video primitive ('frames, shots, scenes, objects (no native names - uses indices)') and an 'ObjectReidentificationResolver' as the video domain's resolver. Neither half is true at HEAD: Header::for_code() writes empty registries with graph_type hardcoded "code" (store/src/lib.rs:315-325) and Container hardwires code_nav: CodeNavStore + symbols: SymbolTableStore (store/src/lib.rs:64-73); kinds and names exist only in code-domain's CodeNav (core::Node is {id, repo, confidence, cells}, core/src/lib.rs:157-162). LC.4/LC.5 fix the store half, LD.13/14/15/12a the engine half; nothing yet proves they compose for a domain that is not code. The activation memory adds: the hook API 'pays off most when a second non-code domain forces real requirements on the trait API'. The toy is deliberately unlike code: nodes have NO names (index-addressed), and its test-only registry REUSES code's numbers - SHOT = NodeKindId(2) (code's CLASS, code-domain/src/lib.rs:36), FEATURES = EdgeCategoryId(3) (code's IMPORTS, :281), TIMECODE = CellTypeId(1) (code's CODE, :445) - so a decoder that consults code-domain instead of the file header produces wrong names and fails. This is not id reuse inside code-domain: the toy's registry is a separate test-only table.

packets.implementation:
INPUT toy-domain/fixtures/reel.txt (the domain's 'input transformer' parses it; one record per line, `#` comments; shot fields = index, start_ms, end_ms, scene):
```
scene 0
shot 0 0 1200 scene=0
shot 1 1200 2600 scene=0
shot 2 2600 4800 scene=0
shot 9 9000 9500
object 0 cat
object 1 dog
object 2 cat
object 9 bird
features 0 0
features 1 1
features 2 2
features 9 9
```
build(): NodeId::from_parts("toy-reel", repo, kind, "<kind>/<index>") (identity key, never displayed); shots get a TIMECODE cell Json {"start_ms","end_ms"}; objects a LABEL cell Text; edges CONTAINS_SHOT scene->shot (3), NEXT_SHOT consecutive shots of one scene (2), FEATURES shot->object from the `features <shot> <object>` lines (4). 9 nodes, 9 edges before passes; edges built in LC.2's Edge shape (empty cell slot) with whatever LC.3 evidence is optional or a `toy-reel` emitter if it is mandatory. ReelNav rows sorted by NodeId; encode = little-endian u32 row count + fixed-width rows (u64 id, u32 kind, u32 index) - opaque bytes to the store.

PASSES (LD.13 PassRegistry<ToyGraph>, C = ()): reidentify_objects (Resolve) - OBJECT pairs with equal LABEL, lower NodeId -> higher, one SAME_OBJECT edge each (cat0 <-> cat2, one edge); screen_time (Post, after=[reidentify_objects], populates=[SCREEN_TIME]) - for each OBJECT, sum the durations of the shots FEATURING any object in its SAME_OBJECT group -> SCREEN_TIME Json {"ms":3400,"shots":2} on both cats (shot 0 = 1200 + shot 2 = 2200), {"ms":1400,"shots":1} dog, {"ms":500,"shots":1} bird; sort_edges (Finalize) sorts edges by (from, to, category). TABLES: graph_type "toy-reel"; registries = the three toy ALL tables; entry = EntryRule { kinds: &[SCENE], named: &[] } (no names exist - is_entry(kind, "")); carry = [CONTAINS_SHOT, NEXT_SHOT, FEATURES, SAME_OBJECT]; effect_sinks = [] (legal: a domain without effects); weights [(NEXT_SHOT,3.0),(FEATURES,2.0),(SAME_OBJECT,4.0),(CONTAINS_SHOT,1.0)]; preset objects = [(SAME_OBJECT, 8.0)]. HOOKS: KindIs(OBJECT) reads ReelNav; ScreenTimeSummary emits one SynthCell per kept OBJECT in view order: text "<label>: <ms> ms across <n> shots".

STORE: the header comes from LC.4's registry-populated constructor fed TOY_TABLES.graph_type and TOY_TABLES.registries; the ReelNav bytes go in LC.5's domain section named "toy.reel.nav"; nodes / edges in the Container as for code. LD.16 needs exactly three capabilities from LC.4/LC.5: (1) a Header built from a graph_type string and three (id, name) tables, not only for_code(); (2) a Container holding a named section of opaque domain bytes and NO code_nav / symbols data; (3) public write + read of such a Container (read_to_owned exists, store/src/lib.rs:471). If (1) or (2) is missing that is an LC.4/LC.5 gap to report in `surprises` and commit nothing - never a toy-side workaround; (3)'s writer this packet adds if absent (4 lines over write_atomic).

Crate hygiene: publish = false; no other Cargo.toml may depend on it (not shipped, not in the wheel: py/Cargo.toml lists its deps explicitly). stamp/build.rs does not hash it (not a graph-shaping root of the CODE build). The end_to_end test prints the marker line.

packets.title: Generic graph delta in activation::algo (the LD.15 home): nodes and edges added / removed / modified / moved between two graph snapshots
packets.rationale: Every change-validation answer in wave E (diff_impact LE.2, tests-to-run LE.3b rev mode, pattern conformance on the delta LE.7a) and Engram's `--since` diff export (LG.8) need one primitive: what a change did to the GRAPH, not to the text. Nothing computes it at HEAD 7a4883b: `grep -rn 'graph_delta\|fn delta' graph/src engine/src activation/src` finds nothing, and the repo-graph wrapper has no equivalent. The item puts it in the LD.15 domain-agnostic home. The LD-x draft of LD.15a names that home `activation::algo` (activation depends on core only, activation/Cargo.toml, so the compiler enforces domain-freedom); this packet follows it. Two facts from HEAD shape the design: (1) one NodeId can sit in several per-language RepoGraphs of one repo (engine/src/answers.rs `collect_queue_nodes`: 'One NodeId can sit in several per-language graphs of one repo'), so node content must be folded across copies before comparing; (2) edges repeat - `message_contracts` dedups QUEUE_FLOWS because 'A node folded from two graphs is walked twice by the resolver, so its edges can repeat' - so edges are compared as a set keyed by (from, to, category), never as a Vec. Every language parser attaches a CODE cell whose CellPayload::Text is the entity's own source text (grep: 19 parser/extractor files emit cell_type::CODE), so 'modified' can be decided from content cells, and a pure line shift (POSITION changes, CODE text does not) is correctly NOT a modification. VERIFIER: two extractors store a CellPayload::Json under CODE that embeds SITE LINE NUMBERS - parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs `finish` writes `{"framework":..,"sites":[{"file":..,"line":N}]}` and cron.rs follows the same precedent - so comparing every CODE payload would flag every queue/cron node below an edited line as modified; only Text payloads are content. Also verified: core NodeId / EdgeCategoryId / CellTypeId derive Hash but NOT Ord (core/src/lib.rs:20-124), and LC.2 keeps it that way ('No Ord derives on the id newtypes'), so the draft's `#[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)] EdgeKey` over NodeId fields and `BTreeMap<NodeId, _>` would not compile.

packets.implementation:
DATA SHAPES (activation/src/algo/delta.rs; core types only - no code_domain, no MergedGraph):
```rust
pub struct DeltaSide<'a> { nodes: Vec<&'a Node>, edges: Vec<&'a Edge> }
impl<'a> DeltaSide<'a> { pub fn new(nodes: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a Node>, edges: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a Edge>) -> Self }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct EdgeKey { pub from: NodeId, pub to: NodeId, pub category: EdgeCategoryId }
impl Ord for EdgeKey { fn cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Ordering { (self.from.0, self.to.0, self.category.0).cmp(&(o.from.0, o.to.0, o.category.0)) } }  // + PartialOrd delegating to cmp; the id newtypes have no Ord
pub struct DeltaOptions<'a> { pub content_cells: &'a [CellTypeId], pub moves: &'a [(NodeId, NodeId)] }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GraphDelta {
    pub added_nodes: Vec<NodeId>, pub removed_nodes: Vec<NodeId>,
    pub modified_nodes: Vec<NodeId>,          // on both sides after remap, content differs; after-side id
    pub moved_nodes: Vec<(NodeId, NodeId)>,   // (before, after) from opts.moves, both ends present
    pub added_edges: Vec<EdgeKey>, pub removed_edges: Vec<EdgeKey>,
    pub reconfidenced_edges: Vec<(EdgeKey, Confidence, Confidence)>,
    pub ignored_moves: usize,
}
pub fn graph_delta(before: &DeltaSide<'_>, after: &DeltaSide<'_>, opts: &DeltaOptions<'_>) -> GraphDelta
```
WHY DeltaSide AND NOT LD.15's GraphSource: GraphSource yields node ids + edges; the delta also needs each node's cells. A caller-built slice pair keeps this module free of any graph type and lets any caller (LE.1b, or a loaded .gmap) feed owned nodes with the same function. The engine builds a side from a MergedGraph in one line (LE.1b).
ALGORITHM (every ordered map is keyed on the raw integers, never on the id newtypes). (1) CONTENT: fold nodes per side into `BTreeMap<u64 /*NodeId.0*/, Vec<(u32 /*cell kind*/, &str)>>` holding ONLY the CellPayload::Text payloads of cells whose kind is in `content_cells`. A Json or Bytes payload under a content kind is positional / structured metadata (queues.rs and cron.rs put `sites:[{file,line}]` JSON under CODE) and is ignored - otherwise a line shift above a queue producer would mark it modified. The per-node list is sorted, so the order in which duplicate copies of one NodeId (several per-language graphs, see engine/src/answers.rs collect_queue_nodes) are folded cannot flip a node to modified. Payloads are borrowed, never cloned (two whole-repo CODE sets would double peak memory). (2) MOVES: `BTreeMap<u64 before, u64 after>` from `opts.moves`, keeping only pairs whose before id exists in `before` and after id in `after`; others count in `ignored_moves`, never an error. remap(id) = mapped id or itself. (3) NODES: BTreeSet<u64> difference of remapped-before vs after; moved pairs go to `moved_nodes`, not added/removed; a moved node whose content also differs is additionally in `modified_nodes` under its after id. (4) EDGES: fold each side into `BTreeMap<EdgeKey, Confidence>` keeping the STRONGEST confidence per key (Strong > Medium > Weak, compared by an explicit rank fn - Confidence has no Ord either); before endpoints are remapped first so a moved file's edges are not reported removed + added. Set difference gives added/removed; equal keys with different confidence go to `reconfidenced_edges`. (5) Edge cells (LC.2) are NOT compared: an edit above a call site shifts the evidence line of every edge below it, and a delta reporting those is noise; the engine layer shows evidence from the after graph. (6) Output Vecs are emitted in BTreeMap/BTreeSet order, so the result is a pure function of the inputs.
ALTERNATIVES WEIGHED: hashing content per node (xxhash) - rejected, activation would need a hashing dep and borrowed comparison is exact; diffing qnames instead of NodeIds - rejected, after LB.1 the NodeId is the identity and qname drift is exactly what LB.6's move map models; comparing every CODE payload - rejected (Json site lists, see (1)). Placement in graph/src - rejected, LD.15 puts domain-agnostic algorithms in activation::algo (graph depends on code-domain).
WIRING: `pub mod delta;` in activation/src/algo/mod.rs; no facade edit (activation/src/lib.rs already has `pub mod algo;` from LD.15a). Test edges are built with LC.2's `Edge::new(..)` (Edge is no longer Copy and gained `cells`).

packets.title: Rev-vs-working-tree delta in the engine: materialise a git rev read-only, build both sides under one repo identity with the shared parse cache, locate every row; plus the two-commit git fixture harness
packets.rationale: LE.1a diffs two in-memory graphs; this packet builds the two graphs for the question users ask - 'what did my uncommitted change (or my branch since <rev>) do to the graph?'. Facts at HEAD that decide the design (verified by the verifier): (1) identity - `generate_one_inner` (engine/src/build.rs) builds `let canonical = format!("file://{repo_path}")`, so a build of a temp checkout mints a different RepoId and every NodeId differs. LB.1 replaces that with `repo_identity(root)` (code-domain walk_gating: git remote / git dir / `dir:<basename>` key); a materialised temp dir has no `.git`, so it would get a `dir:` key - this packet therefore builds the before side under the WORKING TREE's identity explicitly. (2) cost - walk paths are repo-relative, `ParseCache::get(path, hash, lang)` keys on them and `validate_context(repo_canonical, go_prefix)` discards the cache only when identity or go prefix change, so if the before build reuses the after build's cache object every unchanged file skips tree-sitter; LA.12 exposes the per-build CacheDiff through `ParseCache::last_diff()`. (3) external inputs - `SnapshotDocSource::for_repo` reads `<repo>/.glia/docs-snapshot/manifest.jsonl` outside the walk (engine/src/docs.rs), and LF.1a/LF.5a/LF.6a add more untracked inputs under the same control dir (LF.1d: `walk_gating::CONTROL_DIR = ".glia"`); if the before tree lacks them every doc/history node would show as added. (4) walk-derived layout nodes - the walker (engine/src/walk.rs) collapses gitignored / vendored / nested-repo directories into REGION nodes (kind 41) from what is ON DISK; an untracked ignored `node_modules/` exists only in the working tree, so REGION nodes would appear as added on every JS repo - they are excluded from both sides. (5) moves - LB.6 ships `graph::detect_moves(prior, current) -> MoveMap` computed from the two graphs (MODULE body hash, then basename + descendant alignment); that is the move source, so no git rename parsing is needed here. Measured at HEAD: `glia delta /tmp` -> `error: unrecognized subcommand 'delta'`. Security gate respected: local git objects only (`git rev-parse`, `git ls-tree`, `git cat-file`), never fetch, never authenticate. LG.6 lists the two-commit fixture harness 'if LE.1 does not own it' - this packet owns it (engine/tests/git_fixture/mod.rs).

(derive only Serialize: BlastRadius / BlastAnswer derive only Serialize in LD.5's draft; BlastOptions is LD.5's, with its Default.)
SEEDS, rev mode: delta added + modified + moved (after id) nodes, both endpoints of every added edge, and the endpoint of every removed edge that still exists in the after graph (a caller that lost a call). Removed nodes are reported in `changed` located in the BEFORE graph with seed=false (they are not in the after graph). Pasted-diff mode: merged.resolve_signal(diff, "diff") hits (change diff_hit); every `+++ b/<file>` whose file yields no hit goes to `unresolved_diff_files`, so 'nothing changed' and 'glia could not place this file / the hunk only deleted lines' are distinguishable (the pasted mode cannot seed a deletion-only hunk: parse_diff_frames emits frames for added lines only, and resolve_signal is left unchanged because repo-graph's `find` depends on it). MODULE seeds are dropped when a finer node of the same file is also a seed (a MODULE has no carry out-edges and only dilutes PPR); it stays in `changed`. Changed rows are located with one LD.1 Locator per graph.
IMPACT: blast_radius_seeded(after, seeds, opts) - LD.5's one BFS + one PPR over the whole seed list; per-row `seed` (first-reach root) and per-seed linked_seeds come from LD.5 unchanged; empty impact carries LD.8a's absence. Seeds are passed as NodeIds, never re-resolved through qnames (two nodes can share a qname across per-language graphs). ZERO SEEDS (clean tree, or a diff that resolves to nothing): blast radius is not run; impact = an empty BlastRadius whose absence is LD.8a's `empty(..)` with reason no_match and note `no graph change vs <base>` (rev mode) or `the diff resolved to no node` (pasted mode) - constructed inside the engine crate, so #[non_exhaustive] does not block it.
CLI: `glia diff-impact <repo> [--base <rev>] [--diff <file>|-] [--direction both|forward|backward] [--depth 4] [--top-k N] [--live-only] [--scope S] [--json] [--with <repo>...]` - exactly one of --base/--diff (default --base HEAD); `--diff -` reads stdin; --with only with --diff (rev mode builds one repo). Table: a `changed` table, then the impact table in LD.5's blast-radius column layout (its `seed` column). pyo3: `PyGraph.diff_impact(diff_text, direction="both", depth=4, top_k=None, live_only=False, scope=None)` and module `diff_impact_vs_rev(repo_path, base="HEAD", direction="both", depth=4, top_k=None, live_only=False, scope=None)`. ```rust

```rust
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct TestHit { pub qname: String, pub name: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64>, pub tier: &'static str /* fact|derived|heuristic */, pub reason: &'static str /* tests_edge|reaches|module_tests_edge */, pub depth: usize, pub covers: Vec<String>, pub path: Vec<(String, &'static str)> /* witness (qname, category) from the test to its first covered seed */ }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct TestsFor { pub seeds: Vec<String>, pub tests: Vec<TestHit>, pub test_files: Vec<String>, pub untested: Vec<String>, pub unresolved: Vec<String>, pub absence: Option<Absence> /* LD.8a: Some iff tests is empty - reason no_edges, mechanisms [TESTS, CALLS, HTTP_CALLS], with the coverage caveats for the seeds' languages (e.g. CamelCase test modules before A6.7) */ }
pub fn tests_for(merged: &MergedGraph, qnames: &[&str], args: &TestsForArgs) -> Result<TestsFor, String>
pub fn tests_for_diff(merged: &MergedGraph, diff_text: &str, args: &TestsForArgs) -> Result<TestsFor, String>
pub fn tests_for_rev(repo_path: &str, base: &str, args: &TestsForArgs) -> Result<TestsFor, String>
```
TEST_REACH = [CALLS, USES, INJECTS, IMPLEMENTS, TESTS, HANDLED_BY, HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, RPC_CALLS, GRAPHQL_CALLS] walked BACKWARD (reverse HANDLED_BY + HTTP_CALLS is how an integration test that calls `client.get('/users')` reaches the changed handler: handler <- ROUTE <- ENDPOINT <- test). Queue/event flows are excluded: a test that publishes a message does not exercise the consumer synchronously. Adjacency built once over TEST_REACH; one backward reach::bfs per seed (max_depth). Test-case predicate: FUNCTION/METHOD whose ORIGIN provenance is test_fixture and that has no incoming CALLS from another test_fixture node, OR any FUNCTION/METHOD source of a TESTS edge. A test case ends the walk on its branch (it is an answer, not a hop). Tiers: fact = a TESTS edge from the test straight to the seed; derived = reached through >= 1 other edge; heuristic = module_level: the seed's MODULE (nav parent chain) is the target of a module TESTS edge (name-convention pairing) - reported as the test MODULE itself, never expanded into all its cases. A test reached from several seeds is one row with `covers` listing them (sorted) and depth = its minimum. Rows sorted by (tier rank, depth, file, qname); test_files = the distinct files of all rows, sorted; untested = seeds no test reaches. Seeds are NodeIds: qname / name via node_id_by_qname then resolve_name (unknown -> `unresolved`); diff mode = resolve_signal(diff, "diff"); rev mode = LE.1b delta added + modified + moved nodes plus the surviving endpoints of added/removed edges. scope filters rows with node_in_scope semantics. Rows are located through one LD.1 Locator (1-based lines).
Engine records derive serde::Serialize (plus Debug/Clone only where every field type has them - Absence does).
CLI: `glia tests-for <repo> [<qname>...] [--diff <file>|-] [--base <rev>] [--depth 6] [--no-module-level] [--scope S] [--with <repo>...] [--json] [--files-only]` - exactly one seed source; --files-only prints test_files one per line (pipe into pytest / jest / go test). pyo3: `PyGraph.tests_for(qnames, depth=6, scope=None, module_level=True)`, `PyGraph.tests_for_diff(diff_text, ...)`, module `tests_for_rev(repo_path, base="HEAD", ...)`, return convention per LD.2. PYO3 CONVENTION (LD.2): the #[pyfunction] / #[pymethods] body calls a helper that names no pyo3 type and returns serde_json::Value (unit-testable: py/src/lib.rs documents that this crate links without libpython, see the comment above service_map_json), then converts it with LD.2's serde_json::Value -> native Python converter (dict / list, u64 ids stay exact ints); engine Err -> PyValueError.

packets.implementation:
SITES (data_entities.rs, ~90 LOC): `pub enum AccessVerb { Read, Write, Unknown }` and `pub struct AccessSite { pub entity: NodeId, pub offset: usize, pub verb: AccessVerb }`. scan_sql_tables already finds each keyword position (`pos`); it now returns (name, pos, keyword): FROM -> Read unless the preceding token (skipping whitespace, ASCII case-insensitive) is DELETE -> Write; JOIN -> Read; INTO -> Write (INSERT/MERGE/REPLACE INTO); UPDATE -> Write. scan_collection_calls: look at the next `.method(` within 64 bytes after the `collection('x')` close: find*/aggregate/count*/distinct -> Read; insert*/update*/delete*/replace*/bulkWrite/findOneAndUpdate/findOneAndDelete -> Write; else Unknown. scan_cypher_labels: MATCH -> Read, MERGE/CREATE -> Write. Declarations (__tablename__, db_table, mongoose.model, DynamoDB TableName, beanie Settings.name) are NOT access sites: they keep today's module edge and get no site. data_sources.rs provider edges (module -> DATABASE / CACHE / ... bucket) are untouched: they record an import, not a statement. SQL SCANNER OWNERSHIP: LG.3b rewrites scan_sql_tables onto quote-aware SQL string literals (joined across concatenation); this packet builds on that version - each hit's offset is the keyword's byte offset inside the source (for a joined statement, map the keyword back to the literal it came from; use the first literal's start when the mapping is ambiguous) and the verb is read from the joined statement text. Every existing module edge is still emitted by the extractor exactly as today - the extractor stays a pure function of the source, so its unit tests keep passing unchanged; only `sites` is new.
RE-HOME (anchor.rs, ~140 LOC): `pub struct Site { pub target: NodeId, pub line: u32, pub mode: Option<&'static str> }` (line = anchor::line_of(source, offset), mode "read"/"write"/None). rehome_to_owner builds `build_owner_index(&fp.nodes, &fp.nav)` once, groups sites by target (BTreeMap), and for each target: owners = owner_of_line per site (innermost METHOD/FUNCTION); if EVERY site has an owner, remove the (module_id -> target, category) edge; if some are module-scope, keep it. For each (owner, target): fold modes (read+write -> "read_write"; only Unknown -> no mode); if fp.edges already holds (owner -> target, category) - a language parser's own fn-level edge (Go, Python, Ruby) - attach the mode cell to THAT edge instead of pushing a duplicate; else push `Edge::new(owner, target, category, Confidence::Medium)` (LC.2) `.with_cell(Cell { kind: cell_type::ACCESS_MODE, payload: CellPayload::Text(mode) })` when a mode exists, and attach LC.3a's evidence with `evidence::attach(&mut e, Evidence::emitter(emitter).at(path, first_site_line))` (Basis::Site; the emitter string is the caller's, "extractor:data_entities" here - the same stage:name vocabulary LC.3a stamps on run_with_edges! output). When the mode goes onto a parser's existing edge, only the ACCESS_MODE cell is added - that edge keeps its parser evidence. ACCESS_MODE is cell 25, allocated by L0.1. New edges are appended sorted by (from.0, to.0) - never in HashMap order. RehomeStats { to_fn, module_kept, read, write, read_write, unknown }. access_census(fp) recounts those from the finished FileParse (ACCESSES_DATA edges whose `from` is a FUNCTION/METHOD vs MODULE, and ACCESS_MODE cells), so cache-served files count - same pattern as anchor::census.
The helper is generic over the category on purpose: LE.4b re-homes READS_CONFIG through it.

LC.3 adds the evidence (call-site position + emitting extractor / resolver) as edge cells; nothing reads it back as an answer. Every other E packet shows evidence inline, but an agent that doubts ONE edge ("why does glia think the web client calls this route?") needs a direct query - especially for resolver-made cross-service edges (HTTP_CALLS paired by path tier, QUEUE_FLOWS by topic), which are DERIVED, not observed. ENDPOINTS: each side resolves to ALL nodes whose qname equals the argument (qnames_exact), else whose name equals it, capped at 8 per side (two per-language graphs can hold one qname; a name can be shared by several functions); none -> Err("no node with qname/name `x`"). category: validated against edge_category::ALL names (unknown -> Err listing valid names). EDGES: every edge of all_edges() whose (from, to) is in the product (and category matches); rows are one per edge - two call sites of A -> B stay two rows, each with its own site (LC.2 keeps multiplicity). Each row reads `Evidence::of(edge)`: emitter, rule (e.g. the HTTP match tier LC.3c records), basis, and file/line converted to 1-based. TIER from the emitter STAGE (the text before ':'): parser | extractor | docs | graph -> fact (the edge was read at a site in the source, or bound from an extracted reference), EXCEPT emitter graph:refs with rule global_unique -> derived (a unique-name fallback, not a binding); resolver | pass -> derived (paired by name / path / topic / convention); overlay | history -> heuristic. An edge whose basis is none, or with no EVIDENCE cell (an old .gmap loaded without rebuild), is reported with tier derived and note 'no evidence recorded' - never shown as fact. NO DIRECT EDGE: found = false, `absence` = LD.8a's no_edges for the pair (mechanisms = the requested category or every carry category), and `path` = LD.3a's `shortest_path(from_i, to_j, Reach::Forward, Some(CODE_PROFILE.tables.carry_edges), 6)` over the from x to product (first hit in (from, to) product order), each hop explained like a row; empty path + note 'not connected within 6 carry hops' otherwise. packets.title: Tarjan SCC in activation::algo: iterative strongly-connected components plus a shortest witness cycle, over LD.15's Adjacency
packets.rationale: The item puts cycles in the LD.15 domain-agnostic home. Nothing in the workspace finds cycles today (`grep -rni tarjan graph/src engine/src activation/src` -> nothing at HEAD 7a4883b; the only `strongly` hit is an unrelated comment in graph/src/resolvers/grpc.rs). A recursive Tarjan would overflow the stack on long CALLS chains (LD.15's scale gate uses a 40,000-node chain), so the iterative form is required. The witness cycle is what makes a cycle answer located and checkable (LE.6b, LE.8) instead of a bag of node ids.

packets.implementation:
```rust
pub fn strongly_connected(adj: &Adjacency) -> Vec<Vec<NodeId>>
pub fn witness_cycle(adj: &Adjacency, component: &[NodeId], start: NodeId) -> Vec<(NodeId, EdgeCategoryId, NodeId)>
```
strongly_connected: iterative Tarjan over the dense index - explicit frame stack of (vertex, next incidence position), index/lowlink Vec<u32> with u32::MAX as unvisited, on-stack Vec<bool>; roots taken in dense-index order (Adjacency's node order is deterministic). Returns only NON-TRIVIAL components: size >= 2, or size 1 with a self-loop. Each component's ids sorted by NodeId.0; components sorted by their first id - output independent of traversal order. witness_cycle: BFS from `start` restricted to component members (a Vec<bool> membership mask) over successors, parent pointers; the first edge back into `start` closes the cycle; hops returned in order start -> ... -> start with the category of each hop (the first-in-incidence-order edge between two members). Empty Vec when start is not in the component. Both functions are category-agnostic: the caller chooses categories when it builds the Adjacency (LD.15 CategorySet), which is how LE.6b keeps imports and flows apart. Test graphs are fed through a small test GraphSource impl whose edges are built with LC.2's `Edge::new(..)` (LC.2 precedes LD.15a in the leap order). Adjacency's fields are private to activation::algo, which cycles.rs (a child module) may read directly; prefer the `successors` accessor so reach.rs and cycles.rs share one incidence walk.

NODE-LEVEL SERVICE LOOPS (kind event): Adjacency over FLOW_CAUSAL = [QUEUE_FLOWS, EVENT_FLOWS, HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, RPC_CALLS, WS_CONNECTS, GRAPHQL_CALLS, HANDLED_BY, CALLS, USES, INJECTS] -> strongly_connected. Keep components whose members span >= 2 services (arch::service_of with default_keying - one repo is keyed by top-level dir, so orders/ and billing/ are two services, as `glia arch` shows). Witness: witness_cycle from the component's lowest-id flow node (a node with an outgoing QUEUE_FLOWS/EVENT_FLOWS inside the component, else its lowest id). kind event_loop if the witness holds a QUEUE_FLOWS or EVENT_FLOWS hop, else call_loop (sync cross-service recursion). tier derived (every hop is an observed edge; the loop is computed). channels = the topics / paths on the flow hops. 2. SERVICE-LEVEL POSSIBLE LOOPS: from service_map(merged, labels) links whose mechanism is QUEUE_FLOWS or EVENT_FLOWS, build a tiny service graph (an in-memory GraphSource with synthetic ids = hash of the service name) -> strongly_connected. Each service SCC NOT already covered by a node-level loop over the same service set becomes kind possible_loop, tier heuristic, note 'each service both publishes to and consumes from the others, but no consumer-handler -> producer path is in the graph (callback registration and cross-module dispatch may be unextracted)', witness = the service links (file/line of each link's producer). 3. IMPORT CYCLES (kind import): module_import_graph(merged) projects every IMPORTS edge X -> Y to module(X) -> module(Y), where module(n) = n if it is a MODULE, else the nearest MODULE up nav.parent_of in the same graph; self-projections dropped; one projected edge per module pair (first site kept for the witness) -> strongly_connected; rows kind import_cycle, tier derived, services = the modules' services, witness hops located at the importing module's import site (LC.3a `Evidence::of` line when present - LC.3b records import lines - else the module file). Rows located through one LD.1 Locator. scope: keep a row only if all members are in scope (node_in_scope). members capped at max_members (size keeps the full count). Order: event_loop, call_loop, possible_loop, import_cycle; within a kind by size desc, then first member. CLI: `glia cycles [--with ...] [--kind event|import|all] [--scope S] [--json]`, a table per kind with the witness printed as `a -[QUEUE_FLOWS orders.placed]-> b ...`; exit 0 always (reporting, not gating - LE.8's check is the gate). pyo3: `PyGraph.cycles(kind="all", scope=None)`, return convention per LD.2. packets.title: Pattern conformance engine (experimental): roles from kind + edges, population per service, role-chain signature to the first effect sink, verdict as counts with located exceptions; whole-graph and graph-delta modes
packets.rationale: Design source: /home/ivy/.claude/projects/-home-ivy-Code-glia/memory/project_pattern_conformance_hypothesis.md (James's 2026-09-17 handoff: 'an experimental candidate, not an already-decided core feature'; 38/40 handlers go Handler -> Service -> Repository, new code going Handler -> Repository is reported as PATTERN DIVERGENCE, 'does not automatically mean the code is wrong'). Why the graph and not search: the answer is an aggregate over N handlers an LLM will not read before writing the N+1th. Feasibility measured on a Go probe (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/51fd4a3a-5bd1-4db6-8442-972763906d3f/scratchpad/leap-spec/probe/LE/pattern_go, HEAD CLI): ROUTE -HANDLED_BY-> handler, handler -CALLS-> service.GetUser, and `ACCESSES_DATA repository::repository::FindUser -> data_entity:sql:users` (the Go parser's fn-level data access) are all present, so the chain handler > service > repository > db is computable today for Go. The same probe exposed a Go gap outside this item: with the repository file named repo.go (package repository) NO cross-package CALLS into it resolve; renamed to repository.go they all do - cross-package call resolution keys on the file stem (recorded in gaps for LA-core). The fixture therefore uses stem == package. Other languages need Batch C receiver typing (A6.2a/b/c: `this.svc.m()`) and LE.4a's fn-level data access for the chain to exist - hence the dependencies.

packets.implementation:
ROLES (FACT / HEURISTIC by source, never by score): handler = the HANDLED_BY target of a ROUTE (role_source "edge"); service = a SERVICE node (kind 30), a METHOD that a SERVICE CONTAINS (services.rs emits those), a node whose enclosing CLASS has a SERVICE twin (same qname), or an INJECTS target / a method of one (role_source "kind" or "edge"); repository = a node that holds an ACCESSES_DATA out-edge, or whose enclosing CLASS/STRUCT does (role_source "edge"); name fallback ONLY when no structural role applies: a qname segment or name matching /(^|_)(service|services)$|Service$/ -> service, /(^|_)(repo|repository|repositories|store|dao)$|(Repository|Repo|Dao|Store)$/ -> repository (role_source "name", HEURISTIC). Everything else is a helper and does not appear in a signature. SIGNATURE: from each handler, BFS over CALLS / USES / INJECTS / ACCESSES_DATA forward plus IMPLEMENTS backward (interface method -> implementation, A6.6), depth <= max_depth (6), stopping at the FIRST node matching a CODE_PROFILE.tables.effect_sinks entry (LE.4d's EffectSink table: kind + reaching category). Signature = ["handler"] + the roles along the BFS parent path (helpers dropped, consecutive duplicates collapsed) + [sink class], rendered `handler>service>repository>db`; no sink within depth -> `handler>...>(no effect)`. The path hops (with LC.3a `Evidence::of` sites, 1-based via LD.1) are kept as the evidence; rows located through one LD.1 Locator. POPULATION: handlers grouped by arch::service_of(file, repo, &default_keying(merged), repo_labels). A population below min_support (default 5) gets no verdict (counted in skipped_small). CONVENTION: the most frequent signature (ties -> lexicographically smallest); declared only when its count * 100 >= min_share_pct (default 75) * population - a threshold on counts, reported with the counts, never a score. VERDICT per population: `matching/population` (e.g. 38/40) + exceptions: every handler whose signature differs -> Divergence { verdict: "DIVERGENCE", tier: "heuristic" (a convention is observed, not declared - LE.8 owns VIOLATION), handler located, route (method + path from the ROUTE), signature, convention, counts, path hops, role_sources }. ```rust #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct PatternArgs { pub min_support: usize, pub min_share_pct: usize, pub max_depth: usize, pub scope: Option } // Default 5 / 75 / 6 / None #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct Population { pub service: String, pub role: &'static str, pub size: usize, pub convention: Option, pub matching: usize, pub signatures: Vec<(String, usize)>, pub exceptions: Vec } #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct PatternReport { pub experimental: bool /* always true */, pub populations: Vec, pub divergences: Vec, pub skipped_small: usize, pub delta_mode: bool } pub fn pattern_conformance(merged: &MergedGraph, repo_labels: &BTreeMap, args: &PatternArgs) -> PatternReport // labels feed arch::service_of pub fn pattern_conformance_delta(after: &MergedGraph, repo_labels: &BTreeMap, delta: &GraphDelta, args: &PatternArgs) -> PatternReport ``` DELTA MODE ('runs on the graph delta'): populations and conventions come from the whole after graph; `divergences` lists only exceptions whose handler is added / modified / moved in the delta, or whose signature path contains a delta node or an added edge - the 'new code diverges' question. Whole-graph mode: divergences = all exceptions. Ordering: populations by service; exceptions by (signature, handler qname). Marker: `[patterns] experimental populations=

judged= handlers= divergences= skipped_small= role_sources edge= kind= name=`. FACADE (engine/src/lib.rs pub use list changes): `mod patterns;` + `pub use patterns::{Divergence, PatternArgs, PatternReport, Population, pattern_conformance, pattern_conformance_delta};`

(2) below_min_support_no_verdict (4 handlers -> skipped_small 1, no divergence). (3) no_convention_when_split (3 vs 3 -> convention None, no divergences). (4) kind_roles_beat_name - a hand-built MergedGraph where a SERVICE-kind node is named FooHelper still gets role service (role_source kind). packets.title: glia check v1: declared rules (forbidden edges between two paths / projects, no cycles) evaluated to VIOLATION with located evidence; rules read from CONSTRAINT cells; CLI exit code for CI + pyo3
packets.rationale: The design memory (/home/ivy/.claude/projects/-home-ivy-Code-glia/memory/project_pattern_conformance_hypothesis.md) separates the two severities: an explicit human rule ('Domain must not depend on Infrastructure') yields VIOLATION; an observed convention yields DIVERGENCE (LE.7). LE.8 is the first: deterministic, FACT-tier, and gateable in CI. The rules are not re-invented here - LF.4a stores `[[constraint]]` stanzas from .glia/overlay.toml as CONSTRAINT (10) cells anchored on the PROJECT node of their scope and exposes the typed reader LE.8 consumes (sibling LF draft: `declared_constraints(merged) -> Vec<(NodeId, ConstraintRule)>`, ConstraintKind ForbidEdge{from,to} | NoCycle{scope} | Invariant{text}, `categories` as edge-category NAMES, `decl` = '.glia/overlay.toml:<line>'). CONSTRAINT has no emitter and nothing evaluates rules at HEAD (grep cell_type::CONSTRAINT -> registry only); `glia check` is 'unrecognized subcommand'. Cycle rules reuse LE.6's SCC and module-import projection.

```rust

pub fn check(merged: &MergedGraph) -> CheckReport
```
SCOPE MEMBERSHIP IS STRICT: a node is in scope X only when it has a file (arch::node_file on its POSITION) under X on a path-segment boundary (`web` matches web/..., not webhooks/...), or it is a PROJECT node whose path is X. answers.rs node_in_scope KEEPS unlocatable nodes on purpose (for blast/resolve filtering); that leniency would accuse every DATA_ENTITY and queue node here, so check.rs does not use it. Project labels were already resolved to paths by LF.4a (from/to stored resolved + *_raw).
forbid_edge {from, to, categories}: categories = the rule's names mapped through edge_category::ALL (an unknown name -> an `errors` entry, rule skipped); default when empty = IMPORTS + CODE_PROFILE carry edges minus TESTS and DOCUMENTS (tests and docs legitimately cross boundaries). Every edge of all_edges() with category in the set, from-node in `from` and to-node in `to` is evidence (DIRECT edges only - the observed fact; transitive reach is LE.4/LE.2's business). tier fact. Evidence sorted by (file, line, category), capped at 100 per rule with count = the full number; each carries LC.3a's `Evidence::of(edge)` site (1-based) + emitter; rows located through one LD.1 Locator.
no_cycle {scope, categories}: categories empty or [IMPORTS] -> LE.6b's module_import_graph restricted to modules in scope; otherwise a node-level Adjacency over those categories restricted to in-scope nodes; strongly_connected -> one Violation per SCC (tier derived), evidence = witness_cycle hops.
invariant {text}: not machine-checkable -> `unchecked` (listed, never silently dropped).
rules = all CONSTRAINT entries read; checked = forbid_edge + no_cycle evaluated. Violations sorted by rule_id.

scan_feature_yaml (~90 LOC, zero-dep line scanner like scan_openapi): gate = file name `feature.yaml|feature.yml` AND the parent's parent directory is named `features` AND some line starts with `backend_routes:` (whole-file scan - quokka puts it after name/status/purpose; the file is already in memory). Within the backend_routes block (lines indented deeper than the key, up to the next top-level key): items `- <METHOD> <path>` either directly or under one level of group keys (protected:/public:/anything); `backend_routes: []` -> none. Per item: strip a trailing `# comment`, split on whitespace, METHOD case-insensitive in contracts::METHODS, path must start with `/`, strip a `?query` suffix, keep `:param` placeholders verbatim (HttpRouteMatcher folds them). Emit through the existing push_op: qname `contract::feature:<f>::<METHOD>:<path>`, name `<METHOD> <path>`, ORIGIN `{"provenance":"contract","source":"feature_yaml","feature":"<f>","group":"<protected|public|...>"?,"method":"<METHOD>","path":"<path>","raw_path":"<path>"}`, POSITION = the item's 0-indexed line. Everything else in feature.yaml (frontend_components, data_model, ...) is ignored - no DOC_SECTION per file path (fixture forbid).

When Some(slug): the stem segment becomes `feature:<slug>:<stem>` and ORIGIN gains `"feature":"<slug>"` - for openapi, asyncapi and pact alike. Files outside that layout keep today's qnames byte for byte (every existing fixture and contracts.rs unit test is outside it).
Counters: ContractCounts gains feature_yaml and speckit (ops under a spec-kit feature); route.rs prints `[contract] files=.. ops=.. #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct SpecStatusRow { pub feature: Option<String>, pub source: Option<String> /* openapi|feature_yaml */, pub method: String, pub path: String, pub status: &'static str /* implemented|declared_missing|undeclared */, pub confidence: Option<&'static str> /* DOCUMENTS edge: strong exact | medium prefix */, pub route: Option<Located>, pub handler: Option<Located>, pub decl: Option<Located> }   // LD.1's Located (id, name, qname, kind, file, line 1-based) - not LocatedNode, whose PPR `score` means nothing here

DECLARED = DOC_SECTION nodes whose ORIGIN is provenance contract with an HTTP method + path and source in {openapi, feature_yaml} (Pact ops are a CONSUMER's expectation, not a declaration of the provider's surface - excluded and documented; AsyncAPI channel ops have no route). implemented = the op has a DOCUMENTS edge to a ROUTE (confidence from that edge); declared_missing = none. A route documented by several ops (two features declaring GET /orders) yields one implemented row PER op. UNDECLARED = ROUTE nodes (server routes: ORIGIN provenance nav_route excluded - client-side NAV routes are not API) with no incoming DOCUMENTS from a declared op, restricted to GOVERNED services: services (arch::service_of on the route's handler file, else the route's own file) that implement >= 1 declared op. Routes of ungoverned services are only counted (`ungoverned_routes`) - a repo with no specs must not report every route as undeclared. feature: ORIGIN `feature` (LE.9a), else the contract file stem (a repo-wide openapi.yaml is feature `openapi`), None for undeclared rows. route/handler/decl located via one LD.1 Locator (1-based). Sorted by (feature, status rank implemented < declared_missing < undeclared, path, method).

PAYLOAD (CellPayload::Json, compact serde_json, fields in declaration order, capped at 500): `{"format":"proto","fields":[{"name":"total_cents","type":"int64","number":2},{"name":"sku","type":"string","number":3,"label":"repeated"},{"name":"labels","type":"map<string,string>","number":4},{"name":"card_token","type":"string","number":5,"oneof":"payer"}],"reserved":["7","legacy_id"]}`; Avro: `{"format":"avro","fields":[{"name":"coupon","type":"null|string","default":true}]}`. The same object shape (`format` + named sections of field lists) is what LE.10b emits for contract ops, so LE.10c compares one shape.
PROTO (~140 LOC): inside a message body at depth 1: `[repeated|optional|required] <type> <name> = <Num> [\[ options \]] ;` -> field; `map < K , V > <name> = <Num> ;` -> type `map<K,V>` (whitespace removed); `oneof <name> { ... }` -> its fields carry `oneof`; `reserved <nums|ranges|"names"> ;` -> reserved strings; nested `message` / `enum` bodies are skipped here (they are their own nodes and cells); `option`, `extensions`, `extend` ignored. Qualified types (`google.protobuf.Timestamp`, `.shop.v1.Money`) kept as written minus a leading dot. The tokenizer stays comment- and string-aware (existing guarantee).
AVRO (~60 LOC): per record, `fields[]`: name, type rendered canonically - primitive name; union -> members joined by `|` in declared order (`null|string`); array -> `array<T>`; map -> `map<T>`; named/inline record, enum, fixed -> its fullname; `default` -> "default":true when the key is present (value not stored); logicalType appended as `long(timestamp-millis)`.
MARKER in route.rs: `[schema-fields] proto_messages=<M> proto_fields=<F> avro_records=<R> avro_fields=<G>` when M + R > 0.
Unit tests in schemas.rs: proto_scalar_repeated_map_oneof_fields, proto_reserved_captured, proto_nested_message_fields_stay_nested, proto_comment_and_string_braces_ignored (existing guarantee still holds with the new tokens), avro_union_array_map_default, avro_nested_record_type_is_fullname, field_cap_500; existing schemas.rs tests unchanged.

packets.implementation:
ONE INTERMEDIATE SHAPE: `enum YNode { Map(Vec<(String, YNode)>), List(Vec<YNode>), Scalar(String) }`. JSON documents convert from serde_json::Value in 15 LOC; yaml subtrees come from `yaml_subtree` (~110 LOC): the lines indented deeper than a key, parsed as block mappings, `- ` block lists, `[a, b]` flow lists and scalars with quotes stripped - anchors/aliases/multi-line strings are skipped (documented; a skipped construct yields no fields, never a panic). `components` = the document's `components` subtree, built once per file and only when an op references it.
schema_fields(node, components, depth <= 4, seen-refs set) -> flattened `Field { name, type, required }`: `$ref: '#/components/schemas/X'` (or `#/components/messages/X` -> its `payload`) resolved locally (external refs -> one field {name:"$ref", type:<the ref>}); `type: object` + `properties` -> each property (nested objects flattened as `parent.child`, arrays as `name[]` with the item type); `required: [..]` marks fields; allOf merges; oneOf/anyOf -> type `oneOf<A|B>` without descending. Cycle guard via the seen set.
OPENAPI: per op, requestBody.content.<first mime, application/json preferred>.schema -> section `request`; responses.<code>.content.<mime>.schema -> section `response:<code>` for each code. ASYNCAPI v2: channels.<ch>.<publish|subscribe>.message(.payload | $ref); v3: the operation's channel messages' payload -> section `payload`. PACT: interaction request.body / response.body JSON -> keys flattened the same way with the JSON value's type (string/integer/number/boolean/object/array/null), `required` absent (a Pact example states presence, not requiredness) -> sections `request` / `response:<status>`.
PAYLOAD (cell 26, compact): `{"format":"openapi","request":[{"name":"sku","type":"string","required":true},...],"response:201":[{"name":"id","type":"string"}]}` - same object convention as LE.10a (format + named field-list sections).

packets.title: External-input stage + cell sidecar: .glia/cells.jsonl and .glia/vectors.jsonl applied at build through one shared resolver (graph::cells)
packets.rationale: store::upsert_cell (store/src/lib.rs:483) and upsert_cell_sharded (:538) have no caller outside store's own tests (repo-graph impact backward on both = 'No backward nodes found'; grep confirms only store/src/lib.rs tests). Even with a caller they cannot persist: write_sharded (:687) rewrites every shard whose freshly built bytes hash differently from the manifest entry, so the next generate() silently drops any cell written into a .gmap (the rebuild-whole-file design). The leap therefore needs a durable home for externally supplied cells that the BUILD re-applies: a sidecar under .glia/, read by the build exactly like SnapshotDocSource::for_repo (engine/src/docs.rs:193) reads .glia/docs-snapshot/manifest.jsonl. Three consumers must bind a row to the SAME node: the build (this packet), the in-memory write on a live PyGraph and the persisted-gmap write-through (LF.1b). engine only dev-depends on store (engine/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies]) and store cannot call engine, so the one home both reach is the graph crate (store and engine both depend on it, and it already depends on code-domain): graph/src/cells.rs holds the single qname resolver and the single apply function, so in-memory == write-through == next build by construction instead of by two implementations kept in step. The same packet creates the per-repo external-input stage every later LF packet registers in (overlay edges LF.2b, entrypoints LF.3b, declared cells LF.4a, history LF.5b, test reports LF.6b) and loads .glia/overlay.toml ONCE per repo into it (LF.2a's loader), so no later ENGINE stage re-reads the file. The walk and the store's stale scan read only the [walk] / [[project]] sections, through code-domain's walk_gating (LF.3a), because store cannot see RepoInputs. MEASURED at HEAD (probe r1, target/debug/glia analyze): functions carry only CODE / POSITION / IMPORTS; nothing reads any file under .glia/ except the docs snapshot.
