  pub const CELLS_FILE: &str = ".glia/cells.jsonl"; pub const VECTORS_FILE: &str = ".glia/vectors.jsonl"; pub const MAX_VECTOR_BYTES: usize = 65_536;
  pub const WRITABLE: &[CellTypeId] = &[cell_type::CONSTRAINT, cell_type::DECISION, cell_type::CONV, cell_type::VECTOR];
  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct CellRow { qname: String, kind: Option<String> /* NodeKind NAME, disambiguates CLASS vs SERVICE twins */, hint: Option<String> /* LB.6 move-stable hint captured at write time */, cell: String /* cell type NAME */, entry: serde_json::Value }
  #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct VectorRow { qname, kind, hint, model: Option<String>, dims: Option<u32>, b64: String }
  #[non_exhaustive] pub enum WritePayload { Entry(serde_json::Value), Vector { bytes: Vec<u8>, model: Option<String>, dims: Option<u32> } }; #[non_exhaustive] pub struct CellWrite { pub qname: String, pub kind: Option<String>, pub hint: Option<String>, pub cell: CellTypeId, pub payload: WritePayload } with ctors CellWrite::entry(qname, cell, value) / CellWrite::vector(qname, bytes, model, dims) and From<&CellRow> / TryFrom<&VectorRow> (decode + size check).
  pub fn read_rows<T: DeserializeOwned>(path: &Path) -> (Vec<T>, Vec<String>) - one row per non-empty line; a bad line becomes `"<file>:<line>: <serde error>"`, never a panic; missing file = empty.
  pub fn write_rows<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, rows: &[T]) -> io::Result<()> - writes `<file>.tmp` then renames (callers sort). The `.tmp` suffix is what LF.1d's fingerprint excludes, so an in-flight write never counts as an input.
  pub fn canonical(v: &Value) -> Value - rebuild every object through a BTreeMap so key order is sorted even if some crate enables serde_json/preserve_order (feature unification is workspace-wide).
  pub fn validate_entry(cell: CellTypeId, v: &Value) -> Result<(), String>: every entry is an object with `source` in {api, overlay, adr} and `id` (1..=128 chars, no control chars). CONSTRAINT: `kind` in {forbid_edge, no_cycle, invariant}; forbid_edge needs `from` and `to` (scope strings, the --scope vocabulary) and optional `categories` (edge category NAMES); no_cycle optional `scope`/`categories`; invariant needs `text`. DECISION: `title` or `text`; optional `status` lowercased. CONV: `text` 1..=4096 chars, optional `by`, optional `at` (caller-supplied opaque string - glia never reads the clock, the build stays deterministic).
  pub fn merge_entry(existing: Option<&CellPayload>, v: &Value) -> Result<CellPayload, String>: existing must be absent or a Json array (else Err - never clobber an extractor-owned payload); upsert by (source, id); sort by (source, id); serialize the canonical array COMPACTLY (serde_json::to_string, no spaces). This is THE shape of CONSTRAINT/DECISION/CONV (and, via LF.4b/LF.6b, adr DECISION and FAIL) cells: a JSON array of entry objects. LE.8 reads CONSTRAINT through LF.4a's parser over it.
  pub fn remove_entry(existing: &CellPayload, source: &str, id: &str) -> Option<CellPayload> - None when the array empties (caller drops the cell).

  pub struct QnameIndex { by_qname: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(NodeId, NodeKindId)>>, by_hint: BTreeMap<String, NodeId> } - QnameIndex::build(merged, repo: Option<RepoId>) walks g.nodes of every graph (restricted to g.repo == repo when Some) and reads g.nav qname/kind per node - never iterates nav's HashMaps (CODE_RULES §3). by_hint is keyed by the move-stable hint LB.6 gives every node, read through the accessor LB.6's packet ships (LF.1a depends on LB.6, so it exists when this lands; if LB.6 instead makes the stable key a rename map, by_hint is built from that map and a row's `hint` holds the key LB.6 defines). Writers capture the hint of the node they bind at write time (LF.1b set_cell / write_cell, LF.1c cell set). A row written with no gmap and no live graph has hint = null and binds by qname only.
  pub enum CellTarget { Bound(NodeId), Rekeyed(NodeId) /* bound through the hint, qname moved */, Ambiguous(NodeId) /* several matches, smallest NodeId taken */, Orphaned, Rejected(String) }
  resolve(qname, kind: Option<&str>, hint: Option<&str>): candidates by_qname[qname] filtered by kind NAME (node_kind::ALL) when given; one -> Bound; several -> Ambiguous(smallest NodeId); none and hint Some and by_hint hit -> Rekeyed; else Orphaned.

Nodes live in `g.nodes` (find by id in the owning graph).

packets.title: Cell write API: store::write_cell (sidecar + fresh-gmap write-through), pyo3 set_cell / write_cell / remove_cell / node_cell_bytes
packets.rationale: LF.1a gives cells a durable home and one resolver; this packet gives callers a way to write. The MCP wrapper holds a PyGraph in memory and serves the warm path from the persisted gmap (repo-graph server.py:153-157 is_stale -> load_from_gmap), so a write must land in three places to be coherent without a full rebuild: the sidecar (durable), the persisted gmap (warm path) and the live PyGraph. The obvious write-through - patch one shard and refresh the manifest - is UNSAFE: rewriting manifest.json moves its mtime, and scan_for_newer (store/src/lib.rs:1014) compares every source file against that mtime, so a source edited between the build and the write would suddenly predate the manifest and a stale gmap would be served as fresh. Write-through is therefore allowed only when the gmap is fresh right now (is_gmap_stale == false, which covers the stamp, the LF.1d fingerprint and the mtime scan); then every source still predates the rewritten manifest and freshness is preserved. store's existing shard primitive (upsert_cell_sharded, :538) replaces a whole payload (wrong for the JSON-array cells) and `.unwrap()`s in non-test code (:565). PyGraph has no idea where its repo lives: PyGraph {merged, parse_errors, repo_labels} (py/src/lib.rs:21-31) and repo_labels are shortened display labels (engine/src/arch.rs repo_label_map), not paths - so set_cell needs a repo_roots map carried from generate / generate_many / load_from_gmap (which gains its repo path in LC.8). LB.1 is not a prerequisite. Rows are keyed by qname, and the RepoId comes from the GenerateResult (repo_roots keys) or from the gmap itself, so no path-to-RepoId function is called. Ordering after the identity wave still holds through LF.1a -> LB.6.

packets.implementation:
store/src/cells.rs (~170 LOC). `#[derive(Serialize)] pub enum WriteThrough { Applied, NoGmap, GmapStale, NodeMissing, MultiRepo }`; `#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct CellWriteOutcome { pub entry_id: Option<String>, pub rows: usize, pub target: String /* bound|rekeyed|ambiguous|orphaned */, pub write_through: WriteThrough }`.
write_cell(repo_root: &Path, gmap_dir: Option<&Path>, repo: Option<RepoId>, w: &CellWrite) -> Result<CellWriteOutcome, StoreError>:
  1. cell must be in WRITABLE and the payload kind must match (VECTOR <-> Vector), else StoreError::Invalid(msg naming WRITABLE); an Entry gets `source` defaulted to "api" and is validated with validate_entry; a CONV entry without `id` gets the next zero-padded 6-digit id among this qname's api CONV rows (append semantics, no clock).
  2. Lock `.glia/cells.lock` with OpenOptions::create_new (20 tries x 25 ms; a lock older than 30 s is removed as stale). Released by a Drop guard.
  3. `let fresh = gmap_dir.map(|d| !is_gmap_stale(d, repo_root))` - evaluated BEFORE the sidecar changes.
  4. Upsert the row in CELLS_FILE keyed (qname, cell, source, id) - VECTOR rows in VECTORS_FILE keyed (qname) with b64 - sort rows by that key, write_rows.
  5. Write-through only when fresh == Some(true): read_merged_sharded(dir) -> `repo` given ? QnameIndex::build(&merged, Some(repo)) : (the gmap holds exactly one RepoId ? QnameIndex::build(&merged, None) : WriteThrough::MultiRepo) -> graph::apply_cell_write -> on Bound/Rekeyed/Ambiguous store::write_merged_sharded_for_repo(&merged, dir, repo_root) (LF.1d; skip-unchanged rewrites only the touched shard; the manifest's external_inputs is recomputed from disk for THIS root - default or custom dir alike - and now carries the new sidecar hash, so is_gmap_stale stays false) -> Applied; Orphaned -> NodeMissing. fresh == Some(false) -> GmapStale (the next is_stale regenerates anyway); None -> NoGmap.
  remove_cell_entry(repo_root, gmap_dir, repo, qname, cell, source, id) mirrors it with remove_entry. The RepoId comes from the caller when it has one: py passes the owning graph's g.repo, taken from repo_roots. The CLI passes None, and write_cell then uses the one RepoId a per-repo default gmap holds, or returns MultiRepo when it holds several. store never derives repo identity from a path. HINT CAPTURE (LF.1a): when fresh == Some(true), the gmap is read and the row resolved BEFORE the sidecar upsert (step 4). The row's `hint` is the caller-supplied w.hint (py set_cell resolves in memory and passes it), else the hint of the node that read resolved, else null.

packets.title: glia cell set / rm / ls: the CLI surface of the cell write API, with --check and --rekey
packets.rationale: James's CONV ask was explicitly two-surface ("so then we could just write in mempalace info if we wanted to by config ? or other types of things by mcp ?"): config (LF.4a stanzas) and tool calls (LF.1b). The CLI is the third, and the only one that can AUDIT the sidecar: list rows and say which ones no longer bind (a qname renamed by a refactor, or moved - LB.6's hint re-binds those and --rekey rewrites the row). HEAD: `glia cell ...` -> `error: unrecognized subcommand` (exit 2). Depends on LF.2b for the global --no-overlay flag and generate_one_opts, so `ls --check` binds rows against the same graph a normal build produces (wrapper and constant overlays re-key ENDPOINT qnames).
entry_points: cli/src/main.rs Cmd (:43) - new `Cell { #[command(subcommand)] action: CellCmd }` + CellCmd {Set, Rm, Ls}
cli/src/main.rs main dispatch (~:390-425) - `Cmd::Cell { action } => cmd_cell(action)`
cli/src/main.rs - new fn cmd_cell calling store::write_cell / remove_cell_entry and engine apply for --check
packets.implementation:
`glia cell set <repo> <qname> <CELL> (--json '<entry>' | --text '<text>' | --file <path>) [--kind K] [--model M --dims N]`: --text is the CONV shorthand ({"text":...}); --file reads raw bytes for VECTOR; exactly one payload flag (clap ArgGroup). Calls store::write_cell(repo, Some(default gmap dir), None, ..) (a per-repo default gmap holds exactly one RepoId; LF.1b resolves it and captures the node's LB.6 hint into the row) and prints one line `wrote <CELL> <id> for <qname> (write-through: applied|no gmap|gmap stale|node missing)`.
`glia cell rm <repo> <qname> <CELL> --id <id> [--source api]`.
`glia cell ls <repo> [--qname Q] [--json] [--check [--rekey]]`: without --check, reads .glia/cells.jsonl + vectors.jsonl and prints rows (vectors as `<n> bytes`). With --check it builds the graph with engine::generate_one_opts(repo, false, &opts), where opts carries the global --no-overlay flag that LF.2b adds. code-domain/src/walk_gating.rs: `pub const CONTROL_DIR: &str = ".glia";` and is_hard_skip matches it. Consequence: the walk never parses under .glia, no REGION is ever emitted for anything under it, and scan_for_newer never descends into it (its inputs are covered by the fingerprint below). Readers that WANT .glia content (SnapshotDocSource, LF.1a's sidecar, LF.2a's loader, LF.5b/LF.6b snapshot readers) open their files directly, never through the walk.

store/src/lib.rs (~150 LOC incl. tests): Manifest gains `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")] pub external_inputs: BTreeMap<String, String>` (repo-relative path -> hex_xxhash64 of the file bytes). Skipped when empty, so a repo without .glia inputs writes a byte-identical manifest to today. No MANIFEST_VERSION bump - the engine_version / build_stamp precedent (serde default, doc comment at :655-662) applies: an older glia ignores the field, a newer one reading an older manifest regenerates once (LC.1 owns any bump and is a dependency). New `pub fn external_inputs_fingerprint(repo_root: &Path) -> BTreeMap<String,String>`: every regular file under <root>/.glia (sorted recursive walk, '/'-joined repo-relative keys, streaming 1 MiB-chunk hashing) EXCEPT `*.gmap`, MANIFEST_NAME, `parse_cache.bin`, `*.lock`, `*.tmp`, `.gitignore`, and everything under the store's own gmap dir when LC.9 places it inside .glia (compare canonicalised prefixes, as scan_for_newer does for gmap_dir). New `pub fn repo_root_of_gmap_dir(dir: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf>` - the exact inverse of default_gmap_dir (strip the DEFAULT_GMAP_SUBDIR components - after LC.9, its one default dir - from the end; None for any other dir). write_sharded's body moves into a private `fn write_sharded_with(shards, cross_edges, dir, external_inputs: BTreeMap<String,String>)`. The pub write_sharded keeps its signature and passes an empty map, so its external callers store/tests/sharded.rs and store/tests/quokka_dump.rs compile unchanged. write_merged_sharded passes `repo_root_of_gmap_dir(dir).map(|r| external_inputs_fingerprint(&r)).unwrap_or_default()`, so py generate()'s auto-persist and PyGraph.save_to_default (both write to the default dir) record it with NO call-site change. At HEAD the CLI's cmd_build writes flat <repo>/.glia/*.gmap through write_repo_graph, with no manifest. LC.9 routes it through the one writer, and the `*.gmap` exclusion keeps those files out of the fingerprint until then; save_to(<custom dir>) records nothing. is_gmap_stale: after the build-stamp block, `let now = external_inputs_fingerprint(repo_path); if now != m.external_inputs { eprintln!("[gmap] stale: external input changed ({key}) - regenerating"); return true; }` naming the first differing key (added, edited or deleted). New `pub fn write_merged_sharded_for_repo(merged, dir, repo_root: &Path)` records the fingerprint of an explicit root for a custom dir (LF.1b routes pyo3 save_to(dir, repo_path=...) through it). A custom-dir manifest written WITHOUT a root records nothing, so is_gmap_stale(custom_dir, repo) for a repo that HAS .glia inputs reports stale on every call - the safe direction (regenerate, never serve stale), documented on write_merged_sharded.

```rust
pub const OVERLAY_FILE: &str = ".glia/overlay.toml";
#[derive(Deserialize, Default)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct GliaConfig {
  #[serde(default)] pub version: u32,                                   // must be 1
  #[serde(default)] pub walk: WalkConfig,                              // { skip: Vec<String> } gitignore-syntax, root-anchored  -> LF.3a
  #[serde(default)] pub project: Vec<Spanned<ProjectDecl>>,            // { path, label: Option }                          -> LF.3a
  #[serde(default)] pub entrypoints: EntrypointsConfig,                // { qnames: Vec<Spanned<String>> } exact or `::*`   -> LF.3b
  #[serde(default)] pub constants: BTreeMap<String, Spanned<String>>,  // NAME = "literal"                                  -> LF.2d
  #[serde(default)] pub route_prefix: Vec<Spanned<RoutePrefixDecl>>,   // { scope, prefix, origin }                         -> LF.2d
  #[serde(default)] pub wrapper: Vec<Spanned<WrapperDecl>>,            // { call, receiver, kind, method, method_arg, path_arg, topic_arg, broker, origin } -> LF.2e
  #[serde(default)] pub edge: Vec<Spanned<EdgeDecl>>,                  // { from, to, category, note, origin }              -> LF.2b
  #[serde(default)] pub constraint: Vec<Spanned<ConstraintDecl>>,      // { id, kind, from, to, categories, scope, anchor, text } -> LF.4a
  #[serde(default)] pub decision: Vec<Spanned<DecisionDecl>>,          // { id, anchor, scope, title, status, text }        -> LF.4a
  #[serde(default)] pub note: Vec<Spanned<NoteDecl>>,                  // { id, anchor, text, by }                          -> LF.4a
}
#[derive(Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Default)] #[serde(rename_all="lowercase")] pub enum Origin { #[default] Llm, Human }
impl Origin { pub fn provenance(self)->&'static str /* overlay:llm | overlay:human */; pub fn confidence(self)->Confidence /* Weak | Medium */ }
```
Every stanza struct is #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] so a typo fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.
`pub struct LoadedConfig { pub config: GliaConfig, pub errors: Vec<String>, line_starts: Vec<usize> }` with `pub fn line_of(&self, span: Range<usize>) -> u32` (1-based line of span.start via binary search on line_starts) - the evidence line LF.2b/LF.4a record. `pub fn load(repo_root: &Path) -> Option<LoadedConfig>`: None when the file is absent; a TOML or schema error -> Some(LoadedConfig{config: default, errors: [msg with line]}) - NEVER panic, never bail the build (pipeline stages emit empty). Post-parse validation (appends to errors and DROPS only the offending stanza): version must be 1 (else the whole config is defaulted); edge.category must be a name in edge_category::ALL and not DEFINES / CONTAINS / CO_CHANGES (structural or history-owned); route_prefix.prefix starts with '/' and has no whitespace; wrapper.kind in {http, queue_producer, queue_consumer}; `receiver = true` (the review's 'client receivers': `call` names an object whose HTTP-verb members are calls, `api.get('/x')`) requires kind http and forbids method / method_arg (the verb IS the member), path_arg defaults to 0; otherwise http needs path_arg and one of method / method_arg, queue kinds need topic_arg; every *_arg <= 8; constraint.kind in {forbid_edge, no_cycle, invariant} with the same required fields as external_inputs::validate_entry; ids unique within a section; constants keys match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*. `pub fn section_counts(&self) -> [(&'static str, usize); 10]` feeds the marker.
`pub fn is_overlay_empty(&self) -> bool` (no constants/route_prefix/wrapper/edge) so --no-overlay reporting is exact.

packets.title: Overlay applier: [[edge]] stanzas as Weak ORIGIN-overlay edges with evidence, BuildOptions and --no-overlay
packets.rationale: Explicit edges are the overlay's escape hatch for what no extractor can see (a fetch whose URL is built in a helper, reflection, config-driven dispatch). Probe r1 (HEAD): `loadOrders -> list_orders` declared as an [[edge]] produced nothing. Review section 5 fixes the semantics: applied deterministically at build, ORIGIN `overlay:llm`, Weak, and a switch (`--no-overlay`) so primitives can be compared with and without it - which is also how the accept loop (LF.2c overlay_delta) measures an overlay. Edges carry their provenance on the edge itself, which needs LC.2's edge-cell slot and LC.3's evidence (file .glia/overlay.toml + the stanza's line), so LE.5 why(edge) answers 'declared in .glia/overlay.toml:12 by overlay:llm'. The switch is a build option, not an env var: pyo3 generate() may run on several Python threads, so process-global env (the GLIA_API_PREFIXES precedent) would race. The switch is BUILD-time, not a query-time edge filter, because two overlay sections (LF.2d constants and route_prefix, LF.2e wrappers) rewrite qnames and pairings rather than add edges - no query-time filter can undo a re-keyed ENDPOINT, so the only consistent 'without overlay' view is a build without it.

CONSTANTS. ConstTable::pin(key, value) -> bool runs the SAME gates as the source scan's insert: is_secret_name(key) and accept_value(value). An overlay constant never bypasses secret redaction, and a rejected pin returns false and is counted. Otherwise it does `by_key.insert(key, value)`, `alternatives.remove(key)`, `pinned.insert(key)`. Pinning happens AFTER every source merge, so first-wins never overrides it and resolve_expr_strict sees an unambiguous key. merge_from stays as is (a later merge into a pinned key would add alternatives - document that pins must be applied last). conflicts() excludes pinned keys. build_graphs_for_repo: `if opts.overlay { for (k, v) in &config.constants { const_table.pin(k, v.get_ref()) } }` then `[overlay] constants repo=<label> pinned=N overrode=O rejected=R` where overrode counts keys that already had a different source binding and rejected counts pins the secret / value gates refused. endpoint_fold plan_entry: after `folded` is computed from the template, `let pins = consts.pinned_keys_in(template)`; if non-empty set fields "overlay" = "const:" + pins.join(",") and return the stanza origin's confidence in the Plan (the Plan struct gains `confidence: Option<Confidence>`, applied where the plan rewrites the node). Queue topics minted by LA.4's fold from a pinned key are LA.4's call site; ConstTable::is_pinned is the hook it needs (see open question).

MOUNTS. graph/src/resolvers/http.rs: `#[derive(Default, Clone)] pub struct RouteMounts { by_route: BTreeMap<NodeId, Vec<(String, Confidence)>> }` with `pub fn add(&mut self, route: NodeId, prefix: &str, conf: Confidence)` and `is_empty()`. build_route_index gains `mounts: &RouteMounts`: for a ROUTE in by_route, after the normal registration, also insert every `(method, normalise_http_path(prefix + path))` into the STRONG `index` with a RouteTarget whose confidence = weakest(route.confidence, mount conf) and a new `mounted: bool` = true. HttpMatchStats gains `mount_keys` / `mount_hits` and a SEPARATE line `[http] overlay mounts: routes=R keys=K paired=P` (the existing `[http] routes=...` line is unchanged, so no pinned marker moves). HttpRouteMatcher::new keeps RouteMounts::default() (the contract linker pairs DECLARED paths; a gateway mount is not part of an OpenAPI path). engine/src/external/overlay.rs route_mounts: for each repo's [[route_prefix]] (only when opts.overlay): scope -> path via answers::resolve_scope (label or path; `.`/`""` = whole repo), then every ROUTE node of THAT repo whose located file (answers::locate_node(..).3 - ROUTE nodes carry no POSITION, probe r1 shows only IMPORTS+ROUTE_METHOD, so the handler fallback is required) is in scope; unlocatable routes are NOT mounted (unlike node_in_scope's keep rule). run_all_resolvers(merged, &mounts) calls HttpStackResolver.resolve_with_mounts when mounts is non-empty, else the unchanged trait path (so builds without an overlay are byte-identical).

packets.title: Overlay [[wrapper]] maps: call sites of a declared HTTP/queue wrapper or client receiver minted as ENDPOINT / queue nodes
packets.rationale: The commonest client blind spot is a hand-rolled wrapper: the coverage caveat already says so (engine/src/coverage.rs: "calls hidden behind custom wrappers may be missed"). Probe r1 on HEAD: `export async function loadUsers() { return request('GET', '/users'); }` with `function request(method, path) { return fetch(path, { method }); }` yields only `endpoint:GET:<unresolved>` (the inner fetch) - the call site that carries the identity is invisible. A [[wrapper]] stanza names the wrapper and which positional arguments hold the verb / path (or topic), and glia mints the node at every call site with the canonical helper the parsers use (code_domain::endpoint::push_client_endpoint_with, code-domain/src/lib.rs:1510), anchored to its enclosing function. The arg reader already exists: parsers/code/extractors/src/queue_topic.rs scan(source, needle, TopicRule::ArgIndex(n)) returns the first quoted literal inside positional arg n, boundary-safe. The review's section 5 also lists 'client receivers': an object whose HTTP-verb members are the calls. MEASURED at HEAD (probe w1, target/debug/glia merge web api): `const api = makeClient(); ... return api.get('/orders');` and `api.delete(`/orders/${id}`)` mint NO ENDPOINT (`[http] routes=4 endpoints=0 paired=0`), and the wrapper form mints only `endpoint:GET:<unresolved>`. The receiver form is the same machinery with the verb read from the member name, so it lives in this packet. Also measured: the ungated `request(` needle in parsers/code/extractors/src/graphql.rs:22 turns every such wrapper into a false GRAPHQL_OPERATION `graphql_op:request` - not this packet's to fix (reported as a gap), and the fixture does not assert on it.

Runs post-cache (cached parses get it too), per file whose detect_language is Some and that contains the needle `<call>(` (call = `request`, `api.request`, `ApiClient.request`; `languages` filter optional). Hit filtering: the byte before the needle must not be an identifier char (so `xrequest(` does not match; `.` is allowed for receiver forms); skip hits whose line (trimmed) starts with `//`, `#`, `*`, `--` or `/*` (commented-out calls); skip definition sites - the preceding token on the line is `function`, `def`, `fn`, `func`, `fun`, or the text after the closing paren is `{` / `:` on a signature line with type annotations (`request(method: string` - detect a `:` inside the arg region before any quote). Args: `queue_topic::scan(source, needle, TopicRule::ArgIndex(i))` for method_arg / path_arg / topic_arg, joined by hit offset. A non-literal path/topic -> skip (count skipped_nonliteral; no identity = no node); method literal is uppercased, must be one of the HTTP verbs, else skipped; a fixed `method = "GET"` needs no arg.
RECEIVER form (`receiver = true`): needles are `<call>.<verb>(` for verb in get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options, matched case-insensitively on the verb only (C# `Get(`, Dart `get(`); same identifier-boundary, comment and definition skips; method = the verb uppercased; path = queue_topic::scan ArgIndex(path_arg, default 0) of that hit. The needle is built per stanza, so `api.` never matches `this.apiClient.`.
Mint: http -> ClientEndpoint { method, path, file, line, col, confidence: origin.confidence() } through push_client_endpoint_with (dedup per file via its `seen` set; the CALLS edge from the enclosing function comes with it) with the enclosing function found by anchor::build_owner_index + owner_of_line (module id when none); the node gains ORIGIN Json {"provenance":"overlay:llm","rule":"wrapper#<n>"}. queue_producer / queue_consumer -> the same node shape the queue scanner emits (`queue_producer:<topic>` / `queue_consumer:<topic>`, kinds QUEUE_PRODUCER / QUEUE_CONSUMER) with the optional `broker` as the framework tag, POSITION via anchor::position_cell, ORIGIN as above. If the parser already emitted the same qname at the same line, skip (count duplicate). Per-file panic isolation: wrap each file's pass in catch_unwind like apply_rpc_needles and push `<path>: PANIC (overlay wrappers)` to parse_errors.

The walk and store::is_gmap_stale must agree (code-domain/src/walk_gating.rs module doc: 'Two consumers must agree or the graph lies about itself'), so the skip lives in the shared IgnoreStack both construct at the root (engine/src/walk.rs walk_source_files :64 and store/src/lib.rs scan_for_newer :1033). store/src/lib.rs scan_for_newer (:1014, stack init :1033) - IgnoreStack::for_repo(root) instead of IgnoreStack::default(); the file branch also skips is_excluded files
packets.implementation:
Skip semantics: gitignore syntax, anchored at the repo root (GitignoreBuilder::new(root) + add_line per pattern), matched against repo-relative paths. A skipped DIRECTORY becomes a REGION anchor with ORIGIN provenance "excluded" (the map stays honest: the directory exists, glia was told not to read it) - precedence in gate_dir: hard-skip -> nested repo -> excluded -> always-region -> ignored -> dotnet -> bundle -> descend (a user skip on `vendor` records "excluded", the more specific fact). A skipped FILE is simply not read (like a gitignored file). Patterns only extend the defaults: nothing in the config can un-skip a hard-skip or un-collapse a region. Invalid pattern -> logged by the loader, skipped. The matcher lives in an Arc so the per-directory clones in scan_for_newer stay O(depth) pointer copies. The walk calls IgnoreStack::with_config on the config it loaded, and the store calls IgnoreStack::for_repo, which is load + with_config. Both build the matcher through with_config, so they cannot disagree. engine/src/build.rs is NOT touched: the walk loads the file itself, because RepoInputs (LF.1a) is built after the walk and store cannot see it. A second silent parse of a small TOML per build is the price of keeping the build order. GateCounts marker becomes `collapsed N regions (always= gitignore= bundle= dotnet= nested= config=)` - update the pinned string in walk_gating's counts_render_the_marker test in the same commit.
Declared roots: for each [[project]] (path normalised: no leading `./` or `/`, no trailing `/`), require that it is a directory the walk DESCENDED into (not collapsed / skipped) - else `[roots] declared root <path> skipped: <reason>` and count missing. If a detected root already has that rel_path, keep the detected one (count shadowed) - config extends, never replaces. Otherwise push ProjectRoot::declared(path, label) (label fallback = the existing basename chain in ProjectRoot::new). The existing explicit sort then fixes node order. Marker `[roots] declared=D shadowed=S missing=M` printed when the config has [[project]] stanzas. User config is NOT disabled by --no-overlay (it is config, not inference).

packets.title: User config: [entrypoints] as ENTRYPOINT cells that seed liveness
packets.rationale: Liveness only knows kind-shaped entrypoints (engine/src/answers.rs is_entrypoint :35 - routes, handlers, CLI commands, components, main/test*). Scheduled jobs wired by a string, plugin hooks loaded by reflection, and library public APIs are flagged dead. Probe e1 on HEAD: app/jobs.py nightly_rollup() -> summarise(); blast_radius(nightly_rollup, forward) returns summarise with `"live":false`. The user can say 'this is an entrypoint' in config; persisting the declaration as a cell (not re-reading config at query time) makes it survive the .gmap warm path and reach every consumer (Engram, neuropil) with the same semantics. LD.6 unifies the entrypoint set; this adds the per-node declaration it consults.

packets.implementation:
Patterns from [entrypoints].qnames: an exact qname, or a prefix ending `::*` (matches the prefix node's descendants by qname prefix `

::`, not the prefix node itself). Patterns come from RepoInputs.config (loaded once by LF.1a). Matched over graph::QnameIndex for the repo (BTreeMap, deterministic). Each matched node gains cell_type::ENTRYPOINT (id 28, L0.1) Json {"source":"config","pattern":,"decl":".glia/overlay.toml:"} - first matching pattern wins, one cell per node. Unmatched patterns are counted and listed by LF.2c's orphaned_rule. Not disabled by --no-overlay (user config). answers.rs: in LD.6's entrypoint seeding loop, `is_entrypoint(kind, name) || n.cells.iter().any(|c| c.kind == cell_type::ENTRYPOINT)`. The ENTRYPOINT cell also makes the node count as an entrypoint for LD.6's entry_kinds()-based `live` flags, since those derive from entrypoint_reachable. projection-text/src/lib.rs cell_label (:613): 28 => "entry" (dense text would otherwise print the generic `cell` label for ENTRYPOINT), with an assertion beside the existing cell_label test (:1146).

packets.title: Declared knowledge: [[constraint]], [[decision]] and [[note]] stanzas as CONSTRAINT / DECISION / CONV cells, and the rule reader LE.8 consumes
packets.rationale: CONSTRAINT (10), DECISION (11) and CONV (13) are registered (code-domain/src/lib.rs cell_type) and have NO emitter anywhere (grep for cell_type::CONSTRAINT / DECISION / CONV outside the registry finds only bench/tui-viewer's label table). The leap fills them through the override surface: LF.1a/1b for tool-written entries, this packet for the checked-in declarations. LE.8 (check_* v1) stores its forbidden-edge and no-cycle rules as CONSTRAINT cells 'via the override file (LF)', so the rule schema and a typed reader are defined here once. A path-level rule belongs to no single symbol: it anchors on the PROJECT node for its scope (LF.3a lets a user declare a manifest-less project to anchor on), which keeps it on a real node, visible to node_cells, the .gmap and every consumer. VECTOR (14) enters only through LF.1b's bytes API - glia never computes embeddings, and bytes do not belong in a TOML file.
entry_points: engine/src/external/declared.rs (new) - apply_declared_cells(merged, input, config) + pub(crate) fn declared_constraints(merged) -> Vec<(NodeId, ConstraintRule)>
engine/src/external/mod.rs - register the stage (after the sidecar stage, before entrypoints)
code-domain/src/external_inputs.rs - pub struct ConstraintRule + pub fn parse_constraints(&CellPayload) -> Vec<ConstraintRule>
packets.implementation:
Stanzas come from RepoInputs.config (loaded once by LF.1a). Anchor resolution (shared by all three stanza kinds): `anchor = <qname>` -> graph::QnameIndex::resolve in the repo (smallest NodeId on ties); else the scope field (constraint: `from` for forbid_edge, `scope` for no_cycle/invariant; decision: `scope`) -> answers::resolve_scope(merged, scope) -> the PROJECT node whose ORIGIN path equals it (project_roots(merged)); `.`/`""` -> the root PROJECT when one exists. No anchor -> orphaned (counted; LF.2c lists it). Entries (merged with external_inputs::merge_entry, so they coexist with api/adr entries in one canonical array):
  constraint -> CONSTRAINT {"source":"overlay","id","kind","from"?,"to"?,"categories"?,"scope"?,"text"?,"origin":"human|llm","decl":".glia/overlay.toml:<line>"}. `from`/`to` are stored RESOLVED to paths (resolve_scope output) plus the raw value as `from_raw`/`to_raw` so LE.8 never re-resolves labels.
  decision -> DECISION {"source":"overlay","id","title"?,"status"?,"text"?,"decl"}.
  note -> CONV {"source":"overlay","id" (given, else `note#<n>`),"text","by"?,"decl"}.
Declared knowledge is NOT disabled by --no-overlay (it is a rule/decision, not an inferred edge).

packets.title: Git-history snapshot writer: new snapshots crate capturing commits, per-file churn, renames and optional blame runs - local git only, no author identities
packets.rationale: History is an external, HEAD-dependent input, so it must enter like docs do: a separate snapshot step writes files the deterministic build reads (memory project_cochange_blind_spot_audit: 'must enter through a separate snapshot step (the way glia docs sync writes .glia/docs-snapshot/ before build ingests it), or the byte-identical build breaks'). Probe g1 (HEAD): a git repo where svc/a.py and svc/b.py changed together in 4 commits and svc/c.py was renamed to svc/c2.py builds 6 nodes with edge categories {DEFINES} only and no ATTN cell. The capture format was verified on this machine: `git log -z --numstat -M --no-merges --relative --format=%x1e%H%x1f%ct` yields `\x1e<sha>\x1f<unix>` then `\n` then `<a>\t<d>\t<path>\0` per file, renames as `<a>\t<d>\t\0<old>\0<new>\0`, binaries as `-\t-\t`. The item names blame too (ATTN: blame / churn): file churn says a file is hot, blame says which function in it moved and when. HOW git is read, weighed: git2 needs libgit2 (a C build in the manylinux/aarch64 wheel matrix); gix is pure Rust but a large dependency tree the wheel would carry for one command; shelling out to the git binary (std::process::Command) costs nothing when unused and reads exactly what the user's git sees - CHOSEN. No crate in the workspace spawns a process today (grep Command::new over engine/cli/py/store/graph/code-domain/doc-sources = 0), which is why the spawning lives in its own crate: the build never runs git, and the published wheel only runs it when history_sync is called. This packet is the library only; the CLI/pyo3 surfaces are LF.5d so cli/src/main.rs and py/src/lib.rs are touched once for all history work. SECURITY / scope: author names and emails are NEVER captured - per-person attribution is team ownership, which is explicitly out ('everything but team ownership', 2026-04-17); no fetch, no remote, no other repo.

code-domain/src/snapshots.rs (new) - HistoryMeta / HistoryCommit / HistoryFile / BlameFile serde records + read_history(root) / write_history(root, ..) (the build reads through this, like DocRecord)

Records (code-domain/src/snapshots.rs, serde, deny_unknown_fields): `HistoryMeta { version: 1, generator: "glia history sync", head: String /* full sha */, commits: usize, max_commits: usize, since: Option<String>, relative_to: String /* repo root relative to the git toplevel, '' at top */, blame_files: usize, data_hash: String /* xxhash64 over commits.jsonl then blame.jsonl bytes */ }` - NO wall-clock timestamp (a re-sync at the same HEAD must produce identical bytes). `HistoryCommit { c: String /* sha */, t: i64 /* committer unix time %ct */, files: Vec<HistoryFile> }`, `HistoryFile { p: String, a: Option<u32>, d: Option<u32> /* None for binary */, from: Option<String> /* rename source */ }`, `BlameFile { p: String, runs: Vec<[i64; 3]> /* start_line1, end_line1 (inclusive), committer time */ }`. Files under `.glia/history-snapshot/`: commits.jsonl (newest first, as git gives), blame.jsonl (sorted by p; empty file when blame is off), then meta.json LAST (a reader that sees meta sees complete data). read_history(root) -> Option<HistorySnapshot { meta, commits, blame }> (None and a `[history] snapshot incomplete` warning when meta is absent or data_hash mismatches). write_history writes `<file>.tmp` then renames (the `.tmp` suffix is excluded from LF.1d's fingerprint). code-domain/src/snapshots.rs also exports `pub fn data_hash(parts: &[&[u8]]) -> String` (xxhash64, seed 0, over the concatenation, 16 lowercase hex). The writer, the readers (read_history, and LF.6a's read_tests) and fixture authors all use it: LF.5b / LF.6b / LF.6c compute their fixture meta.json data_hash with it.
snapshots/src/git_history.rs (~260 LOC): `HistoryOptions { max_commits: usize (default 2000), since: Option<String>, blame: bool (default false), blame_max_files: usize (default 300), surface: &'static str }`. `git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD` (not a repo / no commits -> Err with a plain message); `git -C <root> rev-parse --show-prefix` for relative_to; `git -C <root> -c core.quotepath=off log -z --numstat -M --no-merges --relative --format=%x1e%H%x1f%ct -n <max> [--since=<since>]` with LC_ALL=C, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_PAGER=cat; parse incrementally: split records on \x1e; header `<sha>\x1f<ct>` up to the first \0 or \n; then \0-separated tokens: `a\td\tpath`, or `a\td\t` followed by two tokens old,new (rename); skip leading '\n'; `-` counts -> None. Paths are bytes -> String::from_utf8_lossy (non-UTF-8 paths degrade, never panic). git's stderr is surfaced in the Err. Blame (only when opts.blame): files ranked by commit count desc then path, first blame_max_files that still exist at HEAD; `git -C <root> blame --porcelain -w HEAD -- <path>`: header lines `<sha> <orig> <final> [<n>]`, `committer-time <t>` recorded the first time a sha appears (cache sha -> t), EVERY `author*` / `committer` / `committer-mail` line skipped unread, content lines start with TAB and are skipped; consecutive final lines with the same t collapse into runs. Finally create `.glia/.gitignore` if absent with `history-snapshot/`, `test-snapshot/`, `docs-snapshot/`, `vectors.jsonl` (never overwrite an existing one). history_sync prints the marker (with surface) and returns HistorySummary { head, commits, files, renames, binary, blame_files, runs }.

packets.title: History ingest at build: ATTN churn on modules, ATTN recency on symbols (blame), and CO_CHANGES edges between files that change together
packets.rationale: ATTN (8) is registered with no emitter (grep: only bench/tui-viewer labels it). Churn is the classic attention signal - where changes (and bugs) concentrate - and it is a FACT given the snapshot; blame recency is the same fact at symbol granularity. Co-change is the raw material for the blind-spot audit (LF.5c): files that repeatedly change together are coupled, and when the static graph has no edge between them the coupling is invisible to it. The memory note that proposed it says 'A cochange edge would be a new EdgeCategory id ... (additive)'. Emitting it as an edge makes 'what usually changes with this file' a graph query; because it is HEURISTIC-tier it is Weak, outside blast_carry_edges (graph/src/blast.rs:41), outside entrypoint reachability, and weighted 0 in activation - activation's weight for an unlisted category defaults to 1.0 (activation/src/lib.rs ~:138 unwrap_or(1.0)), so it must be listed explicitly or it would reshape every PPR ranking in a repo with a snapshot.
entry_points: engine/src/external/history.rs (new) - history_edges(merged, input) (CO_CHANGES) and history_cells(merged, input) (ATTN)

packets.implementation:
Read via code_domain::snapshots::read_history(input.root); absent -> no-op, no marker. File -> MODULE: the repo's MODULE nodes by their POSITION `file` (exact repo-relative match; BTreeMap). Renames: walk commits newest -> oldest keeping `alias: BTreeMap<String,String>` (old path -> current path): a file entry with from=Some(old) sets alias[old] = current(new); every path is attributed to current(path). Paths with no MODULE (yaml, lockfiles, docs) are counted unmapped and ignored.
history_cells - ATTN on MODULE: Json {"source":"git","commits":N,"lines_added":A,"lines_deleted":D,"first":t_min,"last":t_max,"window_commits":W,"head":<12-char sha>} (integers only - no floats, no 'age' relative to now; the consumer computes recency). ATTN on symbols from blame: for each FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS with a POSITION span [s0, e0] (0-based) in a blamed file, intersect runs with [s0+1, e0+1] (blame is 1-based): Json {"source":"git-blame","last":t_max,"span_changes":<distinct t>,"head":..}. A node that already has ATTN is skipped and counted.
history_edges - CO_CHANGES: per commit with 2 <= mapped files <= MAX_COMMIT_FILES (30; mass reformats and vendoring commits are noise), count unordered pairs (a < b by path) in a BTreeMap<(String,String), u32>. Keep pairs with count >= MIN_SUPPORT (3) and 1000*count / min(commits_a, commits_b) >= MIN_RATIO_PERMILLE (300). Sort kept pairs by (count desc, a, b), cap at MAX_PAIRS (5000). One edge per pair onto merged.cross_edges (this stage runs before post_passes' sort) from MODULE(a) to MODULE(b), category CO_CHANGES (L0.1, id 38), Confidence::Weak, with LC.2 edge cell ATTN {"cochanges":n,"ratio_permille":r,"window_commits":W} and LC.3 evidence {emitter: "history", file: ".glia/history-snapshot/meta.json"}. Both halves run whether or not --no-overlay is set (history is a fact input, not the LLM overlay).
All ATTN payloads are serialized compactly (serde_json::to_string over canonical BTreeMaps: `"commits":4`, no spaces) - the fixture's `contains` depends on it. graph/src/merged.rs: SYMMETRIC gains CO_CHANGES (+ unit test cochange_links_are_normalised: two CO_CHANGES edges a->b and b->a between two keys collapse into ONE CrossLink row). graph/src/activation.rs: CO_CHANGES weight 0.0 in code_activation_defaults (profiles inherit it; none upweights it). Do not add it to blast_carry_edges.

packets.title: Co-change-without-edge audit: file pairs that change together but share no static link, in glia coverage and glia gaps
packets.rationale: The point of history in glia is the self-audit (memory project_cochange_blind_spot_audit): 'files that frequently change together but have no edge between them are likely coupled through something static extraction misses ... That turns cochange into a self-audit for the graph, feeding the P2 coverage blind-spot report.' coverage_report (engine/src/coverage.rs) is a static caveat table - it cannot point at a SPECIFIC place where this repo's graph is blind. Probe g1: svc/a.py and svc/b.py co-changed 4 times with no edge of any category between them - the audit's first row. Cross-service coupling is a static link too (a.ts ENDPOINT -> HTTP_CALLS -> ROUTE -> HANDLED_BY -> b.py), so the check allows short bridges through file-less nodes or every correctly paired client/server file pair would be reported. Python reaches the rows through PyGraph.gaps(category="cochange_no_edge") (LF.2c), so no new pyo3 method is needed.
entry_points: engine/src/gaps.rs - pub struct CochangeGap + pub fn cochange_gaps(merged, top_k) and the `cochange_no_edge` category in gaps_report

cochange_gaps(merged, top_k: Option<usize>) -> Vec<CochangeGap { file_a, file_b, cochanges: u32, ratio_permille: u32, language_a, language_b, cross_language: bool, tier: "heuristic" }>: for every CO_CHANGES edge (counts read from its LC.2 ATTN edge cell), A = node ids whose POSITION file == file(a) (incl. the MODULE), B likewise. LINKED if a path of length <= 3 connects any node of A to any node of B, in either direction, over edges whose category is not CO_CHANGES / DEFINES / CONTAINS, where every INTERMEDIATE node is file-less (no POSITION: ENDPOINT, ROUTE, queue / event nodes, PACKAGE_DEP, ...). Direct edges (incl. IMPORTS, CALLS, TESTS, DOCUMENTS) count as linked. One undirected filtered adjacency (BTreeMap<NodeId, Vec<NodeId>>) built once; per pair a bounded BFS from A to depth 3 expanding only through file-less nodes. Unlinked pairs are gaps, sorted by (cochanges desc, file_a, file_b), truncated to top_k. coverage::ext_to_language (pub(crate)) labels languages. gaps_report gains category cochange_no_edge (tier heuristic, suggest edge) using the same function. Marker per call `[cochange] pairs=P linked=L gaps=G (direct=D bridged=B) surface=coverage|gaps`. The coverage section heading states the tier: '(heuristic: co-change is history, not proof of coupling)'.

packets.title: Parallel per-file route/parse/extract on a big-stack rayon pool, thread-safe quiet panics, order-preserving fold
packets.area: LG.1 perf - rayon over walk / parse / extract
packets.rationale: HEAD builds single-threaded. Measured 2026-09-18 on a 16-core box: `/usr/bin/time env GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 target/debug/glia analyze <repo> --format json` = quokka-stack wall 2.93 s / user 2.87 s, glia wall 8.51 s / user 8.37 s (user/wall 0.98, one core). Release wheel (installed, build 0.4.18+p3d23e8828e7ba01a = HEAD code) `repo_graph_py.generate(path, False)`: grpc-go 4.17 s (14,071 nodes), glia 1.29 s, neuropil 0.88 s, quokka-stack 0.48 s, lapse 0.38 s. The per-file tree-sitter parse alone (pyo3 parse_file_to_json over the tracked sources, WITHOUT the cross-cutting extractors) costs 0.66 s of glia's 1.29 s and 1.53 s of grpc-go's 4.17 s; engine/src/route.rs parse_repo_files runs parse_one_with + apply_cross_cutting_extractors for every file in one sequential `for (path, source) in files` loop. Nothing in the workspace is parallel today (grep rayon/par_iter/thread::scope: only std::thread::sleep in store tests); rayon is not in Cargo.lock (crossbeam-deque/epoch/utils already are, via `ignore`). Four things in the current code block a naive par_iter, all verified by reading it: (1) engine/src/build.rs SuppressPanicHook swaps the PROCESS-GLOBAL panic hook for the scope of build_graphs_for_repo, and its own doc comment says it 'assumes single-threaded parsing (true today). If parsing ever goes parallel, switch to panic::update_hook filtering by thread' - update_hook is unstable; (2) the graphql branch of parse_repo_files reaches back into the shared map after stashing (`parses_by_lang.get_mut("graphql").and_then(|v| v.last_mut())`) to attach anchors; (3) the ParseCache is read (`get`) and written (`put`) inline in the loop; (4) rayon workers get a 2 MiB stack by default while the main thread (and a Python caller's) has 8 MiB, and every language parser recurses over the AST (visit_children); a stack overflow aborts the process and is NOT caught by catch_unwind, so a deeply nested file that parses today would kill the whole build on a worker. Also: only the language-parser branch is inside catch_unwind today; a panic in a yaml / Dockerfile / manifest / dotenv / json / proto / graphql / avro extractor propagates and ends the build (memory rule: isolate panics per file). DESIGN CHOICE. (a) std::thread::scope + an AtomicUsize work index, zero deps - rejected: hand-rolled chunking, no work stealing (file sizes are very skewed: glia's largest .rs files dominate), and ordered collection has to be rebuilt by hand. (b) rayon's GLOBAL pool - rejected: stack size is not ours to set (RAYON_NUM_THREADS / the first caller wins), and an in-process consumer that also uses the global pool (neuropil is a Bevy app) would share queues with us. (c) CHOSEN: rayon with a dedicated, lazily built engine pool. `IndexedParallelIterator::map(..).collect::<Vec<_>>()` preserves input order by construction, which is exactly the determinism contract (byte_identical.rs), and work stealing absorbs the size skew. rayon is fetched once from crates.io (network verified available); its crossbeam deps are already in Cargo.lock.

engine/src/parallel.rs (~110 LOC incl. tests):
```rust
static POOL: OnceLock<Option<rayon::ThreadPool>> = OnceLock::new();
pub(crate) fn threads() -> usize  // GLIA_THREADS env (read once): unset/0/unparsable -> std::thread::available_parallelism (fallback 1); clamp 1..=256
fn engine_pool() -> Option<&'static rayon::ThreadPool>  // None when threads()==1; else ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(threads()).stack_size(16 << 20).thread_name(|i| format!("glia-parse-{i}")).build().ok() - a build error degrades to sequential, never panics
pub(crate) fn par_map_ordered<T: Sync, R: Send>(items: &[T], f: impl Fn(&T) -> R + Sync + Send) -> (Vec<R>, usize /*threads used for the marker*/)
    // if rayon::current_thread_index().is_some() -> already inside a caller's pool (a test or an embedding app): items.par_iter().map(f).collect() on THAT pool, report rayon::current_num_threads()
    // else if let Some(p) = engine_pool() -> p.install(|| items.par_iter().map(f).collect()), report p.current_num_threads()
    // else items.iter().map(f).collect(), report 1  (GLIA_THREADS=1 = today's behaviour, on the caller's thread)
thread_local!(static QUIET: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) });
pub(crate) fn install_quiet_hook()  // Once: let prev = take_hook(); set_hook(Box::new(move |info| if !QUIET.with(Cell::get) { prev(info) }))
pub(crate) fn quiet<R>(f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> std::thread::Result<R>  // install_quiet_hook(); RAII guard sets QUIET=true on THIS thread and restores the previous value on drop (also on unwind); catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(f))
```
The hook is installed once per process and never swapped back, so there is no global take/restore race; suppression is per thread and scoped to the guarded closure, so a panic anywhere else in the process (another thread, the embedding app) still reaches the original hook. This replaces the 'switch to update_hook' plan in SuppressPanicHook's comment without the unstable API.

Why 16 MiB: the main thread (and a CPython thread) runs with 8 MiB; the parsers recurse per AST level; rayon's default is 2 MiB and an overflow aborts the process (not catchable). 16 MiB is virtual reservation only (16 threads = 256 MiB VSZ, RSS unchanged) and gives headroom over today's main-thread limit.

packets.risks: Determinism is carried entirely by order-preserving collect + a sequential fold in walk order; never push into shared state from inside route_one, never iterate a HashMap to emit (memory: HashMap iteration is random). Stack: without stack_size(16 MiB) a deep file aborts the process (uncatchable); the deep_nesting test guards it. UTF-8/byte offsets: untouched - route_one is the old body verbatim. LA.12 (ParseCache diff / [incremental] marker computed from diff) and LA.13 (per-root go_prefix threaded into parse_repo_files) both rewrite this same function: land after them and carry their shape into RouteCtx (hence depends_on). Nested pools: a caller already inside a rayon pool gets its own pool used (current_thread_index check) instead of a blocking install into ours. Tiny repos: dispatch overhead is microseconds; no min-length tuning needed. pyo3: worker threads never touch Python objects; the GIL is not needed. Global counters: di_stats uses AtomicUsize (thread-safe) and is reset once per build_graphs_for_repo, before the parallel region - unchanged semantics. Do not parallelise across repos in generate_many here (di_stats::reset is per repo) - LG.1b parallelises only the walks. Branch drift: if a sibling packet adds a route.rs branch between this spec and landing, carry it into route_one (implementation note 2); the pool-size test only protects branches its fixture exercises.

packets.title: install-hooks --pair: G8/u151 branch-pair pre-commit + Glia-Pinned-At commit-msg trailer, and hooks written where git reads them
packets.rationale: neuropil docs/spec-vNext.md u151 (LOCKED, 'pre-commit hook auto-verify'): 'pre-commit hook installed by `glia install-hooks` (extended) checks neuropil's current branch matches a same-name branch in `../glia`; blocks commit on mismatch with a clear message ("glia branch `<name>` missing - `git -C ../glia checkout -b <name>` first"). Also writes the glia commit-SHA into the neuropil commit's trailer (`Glia-Pinned-At: <sha>`).' The G8 convention (memory reference_glia_upgrade_spec_handoff): 'any change touching the public contract uses the same branch name in both repos'. HEAD: cli/src/main.rs HOOK_NAMES = ["post-commit", "post-merge", "post-checkout"] only; `glia install-hooks --pair ../glia .` -> `error: unexpected argument '--pair' found`. neuropil already claims otherwise: crates/neuropil-app/src/hooks_install_prompt.rs says 'the hook bundle now includes the branch-pair verifier (`pre-commit`) ... See `glia install-hooks`' and its modal text says install-hooks writes '.git/hooks/{post-commit, pre-commit} (pre-commit also enforces the cross-repo branch-pair lock per u151)'. neuropil ships tools/check_branch_pair.sh as a stand-in. Probes (scratch, git 2.55): a pre-commit hook receives NO arguments (`pre-commit args=[]`), so it can never write a trailer - check_branch_pair.sh's trailer branch is unreachable from pre-commit; commit-msg receives the message file and is skipped by --no-verify; prepare-commit-msg runs BEFORE the editor (a trailer there turns an empty-message abort into a trailer-only commit - probed: with GIT_EDITOR=true the commit went through with only the trailer). commit-msg + `git stripspace --strip-comments` + `git interpret-trailers --in-place --if-exists replace` was probed end to end: empty message still aborts, edited message gets exactly one trailer, `--amend` replaces the old sha. Two existing install-hooks bugs found by probe: (1) in a linked WORKTREE, cmd_install_hooks resolves `.git` (a file) to `<main>/.git/worktrees/<wt>/hooks` and writes there - git reads hooks from the common dir (`git rev-parse --git-path hooks` -> `<main>/.git/hooks`), so the installed hooks never fire (probe: commit in the worktree, marker file never written); (2) with `core.hooksPath` set, install writes `.git/hooks` and git runs `.githooks` - hooks never fire (probe). Also found: neuropil's needs_install() greps `.git/hooks/post-commit` for `# glia post-commit` but glia writes `# glia-install-hooks: managed`, so neuropil re-prompts forever (handoff item, not fixable in glia). cli/src/hooks.rs (~260 LOC incl. unit tests):
```rust
pub(crate) const REBUILD_HOOKS: &[&str] = &["post-commit", "post-merge", "post-checkout"];
pub(crate) const PAIR_HOOKS: &[&str] = &["pre-commit", "commit-msg"];
pub(crate) const HOOK_MARKER: &str = "# glia-install-hooks: managed";  // unchanged - existing installs stay recognised
pub(crate) const TRAILER: &str = "Glia-Pinned-At";
fn hooks_dir(repo: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String>
   // `git -C <repo> rev-parse --git-path hooks` (honours core.hooksPath and linked worktrees; relative output is joined to <repo>). Fallback when git is not runnable: <repo>/.git dir -> .git/hooks; .git file -> gitdir: line, then if <gitdir>/commondir exists use <gitdir>/<commondir>/hooks (the old code stopped at <gitdir>/hooks = the bug).
enum Verdict { Match { branch, pair_sha }, Missing { branch }, OtherBranch { branch, pair_branch }, PairDetached { branch }, OursDetached, NoPairRepo }
fn verdict(ours: Option<&str>, pair_head_branch: Option<&str>, pair_has_branch: bool, pair_ok: bool, pair_sha: Option<&str>) -> Verdict   // pure, unit-tested
pub(crate) fn run_pre_commit(pair: &str) -> i32
pub(crate) fn run_commit_msg(msg_file: &str, pair: &str) -> i32
pub(crate) fn cmd_install_hooks(repo: &str, uninstall: bool, command: Option<&str>, pair: Option<&str>) -> i32
```
SEMANTICS (the lock, stated in the module doc): pass iff the pair repo's CHECKED-OUT branch equals ours. Checked-out rather than merely existing, because the consumer builds against the pair's working tree through path deps - pinning a sha from a branch that is not checked out would record code that was never compiled. u151's message is used verbatim for the missing case. Messages (stderr, then exit 1): Missing -> `[hooks] branch-pair BLOCKED: glia branch `feat-x` missing - `git -C ../glia checkout -b feat-x` first`; OtherBranch -> `[hooks] branch-pair BLOCKED: ../glia is on `main`, not `feat-x` - `git -C ../glia checkout feat-x``; PairDetached -> `... ../glia is on a detached HEAD`; NoPairRepo -> `[hooks] branch-pair BLOCKED: ../glia is not a git repository (install-hooks --pair)`. OursDetached (rebase / bisect in progress) -> `[hooks] branch-pair skipped: detached HEAD` exit 0. Match -> `[hooks] branch-pair ok: feat-x == ../glia @ <sha7>` exit 0; if the pair tree is dirty (`git -C <pair> status --porcelain` non-empty) also print `[hooks] branch-pair: ../glia has uncommitted changes; the pin records HEAD, not the working tree`. Escape hatches: `git commit --no-verify` (git skips both pair hooks); env `GLIA_BRANCH_PAIR=skip` makes run_pre_commit print `[hooks] branch-pair skipped (GLIA_BRANCH_PAIR=skip)` and exit 0 (the pin is still written). The pair path is resolved relative to the repo top-level (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), matching u151's `../glia`.
run_commit_msg: read msg_file; if `git stripspace --strip-comments` of it is empty -> exit 0 untouched (git then aborts the empty commit, as probed); resolve pair HEAD sha (`git -C <pair> rev-parse HEAD`; failure -> print a warning, exit 0 - commit-msg never blocks on pinning); run `git interpret-trailers --in-place --if-exists replace --trailer "Glia-Pinned-At: <sha>" <msg_file>`; print `[hooks] pinned Glia-Pinned-At: <sha>`. Replace (not add) so `--amend` after the pair moved keeps exactly one, current trailer (probed).
Hook scripts (render_hook_script gains a pair variant; every script starts with `#!/bin/sh` + HOOK_MARKER so is_glia_managed / uninstall keep working):
  pre-commit:  `command -v glia >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo '[hooks] glia not on PATH - branch-pair check skipped' >&2; exit 0; }` then `exec glia hook pre-commit --pair '<pair>'`
  commit-msg:  same guard, then `exec glia hook commit-msg --pair '<pair>' "$1"`
  (single-quote the pair path, escaping embedded `'` as `'\''`). Fail-open when glia is missing: an environment problem is not a branch mismatch, and a hard failure there would block every commit on a machine without glia.
cmd_install_hooks: resolve hooks_dir; install REBUILD_HOOKS always (unchanged content) and PAIR_HOOKS only with --pair (pair must be an existing git repo, else exit 2 with a message); same refuse-to-clobber rule for non-managed hooks; uninstall removes every managed hook in REBUILD_HOOKS + PAIR_HOOKS. Summary line: `[hooks] installed N hook(s) into <dir> (skipped K non-managed, branch-pair=<pair>|off)` (replaces the old `installed N hook(s) into ... (skipped K non-managed)` line). --command still only affects the rebuild hooks.
cli/cli_surface.txt: regenerate with LG.6a's GLIA_UPDATE_SURFACE=1 (new --pair flag, hidden `hook` subcommand listed with hidden=true).

DATA SHAPES (serde::Serialize; field order = output order):
```rust
pub enum FlowGrouping { Feature, Entry }
#[non_exhaustive] pub struct FlowOptions { pub grouping: FlowGrouping, pub depth: usize /*default 6, the wrapper's*/, pub caller_depth: usize /*default 3*/, pub feature: Option<String>, pub scope: Option<String> }  // + Default, per LD.9's convention
pub struct FeatureFlow { pub feature: String, pub services: Vec<String>, pub entries: Vec<FlowEntry>, pub data_sources: Vec<FlowSink> }
pub struct FlowEntry { pub entry: FlowStep, pub weakest: &'static str, pub callers: Vec<FlowStep>, pub steps: Vec<FlowStep> }
pub struct FlowStep { pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub service: Option<String>, pub via: Option<&'static str>, pub confidence: &'static str, pub cross_service: bool, pub depth: usize, pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64> }
pub struct FlowSink { pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub via: &'static str, pub tier: &'static str /* FACT | HEURISTIC */, pub from: String }
pub fn feature_flows(merged: &MergedGraph, repo_labels: &BTreeMap<u64, String>, opts: &FlowOptions) -> Vec<FeatureFlow>
pub fn render_flow_yaml(flow: &FeatureFlow, grouping: FlowGrouping) -> String
pub fn write_feature_flows(repo_roots: &[&Path], dir: &Path, flows: &[FeatureFlow], grouping: FlowGrouping) -> std::io::Result<FlowsWritten>  // repo_roots = the build's repos, for the walked-tree refusal below  // FlowsWritten { written, unchanged, removed: usize }
```
ENTRIES: nodes for which CODE_PROFILE.tables.entry.is_entry(kind, name) holds (LD.6's reconciled set - the same rule LD.4b's entry_flows and `live` use, never a third list), minus COMPONENT and the FUNCTION/METHOD `main`/`test*` name rule (flows describe externally-triggered channels; components show up as callers). Client navigation ROUTEs are entries too: a page with no outgoing edges is listed with empty steps, so the page inventory the script produced (frontend_page) survives.
FEATURE KEY (feature_key, pure, unit-tested), from channel_of(qname, name): ROUTE and WS_HANDLER share one namespace = the first STATIC path segment after dropping a leading `api` segment and version segments matching `v<digits>`; placeholders (`:id`, `{id}`, `<id>`, `*`, `**`, `*any`, `[slug]`) are not static; none left -> `root`; lowercased. Others are prefixed by mechanism: QUEUE_CONSUMER `queue-<topic>`, EVENT_HANDLER `event-<channel>`, GRPC_SERVICE `grpc-<last segment of the service>`, GRAPHQL_RESOLVER `graphql`, CLI_COMMAND `cli-<first word>`, CRON_JOB `cron-<channel>`, anything else `<kind lowercase>-<name>`. Slug to [a-z0-9._-] (others -> `-`, runs collapsed, trimmed, max 64 bytes on a char boundary). FlowGrouping::Entry keys by LD.4b's EntryFlow.key (the wrapper-compatible slug) so `glia flows` and the files agree; two entries with one key get `<key>`, `<key>-2`, ... in (key, entry qname) order - deterministic, never HashMap order. HTTP and WS sharing the path namespace is deliberate: a nav page `/orders`, the API routes `/api/orders/:id` and a `/orders/ws` socket are one feature, which is what the script's per-feature files meant.
STEPS: the entry's downstream hops = LD.3a `merged.bfs(&[entry], Reach::Forward, Some(CODE_PROFILE.tables.carry_edges), opts.depth)` - the same carry adjacency LD.4b's entry_flows walks, so a feature's step set is exactly the union of its entries' LD.4b reach (assert this in a test). Build the Adjacency ONCE per feature_flows call and reuse it for every entry (LD.15a Adjacency::carry), never per entry. For each hop, confidence = the carrying edge's Confidence (strong|medium|weak) read through LD.3's adjacency, kind via kind name, file/line from locate_node (1-based after LD.1), service from arch::service_of under default_keying. Ordered by (depth, qname) - never by HashMap order. weakest = the minimum confidence over callers + steps.
CALLERS: LD.3a `merged.bfs(&[entry], Reach::Backward, Some(CALLER_CATEGORIES), opts.caller_depth)` (one backward Adjacency per call) restricted to HTTP_CALLS, GRPC_CALLS, RPC_CALLS, QUEUE_FLOWS, EVENT_FLOWS, WS_CONNECTS, GRAPHQL_CALLS, CLI_INVOKES, CALLS, INJECTS, up to opts.caller_depth: e.g. ENDPOINT -HTTP_CALLS-> ROUTE, METHOD OrdersService::list -CALLS-> ENDPOINT, COMPONENT method -CALLS-> service method. cross_service from service_of on both ends.
DATA SOURCES: the targets of ACCESSES_DATA edges (node kinds DATABASE, CACHE, BLOB_STORE, SEARCH_INDEX, EMAIL_SERVICE, DATA_ENTITY) whose source is (a) any flow step itself -> tier FACT, or (b) the MODULE that CONTAINS / DEFINES a flow step, which is where the cross-cutting extractor anchors its edges today -> tier HEURISTIC (file-level: 'the file holding this step touches X'). Deduped by qname keeping the strongest tier, sorted by qname. LE.4's function-level ACCESSES_DATA turns HEURISTIC rows into FACT rows with no change here.
YAML (render_flow_yaml): line 1 `# generated by glia <VERSION_LINE> - glia flows; do not edit`, then `feature:`, `grouping:`, `services: [..]`, `entries:` and `data_sources:` blocks where every step / sink is ONE line holding serde_json::to_string of the struct - a JSON object is a valid YAML flow mapping, so qnames containing `::`, `{id}` or `#` need no YAML quoting rules and the file stays greppable one record per line.
WRITER: `<dir>/<feature>.yaml` + `<dir>/index.json` = {generator, grouping, features:[{feature, file, entries, callers, steps, data_sources, weakest}]}; write tmp + rename; skip a file whose bytes are unchanged (mtime-stable for watchers); delete only files named in the PREVIOUS index.json and not produced now (never touch a file glia did not list).

packets.rationale: Necessary work no leap item covers, found by the LG.3 dogfood: the flows' `data_sources` column is garbage on both dogfood repos today. quokka-stack (MongoDB backend, zero SQL) has 41 DATA_ENTITY nodes at HEAD and 0 are real: data_entity:sql:{JWT, NATS, O, a, all, already, backlog, buffer, caller, creating, default, document, each, error, event, every, existing, from, initialMsg, interface, its, logic, match, matches, message, password, profile, room, rooms, seed, signals, spaces, status, stream, swipe, the, token, user, ...} + graph:Api. Root cause, parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs: extract_data_entity_nodes gates on has_sql_context(source) over the WHOLE FILE (its 'select ' signature matches Go's `select {` channel statement - turps/Services/chat/helper.go has six) and then scan_sql_tables(source) runs FROM/JOIN/INTO/UPDATE over the whole file including comments and prose strings, although the section comment says it pulls names 'inside string literals'. lapse (real Postgres SQL in Go backtick literals) has 98 DATA_ENTITY at HEAD: its DDL (migrations/*.sql + CREATE TABLE literals) declares 32 tables; 28 of them are found, the other ~70 nodes are junk: the, their, another, anywhere, both, one, so, prior, deterministic, COALESCE, LATERAL, SET, jsonb, JWT, AusTender, Filename, and CTE aliases (task_counts, opp_ids, chosen_brief). Missing forms: Go mongo-driver / Firestore `.Collection("x")` (capital C) and C# MongoDB.Driver `GetCollection<T>("x" | nameof(T))` - scan_collection_calls only knows `.collection(`; a survey of local repos found 17 `.Collection(` and 60+ `GetCollection<..>(` call sites (webplatform, splortscore). Fixture baselines recorded on HEAD with grade.py (installed wheel = HEAD code): go-data-entity-precision -> nodes 5/6, ACCESSES_DATA 1/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 7 (token, all, the, spaces, recent, LATERAL, SET); csharp-mongo-collection -> nodes 0/2, forbid 0. VERIFIER: fixture baselines re-run on HEAD with the installed wheel (grade.py): go-data-entity-precision nodes 5/6, ACCESSES_DATA 1/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 7; csharp-mongo-collection nodes 0/2, forbid 0 - both match. quokka-stack re-measured with target/debug/glia analyze: 41 DATA_ENTITY, all junk (40 sql:* + graph:Api; graph:Api comes from scripts/generate-repo-map.py itself and disappears when the script is deleted per LG.3e). lapse re-measured: 95 DATA_ENTITY (the draft's 98 was taken on a different dirty-tree state; lapse has uncommitted edits), all 28 DDL tables of the must-keep list present. MISSED BY THE DRAFT: Batch C A13.9 (wave-packets.json, re-verified in rC2) adds parsers/code/extractors/src/migrations.rs whose `extract_sql_migration` calls `data_entities::extract_data_entity_nodes(source, ..)` on a RAW `.sql` migration file - a file with no string literals around its DDL. packets.implementation:
string_literals(source) (~110 LOC): a quote-aware byte scanner that never slices off a char boundary (collect bodies from &source[a..b] only at ASCII delimiter positions). Recognised: `"..."` and `'...'` with backslash escapes (a single-quoted literal must close on the same line, else it is an apostrophe in prose/comments and is dropped), Go/JS/TS backtick literals (JS `${...}` kept as text), triple quotes `"""..."""` / `'''...'''` (Python, Kotlin, Scala, Swift, Java text blocks), C# verbatim `@"..."` (`""` escape), Rust raw `r"..."` / `r#"..."#`, Ruby / PHP heredocs `<<~ID`, `<<-ID`, `<<ID`, `<<<ID`, `<<<'ID'`, `<<<"ID"` up to the line whose trimmed text is `ID` or `ID;`. Skipped as comments: `//` to end of line, `/* ... */`, and `#` to end of line only when `#` is the first non-blank char of the line and is followed by a space (Python/Ruby/shell comments; `#[attr]`, `#include`, `#region` are untouched). The extractor has no language parameter today; this rule set is chosen to be safe across all of them rather than to thread a language through (the engine call site is `run_with_edges!(data_entities::extract_data_entity_nodes(...))` in engine/src/extract.rs, which this packet does not touch).
sql_statements(source): join ADJACENT literals whose gap contains only whitespace / newlines plus at most one concatenation token (`+` Go/Java/JS/C#, `.` PHP, `\\` line continuation; an empty token = Python / C implicit concatenation) - so `"SELECT o.id " +\n "FROM orders o"` stays one statement - then keep a joined literal iff has_sql_statement(lit).
has_sql_statement(lit): trimmed start (after whitespace and `(`) begins, case-insensitively, with one of select / insert into / update / delete from / with / create table / alter table / truncate table / merge into / replace into; `select` also needs ` from `, `update` also needs ` set `; and REJECT a literal containing a Go fmt verb that no SQL driver uses as a placeholder: `%w`, `%q`, `%v` (SQL placeholders are `?`, `$n`, `:name`, `@p`, `%s`, `%(name)s`). Evidence: quokka's only SQL-verb-leading literals are Go error messages, e.g. turps/Services/storage/spaces.go:171 `fmt.Errorf("delete from spaces key=%q: %w", key, err)`.
CTE names: for each statement, collect identifiers matched by `with <ident> as (` and `, <ident> as (` (case-insensitive, recursive allowed) and drop them from that statement's tables.
scan_sql_tables: after capturing an identifier, peek past whitespace - if the next byte is `(`, it is a function call (COALESCE(, jsonb_array_elements(, unnest(, generate_series() -> reject. canonical_sql_name's reject list gains LATERAL, SET, ONLY, VALUES, UNNEST, DUAL, TABLE (TABLE is the keyword A13.9 captures AFTER; it must never be a name).
scan_collection_calls: generalise the needle loop over [".collection(", ".Collection(", ".getCollection(", ".GetCollection(", ".GetCollection<"]; for the `<` form skip a balanced `<...>` then require `(`; argument 1 = first quoted literal before the first `,` or `)`, or `nameof(Ident)` -> Ident; anything else (a variable, an interpolated $"...") -> no node. The existing prev-byte word-boundary rule and is_noise_entity_name apply to every needle.
Debug marker (env-gated like GLIA_QUEUE_DEBUG in queues.rs - a static OnceLock<bool> reading GLIA_DATA_DEBUG once): `[data-entity] literals={l} sql={s} tables={a,b} ctes={c} collections={x} rejected_fn={f} rejected_fmt={g}` per file that produced or rejected anything.
Unit tests in data_entities.rs tests mod (existing tests must stay green unchanged - verify each, especially the `copied from this` / `Array.from(callback)` guard and the raw-SQL users/posts/comments/orders test): go_select_statement_is_not_sql, prose_after_a_real_query_is_not_scanned, concatenated_literals_join, cte_names_are_not_tables, lateral_set_and_functions_are_not_tables, fmt_error_messages_are_not_sql, python_triple_quote_sql, ruby_heredoc_sql, rust_raw_string_sql, go_collection_capital_c, csharp_get_collection_literal_and_nameof, csharp_get_collection_variable_mints_nothing, apostrophe_in_comment_does_not_open_a_literal.

VERIFIER ADDITIONS.
SOURCE OFFSETS. sql_statements returns `SqlStmt { text: String, pieces: Vec<(usize /*source start*/, usize /*text start*/, usize /*len*/)> }`; scan_sql_tables over a statement yields (name, text_pos) and a `to_source(text_pos) -> usize` lookup over `pieces` maps each hit back to its byte offset in the original source (always a char boundary: pieces start and end at ASCII delimiters). Today's extractor output does not carry offsets, so this changes no node or edge; it exists so LE.4a's `AccessSite { offset }` (which re-homes ACCESSES_DATA to the enclosing function by line) keeps working on top of this scanner. LE.4a should list LG.3b in depends_on and consume these offsets (cross-group note).
WHOLE-FILE MODE. `pub fn extract_sql_file_entities(source, module_id, repo) -> DataEntityNodes` shares the emit closure with extract_data_entity_nodes (factor it into a private `fn emit_all(tables: impl Iterator<Item=String>, source, ..)`); it runs scan_sql_tables over the whole file with the CTE / function / LATERAL-SET rejects, then the same ORM / collection / cypher scanners. migrations.rs's extract_sql_migration switches to it - the only caller. If A13.9 has not landed when this packet runs, do NOT create migrations.rs; depends_on A13.9 makes that impossible in the schedule.
Unit tests added: sql_file_mode_scans_raw_ddl (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (...);\nALTER TABLE ONLY orders ADD ...;` -> users, orders), literal_hit_offsets_map_to_source (a two-piece concatenated statement: the offset of `orders` points at `orders` in the source).

packets.implementation:
Schema (LF.2a style, deny_unknown_fields kept): `[[wrapper]] call = "NewCollection"  kind = "data_entity"  flavor = "nosql"  name_arg = 2  origin = "human"`.
Applier (in LF.2e's pass, post-cache, per file containing the needle): reuse LF.2e's hit filtering unchanged (identifier boundary before the needle, commented-line skip, definition-site skip - `func NewCollection[T any](` has `func` before it) and its arg reader `queue_topic::scan(source, needle, TopicRule::ArgIndex(name_arg))`. Needle generalisation: after the call name, if the next byte is `[` or `<`, skip a balanced bracket run (depth counter, max 256 bytes, ASCII only) and then require `(`; LF.2e's http / queue kinds get the same tolerance (a generic HTTP helper `request<T>('GET', '/x')` then matches too). Mint for data_entity: qname `data_entity:<flavor>:<name>` - the SAME shape the cross-cutting extractor uses, so a wrapper hit and an extractor hit collapse onto one node and DbResolver / SHARES_DATA_ENTITY keep working. Name validation: a non-empty string literal of at most 128 bytes with no control characters and no `/` or whitespace; the extractor's noise-word gate (a private fn in parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs) is deliberately NOT applied - the stanza is an explicit human/LLM declaration, and reaching into that file would widen files_touched. Node confidence = origin.confidence() (human Medium, llm Weak), ORIGIN cell Json {"provenance": "overlay:human|overlay:llm", "rule": "wrapper#<n>"}, POSITION via anchor::position_cell; edge ACCESSES_DATA from the ENCLOSING FUNCTION (anchor::build_owner_index + owner_of_line, module id when none) - function-level, better than the extractor's module anchor. Skip if the same qname + owner edge already exists (count duplicate). Non-literal name arg -> skipped_nonliteral.
Marker: LF.2e's line gains a `data_entity=N` count inside its parenthesised kind tally.
Test (engine/tests/overlay_wrappers.rs, new fns): data_entity_wrapper_mints_function_level_access (the fixture shape: chat_previews node, ACCESSES_DATA from NewChatPreviewRepository, ORIGIN overlay:human); generic_brackets_do_not_hide_a_call (`NewCollection[ChatPreview](` and `create<User>(` both match); commented_and_definition_sites_mint_nothing; nonliteral_name_is_skipped (`NewCollection[T](c, d, name)`); missing_name_arg_is_a_config_error.

py/tests/api_surface.rs (~170 LOC): read every `*.rs` under concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src") (sorted; LD.2 may split lib.rs into modules), syn::parse_file each, and collect: (a) `#[pyfunction]` fns -> `fn <name><sig>` where <sig> is the `#[pyo3(signature = (...))]` token text if present else the parameter list minus a leading `py: Python` / `_py`, plus ` -> <return type tokens>` (the return type shows JSON-string vs native, LD.2's concern); `#[pyo3(name = "...")]` renames honoured; (b) `#[pyclass]` structs -> `class <Name>` (+ `#[pyclass(name=...)]`); (c) `#[pymethods] impl T` items -> `  <getter|setter|staticmethod|classmethod|method> <name><sig> -> <ret>`; (d) the `#[pymodule]` fn body -> the set of `wrap_pyfunction!(x, m)` and `add_class::<T>` registrations. Token text normalised: `quote::ToTokens` -> to_string, whitespace collapsed, ` :: ` -> `::`, ` < ` / ` > ` tightened. Render: header line `# repo_graph_py API surface - regenerate: GLIA_UPDATE_SURFACE=1 cargo test -p repo-graph-py --test api_surface`, then module functions sorted, then classes sorted with their members sorted. Assertions: (1) every #[pyfunction] is registered and every registration names an existing #[pyfunction] (`unregistered: [...]` / `dangling: [...]` in the failure message); (2) rendered text == py/api_surface.txt, else fail with a unified-style line diff and the regenerate command; with GLIA_UPDATE_SURFACE=1 write the file and pass. The test binary does not link the cdylib (it only parses source), so the pyo3/extension-module link problem documented in py/src/lib.rs does not apply.
py/check_api_surface.py (~50 LOC, stdlib): import repo_graph_py; for every module function and PyGraph member compare the name set and `__text_signature__` parameter names/defaults against py/api_surface.txt's signature column; print `[api-surface] wheel OK (N functions, M methods)` or each mismatch and exit 1. Run at end-of-wave after the wheel rebuild (harness need for the close-out; not an in-wave gate).
CLI (in cli/src/main.rs's existing tests module, ~70 LOC): walk `<Cli as clap::CommandFactory>::command()` recursively; for every (sub)command path emit `cmd <path>[ hidden]` then one line per argument sorted by id: `  arg <id> long=<l|-> short=<s|-> required=<bool> num_args=<range> default=<values|-> value_names=<..> action=<Set|SetTrue|Append|...> hidden=<bool>`; compare to cli/cli_surface.txt with the same GLIA_UPDATE_SURFACE=1 regenerate path (resolve the file via env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")). Help text is deliberately excluded (doc tweaks are not API).
