packets.title: Capture the pre-leap on-disk artefacts as a committed compat fixture (sharded .ai/repo-graph layout, flat glia build layout, parse cache) before the format bump
packets.rationale: LC.1 bumps FORMAT_VERSION / MANIFEST_VERSION (store/src/lib.rs: FORMAT_VERSION = 1, MANIFEST_VERSION = 1 at HEAD) and must report 'rebuild' for old files; LC.8 makes load_from_gmap self-heal; LC.9 moves the directory. None of that can be tested honestly with a file synthesised by flipping a version byte - users have REAL pre-leap directories on disk: the pyo3/MCP sharded layout at `<repo>/.ai/repo-graph/` (manifest.json schema_version 1 + repo-<id>-NN.gmap shards + cross_stack.gmap + parse_cache.bin) and the flat `glia build` layout at `<repo>/.glia/*.gmap`. Those bytes can only be produced by pre-leap code, and once LC.1 lands nothing in the tree can produce them again; /tmp does not survive a session. So the capture is its own early packet. Gotcha verified: glia's .gitignore ignores `**/.ai/repo-graph/` at any depth, so the layout cannot be committed under that name - it is stored as `layout-ai-repo-graph/` and materialised into a tempdir by the tests (the same trick grade.py's `materialize` uses for `.git`). A dry run of the capture on HEAD (scratch, 3-file go/py/ts repo) produced manifest.json (681 B, build_stamp 0.4.18+p3d23e8828e7ba01a) + 3 shards (2,480 / 800 / 1,216 B) + cross_stack.gmap (176 B). VERIFIER: store/src/lib.rs FORMAT_VERSION = 1 (:45), MANIFEST_VERSION = 1 (:630); only pyo3 writes the sharded layout (py/src/lib.rs:440/:449/:502 write_merged_sharded) and only `glia build` writes the flat one (cli/src/main.rs:1333 write_repo_graph) - re-verified. `git check-ignore -v` confirms `.gitignore:30 **/.ai/repo-graph/` would swallow a fixture dir named .ai/repo-graph, and does not match layout-ai-repo-graph/. WHY THIS PACKET, GIVEN LC.1's OWN FIXTURE: the LC draft's LC.1 captures store/tests/fixtures/gmap-v1 'with the installed wheel (still format 1 at this point)' in LC.1's own wave. LC.1 depends on LC.5a (domain-owned container sections), and the wheel is rebuilt at every close-out, so by LC.1's wave the installed wheel already contains LC.5a's container layout under FORMAT_VERSION 1 - bytes no released glia ever wrote. The only honest capture is pinned to the pre-leap build stamp, in wave 0/1; LC.1 and LC.8 should reuse this fixture instead of capturing their own (cross-group note).

DESIGN. Three ways to build an excluded crate were weighed. (a) In place, `cargo test --manifest-path engram-export/Cargo.toml` - rejected: cargo rewrites the TRACKED engram-export/Cargo.lock whenever resolution changes (it already differs from a fresh resolution at HEAD, and the leap adds crates under engine: tree-sitter-kotlin-ng in A14.2, rayon in LG.1), which dirties the tree and trips closeout's 'uncommitted paths' gate; `--locked` instead fails on every dependency addition anywhere under engine. (b) A Rust test inside the workspace that shells out to cargo - rejected: a nested cargo under `cargo test --workspace` contends for the package-cache lock while packet agents already queue on the target lock. (c) CHOSEN: copy the crate into a fixed build directory inside its own gitignored target, rewrite its path deps to absolute paths, build there. Nothing tracked is written unless --update-lock is passed; the build cache is engram-export/target (.gitignore 'engram-export/target/', 945 MB today), separate from the workspace target, so it never waits on agents' builds.

scripts/check-engram-export.sh (~70 lines, bash, `set -uo pipefail`):
  ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd); ENGRAM="$ROOT/../Engram"; SRC="$ROOT/engram-export/target/check-src"

The GmapDiff doc comment is the apply contract Engram implements (LG.14 hands it over): refuse unless format_version == GMAP_FORMAT_VERSION and base_digest == the digest of the gmap/diff target the store last applied; apply in order (1) modified - find the fact by prior_key (identity_hint as fallback), re-key to node.key, replace content / provenance / hints, keep FactId and salience, classify a retraction only when !location_only; (2) removed; (3) added; (4) edges_removed then edges_added, both keyed by TARGET keys (glia remaps base edge endpoints through the rename map before diffing, so a pure move yields no edge churn); (5) replace the files table; (6) record target_digest. location_only means name, doc, imports, provenance and Proposition text are unchanged - only key / qname / span / concept_hint / identity_hint moved.

The digest is a free function over bytes rather than a Gmap field, so Engram's 19 Gmap literal sites do not move (Engram hashes the bytes it loads). SpanRef gets no Default derive: NONE is explicit. Engram-side workaround: None - full re-seed loses all Path-B learning'; still DEFERRED after v5. The base of the diff is therefore the prior EXPORTED gmap - the one Engram last applied - by G16's own wording. DESIGN CHOICE vs the item text ('built on LE.1 graph delta'): LE.1a / LE.1b (LE draft) compute node / edge deltas between two glia builds keyed by NodeId (HEAD vs working tree, or two DeltaSides of core Node/Edge). The Engram diff is defined over exported facts (after noise filters, doc cleaning, concept / identity hints, NatSpec facts), none of which exist in a glia delta, and its base is generally not HEAD. Diffing the prior exported gmap against the current one is exact for that base, needs no second build, and the base_digest check makes applying to the wrong base impossible. pub struct DiffStats { pub added: usize, pub removed: usize, pub modified: usize, pub moved: usize, pub location_only: usize, pub edges_added: usize, pub edges_removed: usize }
pub fn diff_gmaps(base: &Gmap, base_digest: u64, target: &Gmap, target_digest: u64) -> (GmapDiff, DiffStats);
pub fn read_gmap(path: &Path) -> io::Result<(Gmap, u64)>;           // digest = content_digest(bytes)

read_gmap refuses `format_version != GMAP_FORMAT_VERSION` BEFORE decoding (peek the first 4 bytes, like Engram's persist.rs) with `prior gmap format_version {v} != {GMAP_FORMAT_VERSION}: a --since chain cannot cross a contract bump - run a full export and re-seed Engram`, and maps bincode errors to InvalidData. ALGORITHM (BTreeMap / BTreeSet throughout - no HashMap iteration reaches output):
1. Index base nodes by key. Pass A: every target node whose key exists in base is matched to it. Keys go first because a same-file reorder shifts ordinals: matching hints first would cross-pair swapped siblings.
2. Pass B: among still-unmatched base and target nodes, match on identity_hint when it is Some and unique on both sides - moves and renames.
3. Each match: unchanged when bincode(target node) == bincode(base node); otherwise NodeChange { prior_key: base.key, node: target.clone(), location_only } where location_only = the bincode of both nodes is equal after clearing key, Symbol.qname, Symbol.span / Proposition.span, concept_hint and identity_hint on clones. moved = prior_key != node.key.
4. added = unmatched target nodes in target order; removed = unmatched base keys, sorted.
5. Edges: rename map = {prior_key -> node.key} over the matches; remap base edge endpoints through it; edge identity = (from, kind, to, weight.map(f32::to_bits)); edges_removed = remapped base set - target set, edges_added = target set - remapped base set, both sorted by that identity (EdgeKind is Ord), carrying TARGET keys (a removed node's key stays as in base). A weight change is one removed plus one added.
6. files = target.files.clone(); format_version = GMAP_FORMAT_VERSION; the two digests as given.

WHAT LB.6 PROVIDES (LB draft, graph/src/identity.rs): a DERIVED identity (Identity {kind, basename, local name chain, body hash}) and `detect_moves(prior: &MergedGraph, current: &MergedGraph) -> MoveMap { files: Vec<FileMove { old_path, new_path, tier }>, nodes, rejected }`; it deliberately persists nothing, because history in the graph would break engine/tests/byte_identical.rs. So a move is visible only against a prior MergedGraph. The spec draft assumed LB.6 would persist move state on the incremental build; it does not, so that design is replaced. The repo's own persisted layout is not a usable prior either: install-hooks and the MCP refresh it on every commit, so after `git mv` + commit it already shows the new tree and detect_moves would report nothing. The prior that matches what Engram last applied is the graph the previous export was built from - so each export records it beside its gmap, and `--since <prior>` (the flag G16 already names) reads it back. Using LB.6's Identity::hint() directly as identity_hint was rejected: it embeds the local name chain and a body hash, so every rename and body edit would change the hint and reset reward - losing v3's property that hints survive renames and body edits - and LB.6's own risks note its hints are not unique (two index.ts). SECOND DEFECT, same fixture: when two nodes share a qname the exporter keeps whichever it meets first (seen_keys, :467 / :491). OrderService.validate's ATTRIBUTE twin (the `self.validate` read, no POSITION; listed before the METHOD in g.nodes - verified with the HEAD CLI: kind 35 then kind 4 under one qname) wins, so validate exports with SpanRef {0,0,0}, no doc and identity_hint None (stats: '1 duplicate keys'). quokka-stack: 75 duplicate keys (CLASS/COMPONENT 35, SERVICE/STRUCT 18, CLASS/SERVICE 17, 5 others); LB.3 folds the CLASS + SERVICE/COMPONENT twins at build time, the rest still reach the exporter. The winner fixes the hint's kind component, so it must be deterministic and prefer the located node.

packets.implementation:
(1) HISTORY RECORD. After the gmap is written, the bin persists the glia graph it exported: `repo_graph_engine::persist_result(&result, &history_dir(&out), "glia-export-engram")` (LC.9's single writer - the same layout the MCP reads; quokka-stack's layout is 4.2 MB today). A write failure prints `[engram-export] warning: history not written to <dir>: <e> - the next --since run cannot detect moves` and the exit code stays 0 (the gmap itself is complete). `history_dir(out)` = `<out>.glia`, a directory beside the gmap like the `.files.json` sidecar.
(2) --since <prior.engram-gmap> (a prior FULL v6 export; may equal --out - everything prior is read before anything is written). `let (prior, base_digest) = diff::read_gmap(since)` (LG.8); on Err print `[engram-export] v6 since: refused - <message>` and exit 6. Then `repo_graph_engine::load_layout(&history_dir(since))` (LC.7); on Err (missing dir, or LC.1's needs_rebuild after a glia format change) print `[engram-export] v6 identity: prior graph unavailable at <dir> (<reason>) - moves not detected this run` and continue with no moves - never a hard failure. Moves: `repo_graph_graph::detect_moves(&prior_result.merged, &result.merged).files` -> Vec<(old_path, new_path)> (both tiers; LB.6 already rejects unrelated same-name files). LG.8a later makes --since also write the diff; this packet introduces the flag and the identity chain.
(3) TOKENS. `prior_tokens(prior)`: for every prior node with Some(hint) whose span file id is a key of prior.files, token = the hint minus its trailing `:<kind>:<ordinal>` (split from the right, `hint.rsplitn(3, ':')`, so a path containing ':' survives), keyed by that path; first node in gmap order wins (all nodes of one path carry the same token by construction). `assign_file_identity(current_paths: &BTreeSet<String>, prior: &BTreeMap<String, String>, moves: &[(String, String)]) -> BTreeMap<String, String>`, deterministic in sorted path order: pass 1 (carry) - a current path that is a move's new_path takes prior[old_path] (old_path itself when the prior has no token for it); else a path present in prior keeps prior[path]. Pass 2 (fresh) - every other path takes the path itself if no carried token equals it, else the first free `<path>~1`, `<path>~2`, ... (a file created where a moved file used to live must not share the moved file's token). Without --since the map is empty and every token is the path: v5 hints, the start of a chain. current_paths = position_paths(&result.merged).
(4) HINTS. build_identity_hints(merged, &opts.file_identity): groups in a BTreeMap keyed (token, kind) (the HashMap at :279 goes); ordinal by (start_row, NodeId.0) as today; hint `format!("{token}:{kind}:{ordinal}")`; a path missing from the map uses the path.
(5) DUPLICATE KEYS. A pre-pass over all graphs, applying the same exclude / noise filters as pass 2, keeps per key the winner by max (has POSITION, has DOC cell, Reverse(NodeId.0)) in a BTreeMap<&str, ..>; pass 2 emits a node only if it is its key's winner; stats.duplicate_keys still counts the losers. Edges are unaffected (twins share the qname and edges resolve through qname_of).
(6) MARKER after the 'wrote' line: `[engram-export] v6 identity: {with_hint}/{nodes} hints, {carried} file(s) under a prior identity ({moves} move(s) detected), {dups} duplicate key(s) resolved to the located node` - carried = entries of file_identity whose token != path; moves = the detect_moves file count this run (0 without --since).
(7) DOC. identity_hint doc comment: `<file token>:<kind>:<ordinal>` - the token is the file's path when the chain started, carried across moves by --since; survives renames, body edits and file moves along a --since chain; shifts only when same-kind siblings are reordered within a file (unchanged v3 limitation). Bin doc comment: the run instructions become `bash scripts/check-engram-export.sh` then `engram-export/target/debug/glia-export-engram <repo> --out <file> [--since <prior>]` (`cargo run -p repo-graph-engram-export` from the glia root cannot work for an excluded crate) and document --since and the `<out>.glia` directory.

(b) rename_and_body_edit_keep_hints - rename place -> submit and edit its body in place, export with --since: hints unchanged. (c) duplicate_key_prefers_located_node - hand-built MergedGraph, an ATTRIBUTE node (no cells) and a METHOD node (POSITION + DOC) with one qname, in that Vec order and reversed: the exported node carries the METHOD's span, doc and a Some hint both times. packets.risks: The LB.6 / LC.7 / LC.9 names used here (detect_moves, MoveMap.files, FileMove.old_path / new_path, load_layout, persist_result) come from those groups' drafts: re-read the landed graph/src/identity.rs and engine/src/persist.rs before coding; if LB.6 landed without a file-level move list, derive (old_path, new_path) from its MODULE NodeMoves' POSITION files. LB.6 pairs by content (Identical) and by basename plus half the descendants (SameName, HEURISTIC); a file moved AND renamed AND edited is not paired and starts a new token (documented LB.6 limitation). A deleted symbol plus a new same-kind symbol at the same position shares a hint - the accepted v3 behaviour; Engram's classify_retraction sees the content change. The history directory is a glia layout: if --out is inside the exported repo the next build walks it (walk.rs is_self_output only skips .ai/repo-graph) - tests and docs put --out outside the repo. A --since prior from another repo yields no moves (RepoIds differ after LB.1) and foreign tokens; Engram's base_digest check (LG.8) is the guard against applying such a diff. No HashMap iteration may reach output: tokens, groups and winners are BTreeMaps; detect_moves output is sorted by LB.6. The duplicate-key pre-pass must apply exclude / noise filters first, or a filtered twin could win and then be dropped, losing the key.

packets.title: Scala: top-level classes / objects / traits are package-scoped (<dir>::Type), not file-scoped - no doubled class segment
packets.rationale: The engine hands every parser `module_qname = path_to_qname(path)` (engine/src/extract.rs:307, called by parse_one_with :73) and the Scala parser's visit_top (parsers/code/scala/src/lib.rs:75) passes it as parent_qname to visit_type_def (:117), whose `let qname = format!("{parent_qname}::{name}")` (:132) builds every top-level type qname, so a class named after its file doubles. Measured at HEAD (probe/LB-extra/dbl/scala; re-probed by the verifier on probe/LB-extra/verify/scala with the same result): CLASS `src::main::scala::shop::Widget::Widget`, METHOD `...::Widget::Widget::run`, the companion `object Widget` member `...::Widget::Widget::make`, and a secondary top-level trait `src::main::scala::shop::Widget::Gadget`. A Scala top-level type is a member of its package; two files of one package cannot both declare it (compile error), so scoping by the directory - LB.2's rule for Java, which rejects the declared `package` because two services of one monorepo declare the same package - can never merge distinct types. Scala 3 top-level `def` / `val` are not types, do not double, and a top-level `private def` is file-private: they keep the file scope (measured: FUNCTION `src::shop::Widget::topLevel`). PER-LANGUAGE PROBE at HEAD (debug CLI `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia analyze <dir> --format json`, one language per dir, probe/LB-extra/dbl): Scala `src::main::scala::shop::Widget::Widget::run` DOUBLES (LB.7a); PHP `namespace Shop;` -> `src::Shop::Widget::Widget::run` and namespace-less -> `lib::Widget::Widget::run` DOUBLE, braced `namespace X { }` -> `App::Models::User` (namespace-scoped, its `use` never resolves) (LB.7b); Swift `Sources::Shop::Widget::Widget::run` DOUBLES and a cross-file `extension Widget` mints a second CLASS `Sources::Shop::Widget+Extras::Widget` (LB.7c); C# namespace-less `Svc::Widget::Widget::Run` DOUBLES and so does the C# 10 file-scoped `namespace Shop.Core;` form (`Svc::Widget::Widget::Run` while a PACKAGE `Shop::Core` is emitted), block `namespace Shop.Core { }` -> `Shop::Core::Widget::Run` does not (LB.7d); Solidity `contracts::Token::Token::transfer` doubles literally but is KEPT: a Solidity source unit is its own namespace - solc's fully-qualified name is `contracts/Token.sol:Token`, two files of one directory may legally both declare `contract Token`, and glia's qname is exactly that FQN, so dropping the file segment would merge distinct contracts (the reason TS `src::Widget::Widget`, Python, Dart and Rust keep `<file>::<Type>`). Kotlin `src::shop::Widget::Widget` doubles and is owned by A14.2 (it copies LB.2's recipe). C++ `src::Widget::Widget::run` doubles but is not in this item (see the run's open questions). Ruby / Go / Elixir / Clojure / Python / Dart / Rust / TS do not double. RULE shared by LB.7a-d: drop the file stem only where the language scopes a top-level type by package / namespace / module and forbids two same-named top-level types in that scope, so the change can never merge two distinct declarations; keep the file segment for declarations the language itself makes file-local (Swift private/fileprivate, C# 11 `file`). VERIFIER re-probe (debug CLI at f672dcb, probe/LB-extra/verify/<lang>): Scala CLASS `src::main::scala::shop::Widget::Widget`, METHOD `...::Widget::Widget::make` (companion folded), INTERFACE `...::Widget::Gadget`; Solidity CLASS `contracts::Token::Token`; Kotlin (parsed by the java parser at HEAD, detect_language `kt` -> java) `src::shop::Widget::Widget`; C++ `src::Widget::Widget::run`; TS `src::Widget::Widget::run`; Dart `lib::widget::Widget`, Ruby `app::models::widget::Widget`, Go `shop::widget::Widget`, Python `pkg::widget::Widget`, Rust `src::widget::Widget` - no literal doubling (Ruby and Go carry a lowercase file segment their language does not scope by; that is not the item's doubling and Go resolution is LA.13b's).

packets.title: PHP: top-level classes / interfaces / enums in namespace-less files and under the statement form `namespace X;` are directory-scoped (no doubled class segment); the braced `namespace X { }` form, which does not double, keeps its namespace scope
packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD (debug CLI at f672dcb, probe/LB-extra/dbl/php and the verifier's probe/LB-extra/verify/php): `namespace App\Billing;` (the PSR statement form) -> CLASS `src::Billing::Invoice::Invoice`, METHOD `src::Billing::Invoice::Invoice::total`, INTERFACE `src::Billing::Invoice::Payable`; a namespace-less file -> CLASS `src::Legacy::LegacyThing::LegacyThing`; the braced form `namespace App\Braced { class Report }` -> CLASS `App::Braced::Report` (namespace-scoped, NOT doubled). Cause: visit_children (parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs:89) passes parent_qname to visit_class / visit_interface / visit_enum, whose `format!("{parent_qname}::{name}")` builds the qname; at the root parent_qname is the file module (the statement form's declarations are root siblings of namespace_definition - measured), inside a braced body it is the namespace (visit_namespace :122 walks the body with the namespace qname). DECISION (weighed): (1) statement form and namespace-less -> DIRECTORY scope (LB.2's rule): the namespace (the PHP FQCN) was rejected because Laravel and Symfony put every application under the namespace `App`, so two apps of one monorepo would share every controller NodeId - the `com.example.Application` argument LB.2 uses for Java; PSR-4 makes the directory mirror the namespace anyway (`app/Http/Controllers` <-> `App\Http\Controllers`), and PHP forbids two same-named classes in one namespace, so under PSR-4 the stem drop cannot merge distinct types. (2) The braced form does not double, so it is KEPT (the item: fix the ones that double, keep the ones that do not); moving it to directory scope would also be wrong - the braced form exists to hold SEVERAL namespaces in one file, and directory scope would merge `namespace A { class X }` with `namespace B { class X }` of the same file. The spec draft moved the braced form and fixed its `use` from_module too; both were cut by the verifier as outside the item (the unresolved braced `use` is reported as a gap, with its C# twin). Top-level functions do not double and keep today's scope. See LB.7a for the per-language probe table.

packets.title: C#: file-scoped `namespace X;` types take the namespace scope the block form already has; namespace-less types drop the file stem; C# 11 `file` types and block-namespace types keep today's qname
packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD: namespace-less -> CLASS `Svc::Widget::Widget`, METHOD `Svc::Widget::Widget::Run` (probe/LB-extra/dbl/csnons); the C# 10 file-scoped `namespace Shop.Core;` form ALSO gives `Svc::Widget::Widget::Run` while emitting a PACKAGE `Shop::Core` (dbl/csfs), and the block form `namespace Shop.Core { }` gives `Shop::Core::Widget::Run` (dbl/csns). Cause: visit_namespace (parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs:129) walks the file_scoped_namespace_declaration node itself (:163-164) but tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23 places the declarations that follow it as siblings at compilation_unit level, so visit_children (:94) reaches them with parent_qname = module_qname and visit_type_decl (:170) builds `format!("{parent_qname}::{name}")` (:191). A12.5 (wave-packets.json) measured the same split and recorded that normalising C# type qnames to the namespace form is the prerequisite for its SHARES_SCHEMA unblock; doing it in B means C# identity churns once. DECISION: file-scoped namespace -> namespace scope (it is syntax sugar for the block form, so a repo migrating block -> file-scoped keeps every NodeId, and `resolve_span("Shop.Core.Order.Total")` exact-matches); namespace-less -> directory scope (LB.2's rule; the bare global-namespace name would merge every `class Program` of a monorepo). Why namespace scope here but directory scope for PHP (LB.7b): .NET root namespaces default to the project name (no shared `App` template), block-form namespace qnames are the long-standing C# identity in glia (19 of the 33 committed fixture .cs files use the block form, 12 the file-scoped form, 2 none - verifier count), and .NET directories often do not mirror namespaces (`src/Orders.Api/` vs `Orders.Api`). C# 11 `file` types are file-local by the language: two files of one namespace may each declare `file class Scratch` (distinct today only through the stem, probe csfile) - at the compilation-unit level (namespace-less or after a file-scoped namespace) they keep today's file-scoped qname, since the new scope would otherwise merge them; inside a BLOCK namespace nothing changes (that form does not double; the verifier cut the draft's move of block-namespace `file` types as outside the item). tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23.5's `modifier` rule includes `file` (verified in its grammar.json), and its compilation_unit lists type_declaration beside file_scoped_namespace_declaration, whose only field is `name` (node-types.json) - which is why the declarations after it are root siblings. See LB.7a for the full per-language probe table.

SHARES_SCHEMA must not move for block-form types: nav parents are untouched (xschema-csharp-namespace is the guard). No HashMap iteration added; no byte slicing.

packets.title: Owner segment on channel sides: QUEUE_PRODUCER / QUEUE_CONSUMER, WS_HANDLER / WS_CLIENT, GRAPHQL_RESOLVER / GRAPHQL_OPERATION and GRPC_CLIENT / GRPC_SERVER inside a nested project get ` @<project path>`; the proto GRPC_SERVICE contract stays shared
packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD on a two-projects-per-mechanism monorepo (probe/LB-extra/mono, then the fixture below; `[roots] 11 project roots (go=4 npm=3 python=4)`): services/orders and services/returns both `producer.send("orders.created")` -> ONE QUEUE_PRODUCER `queue_producer:orders.created` with CONTAINS from both files; services/billing and services/audit both consume it -> ONE QUEUE_CONSUMER; one QUEUE_FLOWS edge. services/users and services/catalog both serve NestJS `@Query getUser` -> ONE GRAPHQL_RESOLVER `graphql_resolver:getUser` HANDLED_BY both services' methods (the ROUTE defect LB.4a fixes, in GraphQL). services/gateway and services/admin both build `pb.NewUserServiceClient` -> ONE GRPC_CLIENT `grpc_client:UserService` (USES from both FetchUser). Two gorilla servers -> ONE WS_HANDLER `ws:ws`; web's clients to ws://chat-svc/ws and ws://notify-svc/ws -> ONE WS_CLIENT. `glia arch` therefore prints 4 links (orders -> audit, admin -> proto, web -> catalog, web -> chat) where the tree has 10: engine/src/arch.rs places a node by its first POSITION, so every collapsed side is attributed to one project and the others vanish. Owners are LB.4a's (nested project roots minus LA.5's platform-host shells, owner string = the root's rel path, suffix ` @<owner>`). DECISION PER MECHANISM ("is the channel shared, or is the node a side?"): the CHANNEL - a queue topic, a ws path, a graphql field, a proto service - is genuinely shared, and it stays the pairing key everywhere (resolvers, graph/src/merged.rs channel_of, `glia arch` channel column, `glia contracts` topic). But no node represents the channel: QUEUE_PRODUCER / QUEUE_CONSUMER, WS_HANDLER / WS_CLIENT, GRAPHQL_RESOLVER / GRAPHQL_OPERATION, GRPC_CLIENT and the A5.3 GRPC_SERVER implementation marker are each ONE SIDE of it in one service - the conjugate tier of ROUTE / ENDPOINT, so they take the owner. The proto-declared GRPC_SERVICE (`grpc:<pkg>.<Svc>`) is the contract itself, like MESSAGE_TYPE: vendored copies of one .proto in two projects are one contract, so it stays shared and unowned. Within one project the A2.8 rule stands (one producer node per topic however many files publish, xcut-queue-same-topic-two-files). Real corpus quokka-stack (6 roots) at HEAD: `glia arch` channel rows GRPC_CALLS quokka_android -> turps x2 and WS_CONNECTS quokka_android -> turps x2 - the owner pass must leave both unchanged. The owner rule reproduces what a MULTI-repo build of the same services already gives: generate_many hands each repo its own RepoId, so two services publishing one topic are two QUEUE_PRODUCER NodeIds there; LB.8 makes the monorepo agree. A schema-declared GraphQL field (an SDL `.graphql` file inside a project) is that project's server surface and takes the owner like a code resolver; an SDL file outside every project stays unowned - the rule is by file, structural. Verifier re-measure (2026-09-19, installed wheel = HEAD) on the fixture sketch: grade.py nodes 1/13, edges 0/6, FORBID VIOLATIONS 4; `glia arch` 3 links (services/admin -> (outside projects) GRPC_CALLS UserService, services/orders -> services/audit QUEUE_FLOWS orders.created, web -> services/catalog GRAPHQL_CALLS getUser) and `[queues] resolver paired=1`, `[graphql-resolve] 1 pairs`; quokka-stack `glia arch`: `quokka_android -> turps GRPC_CALLS QuokkaChatService x2` and `WS_CONNECTS ws x2`. neuropil reads these kinds by kind and display name only (layout/tier_stack.rs, render/graph.rs, hud.rs, code_viewer.rs, flow.rs synthesize_step_transforms uses meta.name for QUEUE_CONSUMER) - it parses no channel qname.

packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD (probe/LB-extra/stem2 and the fixture sketch below): api/user.proto + api/user.go -> two MODULE records `api::user` with ONE NodeId (the proto group and the go group are separate RepoGraphs, so the merged graph holds two nodes per id); docs/swagger.yaml + docs/swagger.json -> `docs::swagger` twice; svc/Dockerfile + svc/Dockerfile.prod -> ONE `svc::Dockerfile` (path_to_qname drops `.prod`) with every DEFINES_CONFIG / DEFINES edge doubled; `.env.example` -> MODULE `.env`. Real corpus grpc-go at HEAD: MODULE `reflection::test::grpc_testing_not_regenerate::dynamic` and `::testv3` appear twice each (.go + .proto) - 4 of the 10 duplicate-id records in `glia analyze --format json` (the other 6 are shared CONFIG_KEYs, by design); turps holds docs/swagger.json + docs/swagger.yaml. Cause: every non-code branch of parse_repo_files (engine/src/route.rs:27 - yaml :79, Dockerfile :122, manifest :151, dotenv :177, json :210, proto :239, graphql :289, avro :329) and stash_synthetic_parse (:501, qname :526) key the MODULE on path_to_qname (engine/src/extract.rs:307), which drops the last extension, while stash_synthetic_parse already records the display NAME as the full file name (`user.proto`). A non-code MODULE's children are never path-qualified (grpc:, message:, config:, infra:, contract::, graphql_resolver:, cron:, data_entity: qnames) and nothing imports a non-code module by qname, so naming it by the full file name is a structural rule (no dependence on siblings) that changes zero code qnames and removes the non-code half of LB.9's collision class - cross-group (the grpc-go case) and within-format (Dockerfile / .env variants, x.yml + x.yaml). packets.title: UTF-8 window cuts in the cross-cutting extractors: the fixed 256-byte windows in data_entities.rs (Cypher, Beanie) and cron.rs (node-cron, Celery x2) snap to char boundaries, a pipeline multibyte sweep guards the class, and `glia analyze` names every file that still fails
packets.rationale:
Reproduced on HEAD f672dcb with `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia analyze .` on glia: the summary prints `- parse errors: 1`, stderr names nothing, and `--format json` has 0 nodes under `parsers::code::extractors::src::config` (data_entities.rs, beside it, has 20). repo-graph MCP `find scan_python_env` returns no node: the whole file (51 fns) is missing from the graph glia builds of itself.
The item names config.rs as the site; config.rs is the VICTIM. The panicking code is parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs scan_cypher_labels: find_keyword_ci matches MATCH/MERGE/CREATE in any case (per-byte upper-or-lower), so config.rs's Rust `match t.find(" #") {` at byte 11127 opens a Cypher window `&source[pos..(pos + 256).min(len)]`, and 11127 + 256 = 11383 lands inside '≤' (bytes 11382..11385, the doc comment of is_valid_env_name). LC.7's spec recorded the same message from the wheel: `parsers/code/extractors/src/config.rs: PANIC (rust parser/extractors): end byte index 11383 is not a char boundary`. Delta-debugged (line level, then char level) to a 257-byte snippet with `match` at 0 and '≤' at 254; saved as a.rs, config.rs, x.py, x.ts or x.go it always reports 1 parse error; with 'abc' in place of '≤' it reports 0.
The class, measured on HEAD with the debug CLI: a sweep of the extractor needles x {needle+pad+char, char+pad+needle} x pad 0..520 x {.ts, .py} (118,788 files) fails at exactly these sites, each at exactly the 2 pads where the cut lands inside the 3-byte char, and every other needle reports 0: data_entities::scan_cypher_labels (`MATCH (p:Person) `, `merge `, `create `, `match x `), data_entities::scan_beanie_documents (`class Settings:`, window from the needle END), cron::extract_node_cron (`cronTime:`), cron::extract_celery_beat (`'schedule':` and `"schedule":`, a 256-byte look-back, two copies of the code). A reduced sweep with a 4-byte char (U+1F600) over only the pads that put a 32/64/128/256/512 window cut inside the char (6,392 files, one tree) reports 48 parse errors = those 8 needles x 2 extensions x 3 interior offsets. A per-language sweep (rs, go, java, rb, php, cs, swift, scala, dart, ex, clj, sol, tf, c) adds only the Rust parser's `.at(` / `Router::with_path(` verb window (LA.25b) and the Clojure reitit look-back (already owned by LA.22c).
Per-file isolation (engine/src/route.rs parse_repo_files catch_unwind under build.rs SuppressPanicHook) swallows the message: `glia analyze` shows only a count in the summary table and nothing under --format json / mermaid, which is why this one needed a delta-debug harness to locate.
VERIFIER RE-MEASURED ON HEAD f672dcb (debug CLI, GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1): the self-build summary prints `- parse errors: 1` and stderr names no file; `--format json` has 0 nodes with qname prefix parsers::code::extractors::src::config (data_entities.rs beside it has 20); repo-graph MCP `find scan_python_env` -> no match. In config.rs the only case-insensitive MATCH/MERGE/CREATE + whitespace whose +256 cut lands on a continuation byte is `match ` at byte 11127 (cut 11383; '≤' occupies 11382..11385). One file per site, each with a 4-byte char placed so the cut lands on its 2nd byte, gives exactly 1 parse error each: Cypher (`MATCH (p:Person) `, window from the needle start), Beanie (`class Settings:`, window from the needle end), node-cron (`cronTime: '* * * * *', `), Celery single- and double-quoted look-back; a 300-byte ASCII control gives 0. The 54-needle sweep tree described below (6,392 files) reproduces 48 parse errors and takes 3.1 s through the debug CLI. The config.rs-shaped regression file below gives 1 parse error and ZERO nodes (not even its MODULE).

packets.implementation:
CONTEXT, computed once per call: `#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)] struct GqlContext { client_import: bool, graphql_request: bool, gql_tag: bool, tanstack: bool }`.
  client_import - the file names a GraphQL client package as a quoted module string: a `'` or `"` immediately followed by one of @apollo/client, apollo-client, @apollo/react-hooks, react-apollo, apollo-angular, @vue/apollo-composable, urql, @urql/, graphql-hooks, react-relay, relay-runtime, graphql-tag, graphql-request, and then `'`, `"` or `/` (so 'urql' and '@urql/core' match, 'urql-x' does not).
  graphql_request - the quoted module graphql-request, or the identifier `GraphQLClient` followed by `(` (the client object).
  gql_tag - "gql`", "graphql`", "gql(", "graphql(" preceded by a non-identifier byte (the same tags extract_gql_operation_name reads).
  tanstack - a quoted module starting @tanstack/ or equal to react-query, vue-query, svelte-query.
ARGUMENT SHAPE, read from the SOURCE after the needle's `(` (so a multi-line call works), over at most 512 bytes via as_bytes() - it never slices a str: skip ASCII whitespace and newlines; `{` -> read the first key after `{` + whitespace; QueryObject iff the key is query / mutation / subscription / document and the next non-space byte is `:`, `,` or `}` (shorthand), else OtherObject; [A-Za-z_$] -> Ident (covers GET_USERS, GetUsersDocument, query, an inline gql`...` tag); quote / backtick -> Str; `[` -> Array; `)` -> Empty; else Other.
ACCEPT:
  Hook (useQuery( useMutation( useSubscription( useLazyQuery():  (Ident | QueryObject) && !(ctx.tanstack && !ctx.client_import). Kept: Apollo useQuery(GET_USERS), urql useQuery({ query: Q }), useQuery(gql`...`). Dropped: TanStack useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn }), useQuery(['k'], fn), useQuery('k', fn), useQuery(options) in a TanStack file.
  ClientMethod (client.query( client.mutate( client.subscribe():  QueryObject || (Ident && (ctx.client_import || ctx.gql_tag)). Kept: Apollo client.query({ query }) / client.mutate({ mutation }), urql client.query(Q, vars) with its import. Dropped: mqtt client.subscribe('t'), pg client.query('SELECT ...'), client.query(sql, params), client.query({ text, values }).
  Request (request():  ctx.graphql_request && the byte before `request` is not an identifier byte [A-Za-z0-9_$]. Kept: `request(endpoint, Q)` and `client.request(Q)` in a graphql-request file. Dropped: Guzzle ->request(, requests.request(, ureq .request(, handle_request(, _request( in any file without graphql-request context.

A Rust `match x {` is a Cypher MATCH to it, and `(merged::pick_primary(a, b))` inside the match arm yields the label pick_primary (the first `:` of `::` reads nothing, the second reads the segment).
Measured on HEAD, debug CLI --format json, DATA_ENTITY with qname prefix data_entity:graph: - glia self-build 91 (graph:pick_primary, graph:CLASS / FUNCTION / MODULE from `(node_kind::CLASS)`, graph:Label from a doc comment quoting `MATCH (x:Label)`, ...), neuropil 98, Engram 16, repo-graph 1 (graph:id), quokka-stack 1 (graph:Api, from a Python `for match in ...` in scripts/generate-repo-map.py). None of these repos holds a Cypher query.
Probe (one .py file): SQL `"MERGE INTO t USING s ON (t.id = :id) ..."` -> graph:id; `"MATCH (u:User {active:true}) RETURN u"` -> graph:User AND graph:true; the comment `# create a user (id:abc) here` -> graph:abc.
New fixture cypher-label-precision graded on HEAD (installed wheel): nodes 2/2 (neo4j driver controls Person, Company), FORBID VIOLATIONS 3 (graph:CLASS, graph:pick_primary, graph:Label).
The 256-byte window is also LA.25's panic site (LA.25a makes it char-safe; this packet removes it). LG.3b adds exactly the machinery a literal-scoped scan needs to data_entities.rs - string_literals(source) (quote / triple / raw / heredoc aware, comments skipped) and the concatenation join (SqlStmt { text, pieces } + to_source offsets) - but applies it to SQL only and leaves scan_cypher_labels as it is.
VERIFIER RE-MEASURED ON HEAD (debug CLI json): data_entity:graph:* count glia 91 (includes CLASS, FUNCTION, MODULE, pick_primary, Label, as_str, to_string, extract_grpc_server_nodes ...), neuropil 98, Engram 16, repo-graph 1, quokka-stack 1, lapse 0; one .py probe reproduces graph:id (SQL MERGE INTO), graph:true (property map) and graph:abc (comment); grade.py on the draft fixture: nodes 2/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 3. No Cypher-shaped literal exists in neuropil, Engram, repo-graph, quokka-stack or lapse (git grep for a quote followed by MATCH/MERGE/CREATE + `(`: the only quokka hits are node_modules markdown and an Angular `(click)="create()"`). packets.implementation:
Build on LG.3b's literal machinery in the same file (depends_on LG.3b).
(1) Factor LG.3b's concatenation-join step out of sql_statements into `fn joined_literals(source: &str) -> Vec<SqlStmt>` (adjacent literals joined across whitespace + at most one concatenation token, with their pieces); sql_statements becomes `joined_literals(source).into_iter().filter(|s| has_sql_statement(&s.text))` - SQL output unchanged (LG.3b's tests are the guard).
(2) `fn is_cypher_statement(text: &str) -> bool`, ASCII case-insensitive on the trimmed start (whitespace and `(` skipped): MATCH / OPTIONAL MATCH / MERGE / CREATE qualify only when followed by whitespace and then `(` or `<ident> =` (a path variable) - which rejects CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, SQL MERGE INTO and a bare `create()` call; UNWIND / WITH / CALL / USE qualify only when the statement also holds a word-bounded MATCH / MERGE / CREATE followed by whitespace and `(`.
(3) `fn scan_cypher_labels(source: &str) -> Vec<String>` keeps its HEAD signature: for each joined literal that is_cypher_statement, run extract_node_labels over the WHOLE statement text and push the labels in statement order, then label order (no HashMap iteration). find_keyword_ci stays (scan_sql_tables uses it). Offsets and the MATCH->Read / MERGE,CREATE->Write verb are NOT added here: that is LE.4a's contract (its entry point already says scan_cypher_labels gains offset + verb), and LE.4a lands after this packet and builds its Cypher AccessSite on this literal-scoped scanner with LG.3b's `to_source` piece map.
(4) `fn extract_node_labels(text: &str) -> Vec<String>` (the renamed window scanner, same `(`...`)` walk, bytes only - labels are sliced at ASCII delimiters): inside a node pattern labels are read only before the first `{` (the property map: `{active:true}` holds values, not labels); a `:` next to another `:` (`::` - Rust / C++ / PHP / Ruby paths, Cypher 5 type predicates) is skipped whole; relationship types in `[...]` stay ignored as today.
(5) qnames stay data_entity:graph:<label>; is_noise_entity_name still applies.
(6) MARKER under LG.3b's GLIA_DATA_DEBUG switch: per file with a Cypher statement or a rejected keyword hit, `[data-entity] cypher statements={s} labels={a,b} rejected_outside_literal={k}` where k counts MATCH / MERGE / CREATE hits of find_keyword_ci that fall outside every Cypher statement (HEAD's scanner input that no longer counts).
TESTS (data_entities.rs). Unchanged and green: cypher_match_merge_labels (its statements are JS string literals: Person, User, Account, Wallet), LA.25a's cypher_window_cut_inside_a_multibyte_char (a literal). New: rust_match_over_paths_is_not_cypher (`match kind { k if k == (node_kind::CLASS) => a, _ => (merged::pick_primary(a, b)) }` -> no graph:*), cypher_in_a_comment_is_not_a_label (`// the Cypher form MATCH (x:Label)` and `# MERGE (n:Node)` -> none), lowercase_prose_create_is_not_cypher (`// create a user (id:abc) here` -> none), sql_merge_into_is_not_cypher (`"MERGE INTO t USING s ON (t.id = :id) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET x = 1"` -> no graph:id), property_map_values_are_not_labels (`"MATCH (u:User {active:true}) RETURN u"` -> graph:User only), java_spring_data_query_annotation (`@Query("MATCH (m:Movie)<-[:ACTED_IN]-(p:Person) RETURN m")` -> Movie, Person; ACTED_IN is a relationship type), concatenated_cypher_statement (`"MATCH " + "(o:Order) RETURN o"` -> Order; Python implicit concatenation `"MERGE (c:Company {id: $id}) "\n"RETURN c"` -> Company).

Duplicate on the same call, probed on HEAD: NestJS CQRS `this.eventBus.publish(new OrderPlaced(id))` in a file without a broker import mints event_emit:OrderPlaced (type pass, correct) AND event_emit:publish (string pass fallback).

packets.implementation:
One gate for the two broker-ambiguous verbs that name a pub/sub channel: `publish(` (emitter) and `.subscribe(` (handler). `.on(`, `.emit(`, `.dispatch(`, `.trigger(`, `dispatchEvent(`, `.addEventListener(`, `@OnEvent(` etc. are untouched.
(1) `fn find_gated(source: &str, pattern: &str, ctx: &mut VerbCtx) -> Option<usize>` walks every occurrence in order (HEAD already walks them, but only to skip QUEUE_OWNED_PUBLISH) and returns the first that: (a) is not queue-owned (unchanged); (b) is not a TYPE site - the first token after `(` and whitespace is `new ` (the type pass already minted the typed event; removes the duplicate event_emit:publish); (c) is not a declaration; (d) has bus evidence. For any other needle it returns the first occurrence as today.
(2) DECLARATION (a bare `publish(` only; a dotted `x.publish(` / `x.subscribe(` is always a call). PREFIX = the bytes from the previous `\n` to the needle, trailing whitespace trimmed; LAST = its last whitespace-separated word. `after_paren` = the text after the balanced `)` of the argument list, skipping whitespace and identifier / `,` / `.` runs (Java `throws A, B`, Dart `async`, C++ `const noexcept`). A bare occurrence is a declaration iff one of:
   (i) KEYWORD: LAST is `def`, `defp`, `fn`, `fun`, `func` or `function` (covers `pub fn`, `async def`, `export function`, PHP `public function`, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Ruby, Elixir), or PREFIX starts with `func` and ends with `)` (Go method receiver `func (n *Notifier)`);
   (ii) TYPED (C-family): LAST is an identifier or ends with `>`, `]` or `?` (a type: `void`, `Task`, `Future<void>`, `String[]`), LAST is not a call word {return, await, yield, new, throw, else, do, then, case, in, not, and, or, if, elif, while, for, print, echo, puts, typeof}, and after_paren starts with `{`, `;` (interface / abstract) or `=>` (C# expression body);
   (iii) METHOD (JS / TS class member): PREFIX is empty or only modifier words {async, static, public, private, protected, override, readonly, abstract, get, set, export, default} and `*`, and after_paren starts with `{` or `:` (a TS return annotation).
   Anything else is a CALL: `publish('x', y);`, `return publish(x)`, `const r = publish(x)`, `if (publish(x))`, Python `if publish(x):` (LAST `if` is a call word, and (iii) needs an empty prefix).
(3) BUS EVIDENCE. RECEIVER: for a dotted occurrence, the identifier right before the `.` (a trailing `(...)` call is skipped, so `vertx.eventBus().publish` reads eventBus), lowercased with leading `_`, `$`, `@` stripped, ends with one of bus, pubsub, emitter, events, mediator, publisher, notifications. IMPORT: the lowercased file names an in-process pub/sub library - graphql-subscriptions, pubsub-js, @nestjs/cqrs, wisper. VerbCtx holds the lazily built lowercase copy (the one BrokerGate already makes - shared, built at most once per call) and the cached import flag. A bare occurrence needs IMPORT (Wisper's `publish('order_placed', self)` inside the publisher); a dotted one needs RECEIVER or IMPORT (`const ps = new PubSub(); ps.publish('X')`).
(4) Broker suppression (A2.9, BrokerGate::present) runs after the gate exactly as today - a GCP `publisher.publish(...)` passes the receiver rule and is then suppressed by its google.cloud import.
(5) AWS SDK v3: scan_type_needles skips the `.send(new ` needle when the source contains `@aws-sdk/` (the v3 command pattern `client.send(new XCommand(..))`; queues.rs and data_entities.rs own SQS / SNS / DynamoDB). MediatR's `.Send(new ` (C# casing) is a different needle and unaffected; a lowercase mediator in a file that also imports the AWS SDK loses its typed event (accepted, rare).
(6) MARKER: `fn event_debug() -> bool` (OnceLock, GLIA_EVENT_DEBUG non-empty and != "0", the queues.rs debug_enabled pattern). When set, per file with a gated-needle hit: `[eventbus] verb-gate needle='publish(' kept={0|1} rejected decl={d} no_bus={b} type_site={t}` (no_bus = a call with neither a bus-shaped receiver nor a pub/sub import) (and the same line for '.subscribe('), plus `[eventbus] aws-sdk command skipped type={T}` for each skipped type site. The existing `[queues] broker-event suppressed` line is unchanged.
All reads are byte walks around ASCII anchors (the previous `\n`, the `.`, the balanced `)`); the receiver identifier is read backwards over [A-Za-z0-9_$] bytes only, so every slice starts and ends on a char boundary.
TESTS (eventbus.rs). Every existing test stays green unchanged - checked against the gate: bus.publish / pubsub.publish / bus.subscribe keep their names (bus-shaped receivers), nc.publish stays queue-owned, the broker-suppression shapes stay empty (mqtt `client.publish` and kafkajs `consumer.subscribe` fail the receiver rule, Spring `public void publish(String p)` is a declaration, `sns.publish` fails the receiver rule, GCP `publisher.publish` passes it and is suppressed), `this.eventBus.publish(new OrderPlaced(id))` with kafkajs stays ["event_emit:OrderPlaced"]. New: a_function_named_publish_is_not_an_emitter (Python `def publish(self, m)` / `def publish(report)` / `notifier.publish(x)`, JS `function publish(msg) {}`, TS method `publish(msg: string): void {`, Go `func (n *Notifier) publish(m string) {`, Rust `fn publish(&self)` -> emitted() == []); first_qualifying_publish_wins (`def publish(self, m): pass\nbus.publish('user.created', u)` -> ["event_emit:user.created"], HEAD ["event_emit:publish"]); bus_shaped_receivers_still_emit (this.eventBus.publish('x'), vertx.eventBus().publish("addr", m), ActiveSupport::Notifications.publish('render', p), this.events.publish('user:login', u)); import_admits_other_receivers (graphql-subscriptions `ps.publish('POST_ADDED', p)`; Wisper bare `publish('order_placed', self)`); typed_publish_mints_no_fallback (`this.eventBus.publish(new OrderPlaced(id))`, no broker import -> ["event_emit:OrderPlaced"], HEAD adds event_emit:publish); rxjs_subscribe_is_not_a_handler (`this.route.params.subscribe(p => ...)`, `obs$.subscribe(x)`, `this.http.get(u).subscribe(r => {})` -> handled() == []); bus_subscribe_still_handles (`PubSub.subscribe('MY TOPIC', fn)`, `pubsub.subscribe('POST_ADDED', h)`); aws_sdk_commands_are_not_events (`import { DynamoDBClient, PutItemCommand } from '@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb';\nawait ddb.send(new PutItemCommand({ TableName: 'orders' }));` -> [], and MediatR `_mediator.Send(new CreateOrder(id));` -> ["event_emit:CreateOrder"]); calls_in_conditions_are_not_declarations (`import PubSub from 'pubsub-js';\nif (publish('x', data)) {}` and a Wisper `return publish('order_placed', self)` -> ["event_emit:x"] / ["event_emit:order_placed"]; Java interface `void publish(String p);` and Dart `Future<void> publish(String m) async {` with a pubsub-js-style import -> []).

packets.rationale: Every language parser that emits ENUM with METHOD children is blind to calls into those methods, because the generic resolver treats only CLASS / STRUCT as a method-owning type. graph/src/calls.rs enclosing_class_or_struct accepts CLASS | STRUCT only, graph/src/build.rs build_symbol_table indexes METHOD children into class_methods only for CLASS | STRUCT parents, and resolve_attribute_target resolves a bound base only when its kind is MODULE / PACKAGE / CLASS / STRUCT. Measured on HEAD f672dcb (code 5280cee) with the debug CLI and grade.py on the probe fixture below (a Rust enum `impl Tier { fn rank(&self) { self.weight() } }` beside the same shape on a struct): CALLS 1/2 - `Ledger::total -> Ledger::weight` resolves, `Tier::rank -> Tier::weight` does not. The same holds for Swift (probe/LA-cov3/enumothers: `enum Shape { func area() { self.side() } }` emits ENUM + 3 METHODs, 0 CALLS; Swift additionally has an unrelated `.suffix` defect, reported as a gap). The Java and TypeScript enum packets (LA.30b, LA.30c) need this to resolve `Color.pick()` through an import and `this.helper()` inside an enum body, and they emit enum-member USES refs `Attribute{base: <enum>, name: <member>}` that nothing can bind today: resolve_refs' Attribute arm only looks up MODULE symbols and CLASS methods. graph queries: `impact graph::src::calls::enclosing_class_or_struct` backward -> resolve_calls and the five build_* entry points (every language); `impact graph::src::build::build_symbol_table` backward -> build_typescript / build_dotted / build_go / build_python / build_ruby. LA.3 (Rust) adds an ENUM branch to its own Rust hook for the same self-call; making the generic resolver ENUM-aware first means LA.3's hook only has to handle what is genuinely Rust-specific (impl blocks in another file) - see deps_on_existing. VERIFIER (re-measured on HEAD f672dcb): grade.py on this exact fixture reproduces `XX CALLS 'src/lib/Tier/rank' -> 'src/lib/Tier/weight'`, `OK CALLS 'src/lib/Ledger/total' -> 'src/lib/Ledger/weight'`, CALLS 1/2. The 'only HEAD misses can change' claim was checked parser by parser: the kinds that emit METHOD children under an ENUM at HEAD are Rust (same-file `impl Enum`) and Swift; C# / C++ / Solidity / PHP / Dart enums have no methods and the Java / TS enum bodies are not walked until LA.30b / LA.30c. Swift SelfMethod never resolves on HEAD (verifier probe probe/LA-cov3-verify/swiftnest: `class Outer { enum Inner { func f() { self.g() } } func g() {} func k() { self.g() } }` gives 0 CALLS, not even k -> g, because of the `.suffix` defect), so the one case where the HEAD walk passes THROUGH an ENUM to an outer CLASS (a nested Swift enum) resolves nothing today and cannot lose an edge. LA.3 (risk 6) chose not to widen enclosing_class_or_struct; this packet widens it for ENUM only, because Java has no language hook and its enum-body self-calls need the generic walk, and LA.1a's RustIndex already treats ENUM METHOD children as members for path calls - so the generic and the Rust rules agree. packets.implementation:
parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs (~190 LOC + ~110 test LOC):
1. REFACTOR: the match body of visit_type_decl's member loop (constructor_declaration / method_declaration / field_declaration / nested types) moves verbatim into `fn visit_type_member(child, src, file_rel, owner_qname, owner_id, module_id, repo, class_prefix, is_bean, enum_ctx, acc) -> usize` (returns the composed-route count the loop sums today). Class bodies call it per child exactly as before (byte-identical output for classes, interfaces and records).
2. ENUM BODY: when `node.kind() == "enum_declaration"`, the loop over `body.named_children` handles `enum_constant` -> visit_enum_constant and `enum_body_declarations` -> visit_type_member for each of ITS named children with enum_ctx = Some(enum qname). Constructors, methods and fields are therefore emitted exactly like a class's (METHOD / STATE_VAR / DEFINES / nav parent = the ENUM).
3. `fn visit_enum_constant(node, src, file_rel, enum_qname, enum_id, repo, acc)`: name = field `name`; qname `{enum_qname}::{NAME}`; ATTRIBUTE node (id via NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, ATTRIBUTE, qname), cells = entity_cells(&node) = CODE + POSITION + DOC, Confidence::Strong); Edge ENUM -HAS_ATTRIBUTE-> constant (Strong); nav.record(id, NAME, qname, ATTRIBUTE, Some(enum_id)); `acc.enum_consts[enum_qname].insert(NAME, id)`. If the constant has a `body` (class_body): each method_declaration in it -> visit_method(child, .., parent_qname = constant qname, parent_id = constant id, class_prefix "", enum_ctx = Some(enum qname)) - METHOD `{enum}::{NAME}::{m}`, DEFINES constant -> method. The enum_constant `arguments` are not calls into the constructor (no CALLS emitted).
4. MEMBER REFERENCES (collect_calls_in, per method body; `struct MemberRef { from: NodeId, base: Option<String>, name: String, enum_ctx: Option<String> }` pushed to `acc.member_refs`, deduped per (from, base, name)): (a) `field_access` whose `object` is an identifier X and whose `field` is an identifier Y starting with an ASCII uppercase letter -> MemberRef{base: Some(X), name: Y}; (b) inside an enum (enum_ctx is Some), an `identifier` whose text is one of that enum's constants (acc.enum_consts is filled before the enum's methods are walked, because constants precede enum_body_declarations in the grammar) and that is in value position -> MemberRef{base: None}. Value position = the parent is not a declaration name (variable_declarator.name, formal_parameter, catch_formal_parameter, enhanced_for_statement.name, lambda parameters), not a method_invocation `name` / `object`-less invocation, not the `field` of a field_access, not a labeled_statement label; switch_label identifiers (`case RED:`) ARE value position. A local declared in the same body with the same name (collected in one pre-walk of the body) suppresses (b).
5. RESOLUTION at the end of parse_file (after every type is visited, so a reference to an enum declared later in the file resolves): base None -> acc.enum_consts[enum_ctx][name] -> Edge from -USES-> constant (Strong); base Some(X) with X the simple name of exactly one enum declared in this file -> that enum's constant, direct USES edge; base Some(X) with X a single-type-import simple name of this file (ImportTarget::Symbol name, collected from acc.imports) -> UnresolvedRef{from, from_module: module_id, qualifier: Attribute{base: X, name}, category: USES} (LA.30a binds it when X resolves to an ENUM; a CLASS base stays in unresolved_refs); anything else is dropped (keeps `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, `HttpStatus.OK` from an unimported / wildcard-imported type out of the persisted unresolved_refs).
6. MARKER (per file, printed when the file declares an enum or produced a member reference; the [java-routes] per-file precedent): `[java-enums] enums=E constants=C methods=M const_bodies=B member_uses=U member_refs=R file=<file_rel>` (U = direct USES edges, R = UnresolvedRefs).
TESTS (parsers/code/java/src/lib.rs mod tests, module qnames engine-realistic per LB.2): enum_constants_are_attributes (3 ATTRIBUTE + 3 HAS_ATTRIBUTE, qnames `<scope>::Color::RED` ..); enum_body_declarations_are_walked (METHODs label / pick / warm / isRed, constructor METHOD `Color`, STATE_VAR for a documented `static final`); constant_body_methods_hang_off_the_constant (METHOD `..::Color::GREEN::label`, parent ATTRIBUTE GREEN, DEFINES GREEN -> label, NOT a child of the ENUM); bare_constant_reference_is_a_uses_edge (pick -> RED, isRed -> RED, a `switch (this) { case BLUE: }` label -> BLUE); local_named_like_a_constant_is_not_a_reference; qualified_reference_to_imported_enum_is_a_uses_ref (Picker.green -> UnresolvedRef Attribute{Color, GREEN} USES); qualified_reference_to_same_file_enum_is_a_direct_edge; unimported_uppercase_field_access_emits_nothing (`Integer.MAX_VALUE`); interfaces_and_enums keeps ENUM == 1 and gains ATTRIBUTE == 3. engine/tests/java_enum_members.rs: generate_one over the fixture - every expect row by qname (incl. warm -> isRed CALLS and Picker.choose -> Color.pick CALLS, both through LA.30a) and both forbids absent.
EVIDENCE (LC.3): edges pushed inside the parse (DEFINES / HAS_ATTRIBUTE / in-file USES / direct HANDLED_BY from this packet) are attributed by LC.3a's stage stamp (`stamp_missing(.., "parser:<lang>")` in engine/src/route.rs, `extractor:<name>` in engine/src/extract.rs) in either landing order; if code_domain::evidence already exists, a parser-pushed edge with a site also gets `Evidence::emitter("parser:<lang>").rule("intra_file").line(row)` (LC.3b's rule for parser-pushed CALLS). Edges resolved from the CallSites / UnresolvedRefs this packet emits are pushed by graph resolve_calls / resolve_refs and carry LC.3d's branch rule. If LC.3b has landed when this packet starts, CallSite / UnresolvedRef have a non-Option `line` and the compiler lists every new construction site: fill it with the 0-based start row of the call / reference. Preferred order: this packet before LC.3a, LC.3b and LC.3d, so their sweeps and rule tables see the new sites (deps_on_existing).

DESIGN (weighed): (a) pass `path` into the tRPC extractor and write POSITION cells there - REJECTED: it would duplicate what anchor::attach already does for every other RPC-family marker and still leave the nodes edge-less; (b) CHOSEN: report anchors and let anchor::attach place them, like gRPC clients. RPC_CALL is outbound (the calling function USES it, the gRPC-client shape); RPC_PROCEDURE is inbound (HANDLED_BY the function whose span holds the procedure key, the GRPC_SERVER / GRAPHQL_RESOLVER shape). A T3 router declared at module level has no enclosing function, so its procedures get the module CONTAINS fallback (structural, not a blast carry edge) plus the POSITION cell - which is what makes them locatable. LA.17's Connect / Twirp nodes are grafted post-cache with their own edges and never pass through attach; with these kinds now marker kinds the `[marker-anchor]` census counts them too (they are owner-linked or module-linked, so they classify correctly).
trpc.rs (~80 LOC): `Scan::text_mapped(&self, s, e, map: &[usize]) -> (String, Vec<usize>)` = text() plus, per kept byte, its offset in the ORIGINAL source (map[i] for body byte i), trimmed in step. parse_router_body(body, map, prefix, decl, depth): the top call passes `&source[open+1..close]` with map = (open+1..close).collect(); per entry `(entry, emap) = scan.text_mapped(s, e, map)`; key offset = emap[0]; value = the &str split_key returns (a subslice of entry, so its start is `value.as_ptr() as usize - entry.as_ptr() as usize`); a nested inline router recurses on `&value[open+1..close]` with the matching emap slice - offsets survive comment stripping and nesting. procedures.push((path, key_offset)). extract_trpc_procedure_nodes: for every emitted (prefix, path, off) push `Anchor { node: id, line: anchor::line_of(source, off) }` (a mounted router's procedures anchor at their own declaration). scan_client_calls -> Vec<(String, usize)> (offset = the root identifier's first byte); extract_trpc_call_nodes keeps one node per distinct path and pushes an Anchor for EVERY site (the gRPC-client density rule: each calling function gets its USES edge); is_trpc_client_line uses `!scan_client_calls(line).is_empty()` unchanged in meaning.
anchor.rs (~6 LOC + doc): OUTBOUND += node_kind::RPC_CALL, INBOUND += node_kind::RPC_PROCEDURE; header lists tRPC. extract.rs (~6 LOC): `run_marked!(procs); run_marked!(calls);` (if LC.3a has landed, its named-macro form, name "trpc"); the `[trpc]` line becomes `[trpc] routers=R procedures=P calls=C anchors=A path=<path>` (A = procs.anchors.len() + calls.anchors.len(), read before the macros move them).

packets.rationale: Measured on HEAD f672dcb. (1) POSITION: parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs emit_route_from_call pushes each ROUTE with a single JSON ROUTE_METHOD cell and no POSITION. Dump of the fixture below through grade.py's build_graph: route:/users carries `{"method":"GET","handler":"listUsers","file":"main.go","line":18,"col":2}`, an IMPORTS cell, the POST twin and its IMPORTS cell - no POSITION. engine locate_node (tier 2) and arch::node_file fall back to ROUTE_METHOD, but every POSITION-only reader misses Go routes: pyo3 nodes_json prints `path=None` for them (grade.py --dump), projection-text node_position, passes position_file and engram-export's spans / identity hints. packets.implementation:
PARSERS EXTRACT, THE GRAPH RESOLVES: the extractor records WHICH expression is the handler; a plain or member name becomes an UnresolvedRef (HANDLED_BY) that graph::calls::resolve_refs binds through the file's import bindings, module symbols and its existing HANDLED_BY unique-global fallbacks - the Go ROUTE handler precedent - so a handler imported from another file resolves and nothing cross-file is guessed in the extractor. Only `this.x` / `self.x` (and a receiver-method value on the owner's own type) are bound in-file, because the enclosing class is a fact of this file.
queues.rs (~200 LOC):
```rust
enum HandlerRule { ArgIndex(usize), Keyed(&'static [&'static str]), KeyedOrArg(&'static [&'static str], usize), RunCallback(&'static [&'static str]) }
const HANDLER_RULES: &[(&str, HandlerRule)] = &[
    ("consumer.subscribe", HandlerRule::RunCallback(&["eachMessage", "eachBatch"])), // kafkajs
    ("channel.consume", HandlerRule::ArgIndex(1)),                                   // amqplib
    ("new Worker(", HandlerRule::ArgIndex(1)),                                        // BullMQ processor
    ("nc.subscribe", HandlerRule::Keyed(&["callback"])),                              // nats.js
    ("nc.Subscribe", HandlerRule::ArgIndex(1)),                                       // nats.go
    ("nc.QueueSubscribe", HandlerRule::ArgIndex(2)),
    ("basic_consume(", HandlerRule::KeyedOrArg(&["on_message_callback"], 1)),         // pika
];
pub enum HandlerExpr { Name(String), Member { base: String, name: String }, SelfMember(String) }
pub struct ConsumerCallback { pub consumer: NodeId, pub line: u32, pub handler: HandlerExpr, pub inline: bool }
```
Rows are keyed by the SAME needle strings as CONSUMER_PATTERNS (a unit test asserts every HANDLER_RULES needle exists there). In emit_queue_nodes, only for kind == QUEUE_CONSUMER, per recorded site (topic sites and the sentinel fallback alike - the handler is a queue handler whatever the topic): ArgIndex(n) / Keyed / KeyedOrArg read the arg slice through queue_topic::arg_region + split_args (Keyed: the value after `key:` / `key=` in that region, the keyed_literal lookup rules); RunCallback(keys): the receiver chain immediately before the needle's `.subscribe` (ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_$.] back-scan: `consumer`, `this.consumer`), then every `<chain>.run(` occurrence in the file (exact chain, identifier boundary before it) - the object arg's `eachMessage` / `eachBatch` values. handler_expr(text) on the trimmed value: `ident` -> Name; `a.b` (one dot) -> Member; `this.x` / `self.x` -> SelfMember(x); a trailing `.bind(<anything>)` is stripped first; an inline function whose body is exactly ONE call - JS `[async] (p) => [await] f(p)`, `[async] p => ..`, `[async] (p) => { [await|return] f(p); }`, `function (p) { .. }`, Go `func(m *nats.Msg) { f(m) }`, Python `lambda ch, m, p, b: f(m)` - -> that call's callee through the same rules with `inline: true`; anything else (multi-statement bodies, chained calls, computed values) -> None (LE.4c's owner edge remains the only link). Every slice goes through get() / char-boundary-safe ASCII scanning. Deduped per (consumer, handler); a site on line L gives `line: L`.
`bind_consumer_callbacks(fp, module_id, callbacks)`: owner index = anchor::build_owner_index(&fp.nodes, &fp.nav) built once; SelfMember(x) -> owner = anchor::owner_of_line(idx, line) -> its nav parent (CLASS / STRUCT) -> the METHOD child named x -> Edge consumer -HANDLED_BY-> method (Confidence::Medium); Member{base, name} with `base` a single identifier that is NOT an import binding of this file (fp.imports aliases / names) and whose owner's parent type declares a METHOD `name` -> the same direct edge (a Go method value `w.handle` inside `(w *Worker) Start`); any other Member -> UnresolvedRef{from: consumer, from_module: module_id, qualifier: Attribute{base, name}, category: HANDLED_BY}; Name(n) -> UnresolvedRef Bare(n) HANDLED_BY (resolve_refs: import binding, then this module's symbols, then the unique-global HANDLED_BY fallback). Edges are deduped against fp.edges by (from, to, category), pushed in callback order. Returns CallbackStats{consumers, direct, refs, inline, unbound}.
replace_queue_nodes (LA.4, post-cache constant-topic fold) removes EVERY queue node of the file and re-appends the fold's consumers and producers - a literal-topic node comes back with the SAME id, a sentinel `queue_consumer:unresolved:<framework>` whose sites all folded does not come back. Extend it: `let gone: HashSet<NodeId> = old queue ids minus the fold's new ids` (computed before the swap); after the swap retain only fp.edges with neither end in `gone` and fp.refs whose `from` is not in `gone` (this also drops LE.4c's owner edges and this packet's HANDLED_BY edges / refs that pointed at a vanished sentinel - they would otherwise dangle); then bind_consumer_callbacks(fp, module_id, &fold.consumers.callbacks). Edges survive for re-added same-id nodes, so bind_consumer_callbacks dedupes edges by (from, to, category) AND refs by (from, qualifier, category) against what fp already holds - a re-bound literal consumer never doubles. The replace_queue_nodes signature is unchanged (engine/src/build/grafts.rs is not edited); LE.4c's owner edges for a folded NEW id are not re-created here (anchor::attach needs the file path, which replace_queue_nodes does not take) - reported to the orchestrator as an LE.4c / LA.4 gap. Unit test replace_queue_nodes_leaves_no_dangling_edge_or_ref: a file with a literal consumer (same id before and after) and a sentinel consumer that folds to `orders` - after the replace no edge or ref names the sentinel id, the literal consumer keeps exactly one HANDLED_BY per callback, and the folded consumer gets its callback edge / ref.
queue_topic.rs: `arg_region` and `split_args` become pub(crate) (no behaviour change).
engine/src/extract.rs (~12 LOC): take the consumer QueueNodes' callbacks before the macro moves the nodes (`let callbacks = std::mem::take(&mut consumers.callbacks);`), and after `anchor::attach(..)`: `let cb = queues::bind_consumer_callbacks(fp, module_id, &callbacks);` and, when cb.consumers > 0, eprintln `[queue-callbacks] consumers=C bound=B (direct=D refs=R inline=I) unbound=U path=<path>`.

packets.title: Dart unqualified calls inside a class follow Dart lexical scope: a name the enclosing class declares (instance or static member) is a SelfMethod and wins over a same-named top-level function; parameters and locals shadow both
packets.rationale: On HEAD no Dart unqualified call reaches the graph: parsers/code/dart/src/lib.rs collect_calls_in only matches a `selector_expression`, which tree-sitter-dart 0.1.0 does not have. LA.23e rewrites that walker over the real `identifier` + `selector` sequences and emits `Bare(id)` for `<id>(args)`, and its own acceptance records the rest of this item: 'dart/calls' bare self-call `add(acc, x)` is emitted as `Bare(add)` and stays unresolved - a Dart instance-member bare call needs a SelfMethod-then-Bare fallback the resolver does not have'. graph resolve_calls' Bare arm looks up import bindings, the file MODULE's symbols and an enclosing PACKAGE - never the enclosing class - so a bare call to a class member resolves nowhere, and WORSE, once LA.23e emits Bare, a same-named top-level function or a parameter named like one binds wrongly (Dart resolves a bare name local scope first, then the class's own members, then library scope). CARRIER (code-domain, ~25 LOC): `pub local_types: HashMap<NodeId, HashMap<String, String>>` on CodeNav (derive list unchanged; build-time only like field_types - never mirrored into CodeNavStore). `record_local_type(scope, name, ty)`: first write stores ty; a later write with a DIFFERENT ty stores "" (conflict = unknown); "" means 'a local of unknown type'. The parse cache is keyed on PARSER_STAMP (code-domain is a hashed root), so the field invalidates caches by itself.
GENERIC PASS (graph/src/calls.rs, ~30 LOC + tests): factor A6.2a's receiver lookup into `pub(crate) fn receiver_type<'g>(g: &'g RepoGraph, site: &CallSite) -> Option<&'g str>` (pub(crate) because LA.35b's Rust hook reuses it): receiver = Attribute base or ComplexReceiver receiver; strip `this.` / `self.` (is_self); reject anything receiver_field rejects; if !is_self and local_types[site.from] has the name -> "" returns None (shadow: never fall through to fields), `self.<f>` -> field_types[owner][f], otherwise that type; else A6.2a's field lookup. resolve_via_receiver_type uses it, then A6.2a's resolve_type_name + class_methods unchanged. Parsers that record no locals (every other language) see identical behaviour. merge_nav (graph/src/build.rs): `for (k, v) in src.local_types { dst.local_types.entry(k).or_default().extend(v); }`.
RUST PARSER (~165 LOC + ~110 test LOC):
(1) classify_call: a `field_expression` whose `value` is an `identifier` (not `self`) whose first character is an ASCII lowercase letter or `_` -> ComplexReceiver{receiver: ident text, name: field} instead of Attribute (A6.2a's receiver_field accepts a dot-free receiver; LA.1a's hook examines Attribute sites only, so a method call on a value can no longer be read as a module path). An UpperCamel / SCREAMING identifier receiver STAYS Attribute: `Repo.find(5)` on a unit-struct value (or `CONFIG.get()` on a static) is bound on HEAD through the import binding + class_methods (verifier probe: the fixture's `unit_value -> Repo::find` row is OK on HEAD) and would be lost as a ComplexReceiver, because no local or field is named `Repo`. LA.2's collect_macro_calls METHOD CALL rule: the same lowercase test (update its unit test). Path calls (`scoped_identifier`) stay Attribute.
(2) `fn rust_type_name(ty: TsNode, src, impl_type: Option<&str>) -> Option<String>`: reference_type -> inner; generic_type whose base is Arc | Rc | Box | Cow -> first type argument recursively; generic_type otherwise -> its base name (`Repo<T>` -> Repo) unless the base is Option | Result | Vec | HashMap | BTreeMap | HashSet | RefCell | Mutex | RwLock (None: a method on it is the container's); scoped_type_identifier -> last segment; type_identifier -> text, `Self` -> impl_type; primitive / tuple / array / pointer / function / dyn / impl types -> None.
(3) Fields: for each struct_item with a field_declaration_list, record_field_type(struct id, field name, ty) for every field whose rust_type_name is Some (tuple structs have no names: skipped).
(4) `collect_local_types(fn_node, body, fn_id, impl_type, acc)` (one walk, not descending into nested function_item): parameters (`parameter` with an identifier pattern: rust_type_name(type) or ""; self_parameter skipped); closure_parameters (typed -> type, untyped -> ""); let_declaration with an identifier pattern: the `type` annotation if present, else the initialiser: struct_expression `T { .. }` -> T; call_expression `T::new(..)` / `T::default()` / `T::from(..)` / `Self::new(..)` (path whose last segment is new | default | from, type = the segment before it, Self -> impl_type); an UpperCamel-last-segment path or call `E::Variant` / `E::Variant(..)` -> E (an enum value; its methods bind in the generic pass once LA.30a indexes ENUM methods, else through LA.35b's hook); `&self.f` / `self.f.clone()` / `self.f` -> the alias `self.f`; an identifier naming an already-recorded local -> that local's type; anything else -> "". Every OTHER pattern binding in the body - for-loop patterns, if-let / while-let / match-arm patterns, tuple / struct destructuring, `let` with a non-identifier pattern - records its bound identifiers as "" (they shadow fields and outer names). All go through record_local_type(fn_id, ..), so conflicts become "".

Measured on HEAD on the fixture: `self.cache.lookup("k")` with `cache: Arc<Cache>` and `impl Cache` in src/cache_impl.rs - `Cache::lookup` is METHOD `src::cache_impl::Cache::lookup` parented to MODULE src::cache_impl, so class_methods[Cache] has no `lookup` and the call stays unresolved even with the field type known. The Rust hook already owns the data: LA.1a's RustIndex keeps `impl_elsewhere: (type name, member) -> sorted METHOD ids` and LA.3 adds ENUM members; LA.3's SelfMethod rule already recovers the owning type of a module-parented method from its qname. The receiver pass is a generic miss, so the hook (consulted only after a generic miss) is the right seam. Also: LA.1b's coverage row claims typed receivers are not implemented at all - after LA.35a/b only the residual shapes remain blind.

graph/src/rust_paths.rs (~90 LOC + ~60 test LOC): in resolve_call, for `ComplexReceiver{receiver, name}` (and Attribute sites whose base LA.1a's path rules did not start - defensive, LA.35a routes `.` calls to ComplexReceiver): (1) type name = crate::calls::receiver_type(g, site) (LA.35a declares it pub(crate)); when it returns None because the receiver is `self.<f>` and enclosing_class_or_struct found no owner, recover the owner the LA.3 way: the caller METHOD's nav parent is a MODULE -> the type segment of the caller's qname (`<module>::<Type>::<m>`) -> the unique crate-local STRUCT / ENUM of that name (RustIndex type index, sorted candidates, ambiguity -> None) -> field_types[owner][f]. A shadowing local ("") returns None here too. (2) type node: RustIndex's scope-aware lookup of the bare type name from the caller (fn-scoped / module bindings from LA.1b, module-local types, then the unique crate-local STRUCT / ENUM / INTERFACE of that name - never the cross-crate unique_global_function fallback). (3) member: class_methods[type][name], else LA.3's ENUM member index (METHOD children), else impl_elsewhere[(type name, name)] restricted to the caller's crate and unique -> the METHOD. A hit calls code_domain::recv_stats::record() (so A6.2a's `[recv]` rust token counts it) and a hook counter by kind (impl_elsewhere / cross_file_self_field / enum_member). Lookup-only over sorted Vecs; no HashMap iteration chooses a result.
