packets.area: LB - identity: channel-side identity (monorepo, rpc + events)
packets.rationale:
LB.8 gives queue / ws / graphql / grpc sides the LB.4a owner suffix; run-2 decision 7.3.4 moved the two remaining channel families here. MEASURED on HEAD ee4a84a (debug CLI + installed wheel) on the fixture below (scratch copy; `[roots] 8 project roots (npm=8)`): services/users and services/legacy both declare `userRouter = t.router({ list: ... })` -> ONE RPC_PROCEDURE `rpc:user.list`; apps/web and apps/admin both call `api.user.list.useQuery()` -> ONE RPC_CALL `rpc_call:user.list`; `[trpc-link] calls=1 paired=1 procedures=1 edges=1`. services/orders and services/billing each create their OWN `new EventEmitter()` and emit / handle `orderPlaced` -> ONE EVENT_EMITTER `event_emit:orderPlaced` (USES from both services) and ONE EVENT_HANDLER `event_handle:orderPlaced` (HANDLED_BY lib::bus::registerAudit, services::orders::events::registerOrderHandlers AND services::billing::events::registerBillingHandlers); services/orders' `this.client.emit("orderShipped")` (ClientProxy, @nestjs/microservices) and services/notify's `@EventPattern("orderShipped")` -> `event_emit:orderShipped` / `event_handle:orderShipped`; `[eventbus] 2 pairs (exact=2 type-folded=0)`; `glia arch --include-shared`: `[arch] 8 services, 2 links (keying=project_roots buckets=2 unplaced=1 self=0 unlocated=2)` - services/billing -> (outside projects) EVENT_FLOWS orderPlaced and services/orders -> services/notify EVENT_FLOWS orderShipped; the tRPC link is unplaced. grade.py: nodes 0/10, EVENT_FLOWS 0/3, RPC_CALLS 0/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 4.
DECISION - may an in-process event pair across projects? NO; a transport event may, and an unowned side still pairs with every owner. (1) An in-process bus (Node EventEmitter / EventEmitter2 `.emit(` / `.on(`, NestJS `@OnEvent(`, CQRS `@EventsHandler(` / `.publish(new`, Spring ApplicationEventPublisher / `@EventListener`, MediatR, RxJS Subject, DOM events, pubsub-js) delivers only inside one process, and two nested projects are two build artefacts - exactly what `glia arch` calls two services (LB.4a: owner == arch service id). A cross-owner EVENT_FLOWS between two in-process buses asserts a flow the runtime cannot carry; event names are generic (`error`, `change`, `data`, `close`, the extractor's verb fallbacks `emit` / `on`), so all-to-all across owners would mesh every service pair in `glia arch` (EVENT_FLOWS is in arch::FLOW_MECHANISMS). (2) But the EVENT_* kinds are NOT all in-process, so the draft premise 'EVENT_* is by construction an in-process bus' is wrong: parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs HANDLER_PATTERNS mints `@EventPattern(` - the NestJS microservices handler, fed over a transport (Kafka / RMQ / Redis / NATS / TCP) by `ClientProxy.emit(` in ANOTHER service - and EMITTER_PATTERNS mints `EventBridge.putEvents` / `eventBridge.putEvents` (AWS EventBridge, a network bus). Run 3's LA.39 keeps `.emit(` in a `@nestjs/microservices` file precisely as the conjugate of `@EventPattern(`. Measured above: HEAD shows services/orders -> services/notify EVENT_FLOWS orderShipped; an owner-only rule would delete that real cross-service flow. So the extractor marks those nodes transport-scoped and a transport side pairs across owners like LB.8's queues. (3) An UNOWNED side (a file under no nested project: root-level shared code, a repo without nested manifests, a multi-repo build of manifest-free repos) keeps pairing with every owner - it may be linked into any of them. The committed fixture arch-monorepo-flows keeps its api -> worker EVENT_FLOWS: worker/notify.ts imports `bus` from `../api/orders` (one process, one bus) and neither api/ nor worker/ holds a manifest, so both sides are unowned (verified: no committed fixture or matrix probe holds an EVENT_* or RPC_* node in a file under a nested manifest - the only nested-manifest trees are walk-project-roots and matrix/{go,java,typescript}/subproject, none with event or rpc code); fixtures/xcut-eventbus-spring (two manifest-free repos) stays unchanged. Real corpora at HEAD lose nothing: quokka-stack has 10 event nodes, all in quokka_web files, 0 EVENT_FLOWS (debug CLI json, this session); glia's own build shows the defect: event_emit:OrderPlacedEvent / event_handle:OrderPlacedEvent each fold the bench project's xcut-eventbus-spring sources and the parsers/code/extractors crate's test strings into one node.
RPC: tRPC, Connect and Twirp are network RPC, so RPC_PROCEDURE / RPC_CALL are channel SIDES like GRPC_SERVER / GRPC_CLIENT and pair all-to-all across owners on the exact path (LB.8's rule). There is no RPC contract node to keep shared (LA.17 derives procedures from the registered handler; GRPC_SERVICE stays unowned under LB.8).
Code-qname events stay out of the owner table: the Solidity parser mints EVENT_EMITTER for `event BidPlaced(..)` with an ordinary code qname (`<module>::Auction::Auction::BidPlaced`, parsers/code/solidity/src/lib.rs emit of `format!("{parent_qname}::{name}")`), already path-scoped, and an on-chain event is consumed off-chain by other processes - so it is left unowned (pairs with every owner). The owner rows therefore carry a required qname prefix.
Graph queries run: find EventBusResolver / emit_route_from_call / tag_synthetic_provenance, read graph::src::resolvers::eventbus::EventBusResolver::resolve, impact parsers::code::extractors::src::eventbus::push_event_node backward (-> extract_event_emitter_nodes :118, extract_event_handler_nodes :172).

The node's file: crate::arch::node_file (POSITION - event markers carry it since A5.8, tRPC after LA.31, Connect / Twirp after LA.17), else the fp's MODULE file. rekey_node, the foreign census and the incremental rule are LB.4a's; rekey carries every cell, so the transport ORIGIN below survives. OwnerStats { .., rpc, event, declared }. report(): LB.8's `[channel-owner]` line unchanged (still gated on q+w+g+r > 0) plus `[channel-owner] qualified rpc={p} event={e} over {owners} owners (declared={d}) repo={label}` when p+e+d > 0 - a second line instead of new fields, so LB.8's marker and any test that reads it stay byte-identical.
parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs (~30 LOC). DELIVERY SCOPE, recorded where it is known (the needle): `const TRANSPORT_NEEDLES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("@EventPattern(", "nestjs-microservices"), ("EventBridge.putEvents", "aws-eventbridge"), ("eventBridge.putEvents", "aws-eventbridge")];` plus the `.emit(` needle when the source contains `"@nestjs/microservices"` or `'@nestjs/microservices'` (the ClientProxy.emit conjugate; the same test LA.39's R4 uses, computed here without depending on it). After the string-keyed push_event_node call (which returns the id whether it minted or re-saw the name), `mark_transport(&mut nodes, id, via)` pushes `Cell { kind: ORIGIN, payload: Json(r#"{"provenance":"synthetic","delivery":"transport","via":"<via>"}"# ) }` onto that node unless it already carries an ORIGIN cell. provenance stays "synthetic": engine/src/passes.rs tag_synthetic_provenance skips any node that already has ORIGIN and would otherwise write exactly {"provenance":"synthetic"} on every EVENT_* node, and engram-export's origin_provenance reads only `provenance`, so engram still drops these nodes as before. ALTERNATIVES weighed: (a) a name / qname marker - REJECTED, a second identity change; (b) a new cell type - REJECTED, ORIGIN (15) already means provenance / locality and needs no id; (c) inferring scope in the resolver from the handler's imports - REJECTED, the resolver sees no source. The mark is parse content, so PARSER_STAMP re-keys the cache.
graph/src/resolvers/rpc.rs (~3 LOC): the RPC_CALL read goes through split_owner. Pairing stays exact on the path, all-to-all across owners; `[trpc-link]` unchanged.
graph/src/resolvers/eventbus.rs (~60 LOC). DESIGN weighed: (a) all-to-all across owners like LB.8 - REJECTED for in-process nodes (rationale (1)); (b) pair across owners when one project's manifest depends on the other (a workspace dependency closure from PACKAGE_DEP names vs root labels) - REJECTED here: PROJECT nodes are edge-less by A8.5, maven / gradle / dotnet manifests carry no PACKAGE_DEP extraction, and it would be a new build-wide pass (listed as a gap); (c) owner-only co-residence - REJECTED, drops NestJS microservices / EventBridge flows (rationale (2)); (d) CHOSEN: co-residence OR transport. `fn event_key<'q>(nav, id, qname: &'q str, prefix) -> Option<(String, Option<&'q str>)>`: `let (bare, owner) = split_owner(qname);` then today's prefix / name rule on `bare` (a Solidity code qname never carries ` @`, so owner None). `fn is_transport(cells: &[Cell]) -> bool` = any ORIGIN cell whose Json payload contains `"delivery":"transport"` (a substring test, the extract_method_field precedent - no serde_json in the graph crate). Handler index: `HashMap<String, Vec<HandlerEntry>>` with `struct HandlerEntry<'g> { target: ServiceTarget, repo: RepoId, owner: Option<&'g str>, transport: bool }`, pushed in graph / node order (lookup-only map, deterministic Vec). `fn pairs(e: &Side, h: &HandlerEntry) -> Pairing` = SameOwner when both owners are Some and (repo, owner) are equal; UnownedSide when either owner is None; Transport when either side is transport; else Dropped (the owner is compared together with the RepoId, so two repos' identical rel paths are two projects). Per matched target: push the edge unless Dropped; count same_owner / unowned_side / transport / cross_owner_dropped. `exact` / `folded` count PUSHED edges only (identical to today when no node is owned). After the loop, when any indexed or matched node carried an owner: `[eventbus-owner] same-owner={s} unowned-side={u} transport={t} cross-owner-dropped={x}`; the existing `[eventbus]` line is unchanged for owner-free builds.

METHOD TOKEN (~8 LOC): add_method upper-cases the method; `all` (Express `.all(`, Nest `@All(`, Hapi `*` / ANY / ALL via canonical_http_method) -> `ANY`; the Pages Router default export -> `ANY` (Next.js hands every method to it); a Bun route whose value is not a verb object -> `ANY` (Bun serves a handler function or a Response for every method; HEAD's test comment says it 'defaults to get'). ALTERNATIVE weighed: keep `ALL` / `GET` - REJECTED: `ALL` is a token no client ever sends and the any tier keys on `ANY`, so an `.all(` route pairs with nothing today, and a GET-named default export would be a wrong identity now that the method is in the qname. SvelteKit / App Router files only use named exports, so the fallback only fires for Pages Router default exports in practice. The ANY choice is also load-bearing for LA.6d's committed-later fixture nav-next-pages, whose exact forbid `GET /api/health` would falsely fire if pages/api/health.ts became `GET /api/health`.
ROWS (~70 LOC): every shape reports the 0-based row of its registration: Express and Nest from `lines().enumerate()` (the decorator's row for Nest); Next / SvelteKit from anchor::line_of at the export needle; Hapi from the `{` of the route config object (body offsets are relative, so extract_hapi_configs takes the body's absolute base); Bun from the route key (subslice pointer offset of `routes_obj` within `source`, the LA.31 technique; every slice is a &str subslice of `source`, so offsets are char boundaries). Rows feed both the POSITION cells and the ROUTE_METHOD `line` (1-based, the Go convention; `col` stays 0 = unknown).
EMISSION (~40 LOC): one node per (path, METHOD) in BTreeMap order (deterministic); `RouteNodes.positioned` = POSITION cells pushed, `.any` = ANY nodes. HANDLED_BY refs: one per (path, METHOD, handler) with `from` = that node's id. Next.js and SvelteKit paths come from nextjs_route_from_path / sveltekit_route_from_path unchanged.
ENGINE (~8 LOC): the per-file `[ts-routes]` line in engine/src/extract.rs beside the `[trpc]` one.

Walking every #if branch emits code for every platform (a function defined per platform folds into one node through `emitted`); only a literal `#if 0` is treated as dead. packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD by the verifier (debug CLI on a copy of the fixture sketch, probe/LB-r3b-verify/msg, and grade.py): src/util.ts + src/util.js are ONE MODULE `src::util`; both `fmt` functions are one FUNCTION `src::util::fmt` (DEFINES src::util -> src::util::fmt x2) with CALLS to BOTH `pad` (util.ts) and `legacy` (util.js) - a call graph neither file has - and the IMPORTS from app.ts and old.js both land on the merged module. clj/app/core.clj + core.cljs: one MODULE `clj::app::core` whose one `f` calls g (the JVM file) and h (the JS file); DEFINES core -> core::f x2. jvm/shop/Foo.java + Foo.kt: one MODULE `jvm::shop::Foo` (at HEAD .kt goes to the java parser; after A14.2 the Kotlin crate emits Foo.kt's top-level functions under the same MODULE qname, one JVM graph). Cause: path_to_qname (engine/src/extract.rs:307) drops the extension, and LB.9b's ModuleQnames qualifies a stem only when >= 2 BUILD GROUPS claim it - its plan test pins `{a/x.js, a/x.ts}` as not qualified and its SCOPE line leaves util.js + util.ts and core.clj + core.cljs merged as a residual; for a cross-group key that ALSO holds a same-group pair (util.py + util.ts + util.js) LB.9b registers no TS alias and declares `./util` unresolved. Real corpus: the verifier's `git ls-files` scan of every repo under /home/ivy/Code finds no same-group same-stem pair outside C/C++ (quokka_app 6, samples 150, splorts 2 - all LB.10a's), and no committed fixture or matrix probe holds one; this packet is correctness for the idioms that produce them: tsc output beside its .ts, a JS -> TS migration, the ClojureScript macro-namespace pair (foo.cljs + foo.clj), Java classes with Kotlin extension files (Foo.java + Foo.kt), Elixir .ex + .exs, Terraform .tf + .hcl. IDENTITY: every file of a same-stem key is qualified whatever its group (LB.9b's naming, sibling-dependent as LB.9b already is - accepted in plan 7.3.5). RESOLUTION after the split (weighed): (a) register the bare alias to one fixed precedence (.ts before .js) - rejected: a JS importer of util.js and a ClojureScript require of core.cljs would bind the other platform's file; (b) leave the pair's bare imports unresolved (LB.9b's rule) - rejected: every IMPORTS edge and the CALLS riding on its binding that HEAD resolves (onto the merged node) would be lost; (c) CHOSEN: bind a bare import to the sibling the IMPORTER's language loads - an explicit extension in the specifier wins, else the importer's extension selects that language's own resolution order. Only the TS family and Clojure import FILES: Java / Kotlin imports name classes (resolve_imports_python's tail fallback binds the CLASS by its unique name, untouched by a MODULE rename), Elixir aliases name defmodule PACKAGEs, Terraform modules are directories - so their order is empty and they only get the identity split. A .cljc importer is compiled for both platforms and loads a different sibling on each, so its order is empty too (unresolved and counted, never guessed). The order table lives in code-domain beside LB.9b's bare_module_qname; the pick is build-local (never stored in the SymbolTable, so the .gmap does not move). C/C++ files claim no bare key after LB.10a, so this packet never touches them. VERIFIER CHANGES: the draft's table entries for java / kt / ex / exs / tf / hcl (never exercised: those imports do not resolve by file) and cljc -> [cljc, clj, cljs] (platform-dependent) were cut to empty orders.

packets.rationale: HEAD: every C/C++ type qname is `<file module>::[<namespace block>::]<Type>`: visit_type (parsers/code/c_cpp/src/lib.rs:140) builds `format!("{parent_qname}::{name}")` (:158) with parent_qname = the MODULE or the file's namespace PACKAGE (visit_namespace :104 builds `{parent_qname}::{name}`, :117), so a namespaced header class is `include::shop::cart::shop::Cart` (verifier, grade.py on the fixture sketch: forbid matched=1) and, once LB.10a has walked the include guard, src/Widget.h's `class Widget` would be `src::Widget.h::Widget` - still scoped by a file the .cpp half never names. An out-of-line member is a FUNCTION named `Q::m` under the file MODULE even when its class is declared a few lines above in the same file (verifier runner probe: FUNCTION `windows::runner::win32_window::WindowClassRegistrar::GetWindowClass` beside CLASS `...::WindowClassRegistrar`; fixture: FUNCTION `src::Widget::Local::a` next to CLASS `src::Widget::Local`, forbid matched=1), so `this->b()` in its body resolves to nothing (CALLS 0/1). extract_func_name (:295) falls to its text branch for a reference_declarator (tree-sitter-cpp 0.23.4 gives it no `declarator` field - node-types.json read by the verifier), so `const T& Foo::get()` is named `& Foo::get` and could never be split into its class and member. RULE (the LB.7 family; LB.7d's C# shape): a type a HEADER declares is the same type in every translation unit that includes it, and C++'s one-definition rule forbids two different definitions of one qualified name in a program, so its identity is its C++ name - the namespace path (`shop::Cart`, as C# block namespaces) or, in the global namespace, the header's directory (`src::Widget`, LB.2's monorepo rule: samples holds 25 copies of the Flutter runner's global `Win32Window` / `FlutterWindow` in 25 app directories, which a bare name would merge). A type a SOURCE file (.c/.cc/.cpp/.cxx) declares is visible only in that translation unit and keeps the file scope (HEAD's shape under LB.10a's file-name MODULE), like C# `file` types (LB.7d / LB.14). Free functions keep the file scope: a function has exactly one definition, the header prototype is not a node, and a directory scope would merge every `main` of a directory of small programs. Measured on ~/Code headers (spec agent's regex scan of samples / quokka_app / splorts): 105 header-declared class/struct types, 0 same-name pairs inside one directory, 0 namespaces in the Flutter runners - the global-namespace directory rule carries the real corpus; the namespace rule carries the include/<lib>/x.hpp + src/x.cpp library layout (both halves compute `shop::Cart` without knowing each other's directory). An out-of-line member whose class this file does NOT declare cannot be bound by the parser (it cannot see the header, cannot tell a class from a namespace, and does not know CLASS vs STRUCT, which is part of the NodeId): it is emitted as a provisional METHOD at the header-rule qname, which is already the final qname whenever the class is in the definition's directory or namespace, and LB.10c binds or renames it at graph build. packets.title: Swift call names drop the navigation dot: `self.m()` / `self?.m()` / `Self.m()` are SelfMethod("m"), `super.m()` is SuperMethod, `x.m()` is Attribute{x, m}
packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD ee4a84a (code 5280cee). tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 (Cargo.lock) shapes `self.helper()` as call_expression > navigation_expression{target: self_expression, suffix: navigation_suffix} and the navigation_suffix node spans the dot: its text is `.helper`, the bare name is its own `suffix` field (simple_identifier) - pinned with a scratch tree dump (probe/LA-r3a/tsdump over probe/LA-r3a/swift1 and swift2) and node-types.json (`navigation_suffix` fields: suffix -> simple_identifier | integer_literal). parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs classify_call reads `func_node.child_by_field_name("suffix")` and takes the navigation_suffix's TEXT, so every SelfMethod / Attribute / ComplexReceiver name starts with `.`: SelfMethod(".helper") never matches class_methods["helper"] in graph resolve_calls, so zero Swift self-calls resolve. Probe (debug CLI `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia analyze probe/LA-r3a/swift1 --format json`): class Widget with `run -> self.helper()`, `bare -> helper()`, `viaField -> repo.find()` and a top-level `topLevel -> Widget()` -> the ONLY CALLS edge is `topLevel -> Widget` (a Bare constructor call); no method has an outgoing CALLS edge. Same tree dump: `super.k()` has target super_expression (classified today as ComplexReceiver{receiver: "super", name: ".k"}), `Self.make()` has target simple_identifier `Self` (classified Attribute{Self, .make} - never bound, although Self IS the enclosing type), and `self?.g()` inside a `[weak self]` closure has target self_expression (text `self`). Graph queries: find classify_call (6 hits; parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs:275), impact classify_call backward -> collect_calls_in :253 -> visit_method / visit_function -> visit_type / visit_top (nothing outside the parser reads the name). SCOPE: implicit-self calls (`helper()` inside a type, which reach the graph as Bare) are a different cause and not this item; they stay as HEAD and are reported as a GAP (no owner), with the measured wrong bindings. VERIFIER (re-measured at HEAD ee4a84a): tree dump of `self.helper()`, `self?.refresh()` in a `[weak self]` closure, `Self.make()`, `super.k()` and `self.items.map {}` (probe/LA-r3a/verify/swift/a.swift) confirms every shape above; tree-sitter-swift names its closures `lambda_literal`, so collect_calls_in's `closure_expression` skip never fires and closure bodies ARE walked (the `[weak self]` row is attributed to the enclosing method). grade.py on a fresh copy of the fixture: CALLS 1/6 (0.17) PARTIAL, forbid 0, nodes=16 edges=17 - identical to the draft. graph: find classify_call (6 hits, swift :275), read classify_call + collect_calls_in, impact classify_call backward depth 3 -> collect_calls_in :253, visit_method :204, visit_function :167, visit_top :69, visit_type :113 (nothing outside the parser).

packets.implementation:
parsers/code/swift/src/lib.rs (~35 LOC non-test):
```rust
/// tree-sitter-swift's `navigation_suffix` spans the dot (`.helper`); the member name is its own
/// `suffix` field (simple_identifier, or integer_literal for a tuple index). "" when absent.
fn nav_member_name<'a>(nav_expr: TsNode<'a>, src: &'a [u8]) -> &'a str {
    nav_expr.child_by_field_name("suffix")
        .and_then(|s| s.child_by_field_name("suffix"))
        .map(|n| text_of(n, src))
        .unwrap_or("")
}
```
classify_call's navigation_expression arm: `let target = func_node.named_child(0)` (the `target` field, as HEAD); `let name = nav_member_name(func_node, src)`; match target kind: `self_expression` -> SelfMethod(name) (covers `self?.g()` - the `?` is not part of the self_expression); `super_expression` -> SuperMethod(name) (graph resolve_calls leaves SuperMethod unresolved - diagnostic only, same as Python cross-file super); `simple_identifier` whose text is exactly `Self` -> SelfMethod(name) (Swift's `Self` is the enclosing type, so `Self.make()` is a static member of the type SelfMethod walks to; `Self` inside a protocol extension resolves against the extension node, as any SelfMethod there does); other `simple_identifier` -> Attribute{base: text, name}; otherwise ComplexReceiver{receiver: target text, name}. When `name` is empty (an unexpected suffix shape) the arm falls back to ComplexReceiver{receiver: whole callee text, name: ""} exactly as the `_` arm does. The Bare arm and the `_` arm are unchanged.
Design (weighed): (a) strip a leading '.' from the suffix text - REJECTED: it keeps a text-shaped parse where the grammar already exposes the identifier node, and it silently passes tuple-index / backticked names through; (b) CHOSEN: read the navigation_suffix's own `suffix` field. Classification by node kind instead of `text == "self"` is equivalent for self (self_expression's text is `self`) and adds the `super` / `Self` cases the kind makes unambiguous.
MARKER: Acc counts SelfMethod and SuperMethod sites; parse_file prints `[swift-calls] self={s} super={p} file={file_rel_path}` when `swift_debug()` (a `static SWIFT_DEBUG: OnceLock<bool>` reading GLIA_SWIFT_DEBUG once, the parsers/code/php bind_debug_enabled precedent) and s + p > 0. Gated because nearly every Swift file has self calls.
UNIT TESTS (mod tests, ~70 LOC; assert on fp.calls qualifiers): self_call_name_drops_the_navigation_dot (`class W { func a() { self.b() } func b() {} }` -> SelfMethod("b")); optional_self_in_a_closure_is_self_method (`schedule { [weak self] in self?.g() }` -> SelfMethod("g") from the enclosing method); upper_self_is_self_method (`Self.make()` -> SelfMethod("make")); super_call_is_super_method (`super.k()` -> SuperMethod("k")); identifier_receiver_is_attribute_without_dot (`repo.find()` -> Attribute{base: "repo", name: "find"}); chained_receiver_is_complex_without_dot (`self.items.map { }` -> ComplexReceiver{receiver: "self.items", name: "map"}).
ENGINE TEST engine/tests/swift_calls.rs (~50 LOC, new): `generate_one(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/swift-self-calls"))`; collect CALLS edges as (from qname, to qname, to kind) from `r.merged.graphs` (nav.qname_by_id / kind_by_id); assert METHOD targets for `Sources::Shop::Widget::run -> Sources::Shop::Widget::helper`, `Widget::later -> Widget::refresh`, `Widget::build -> Widget::make`, `Sources::Shop::Part::weight -> Sources::Shop::Part::base`, `Sources::Shop::Mode::label -> Sources::Shop::Mode::describe` (qnames in LB.7c's module-scoped shape, LB.7c lands first); assert no CALLS from `Sources::Shop::Widget::run` to the FUNCTION `Sources::Shop::Shapes::helper`.
EVIDENCE (LC.3): no edge is pushed by the parser; the new CALLS edges come from graph resolve_calls' SelfMethod arm and carry LC.3d's branch evidence (or LC.3a's graph stamp before LC.3d). If LC.3b has landed, CallSite has a `line` field that the existing construction site already fills; this packet changes only the qualifier. Order relative to LC.3 is free.

packets.title: Dart top-level functions, getters and setters own their sibling function_body: the body is walked (calls, client ENDPOINTs) under LA.34's local scope, a getter / setter pair is one FUNCTION, and the FUNCTION's CODE / POSITION span signature + body
packets.rationale: tree-sitter-dart 0.1.0 (the only version in Cargo.lock) puts a top-level function's body BESIDE its signature: source_file children are `function_signature` then `function_body` (and `getter_signature` / `setter_signature` then `function_body` for a top-level getter / setter; a setter WITHOUT a return type, `set x(int v)`, parses as a function_signature whose return_type is the identifier `set`, while `void set x(int v)` parses as setter_signature) - pinned with the scratch tree dump (probe/LA-r3a/tsdump over probe/LA-r3a/dart1/lib/api.dart and fx/dart-top-level-bodies/lib/app.dart), which also shows a `comment` node can sit between the two and an `external` function has no body at all. parsers/code/dart/src/lib.rs visit_top matches `function_signature | function_definition | top_level_definition` (the last two kinds do not exist in the grammar - node-types.json checked) and visit_function records the FUNCTION from the signature and returns; the sibling function_body falls into `_ => {}`. Consequences measured at HEAD ee4a84a: (a) no top-level function has an outgoing call or ENDPOINT - probe dart1 (debug CLI): `loadUsers() { await dio.get('/users'); helper(1); }` yields no ENDPOINT for /users while the same call inside a class method yields `CALLS Svc::reload -> endpoint:GET:/orders`; (b) a top-level getter and a `void set` setter have no node (`String get banner => ...` absent); (c) the FUNCTION's CODE and POSITION cells come from entity_cells(signature) and cover the signature line only, so `read` shows no body. Real repos: quokka_app has 14 top-level function bodies in 39 .dart files, flutter samples 502 in 526 (counted with the scratch tree dump); every `main()` is one. Graph queries: find visit_class_member / impact visit_function backward -> visit_top -> parse_file. LA.34's verifier cut this from LA.34 as a separate finding ('visit_function records a FUNCTION but never reads its sibling function_body'); no packet owns it. VERIFIER (HEAD ee4a84a): node-types.json of tree-sitter-dart 0.1.0 has no `function_definition` / `top_level_definition` and lists `setter_signature` as a source_file child; a dump of probe/LA-r3a/verify/dart/set2.dart shows `void set x(int v) { a(); }` as setter_signature + function_body, which the draft's arm missed. The verifier re-counted with the scratch tree dump: quokka_app 14 top-level function bodies in 39 files, flutter samples 502 in 526 (1 top-level accessor signature). The fixture below adds a top-level getter / `void set` setter pair and was graded on HEAD.

packets.title: C#: a `using` directive inside a block namespace is recorded with the FILE module as from_module, so it resolves like a file-level using
packets.rationale: Measured at HEAD ee4a84a. parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs visit_children (:94) hands its `parent_qname` to collect_using (:1291) as from_module; inside `namespace Shop.Controllers { using Shop.Models; ... }` visit_namespace (:129) walks the body (declaration_list) with the namespace qname, so the ImportStmt says from_module `Shop::Controllers`. graph/src/imports.rs resolve_imports_python (build_dotted) begins `module_by_qname.get(&stmt.from_module)` and module_by_qname holds MODULE qnames only (graph/src/build.rs build_symbol_table), so the statement is silently dropped. Probes: run 2's probe/LB-extra/csblockuse -> 0 IMPORTS while its twin csuse (the same using at file level) -> `IMPORTS Controllers::UserController -> Shop::Models` (debug CLI, re-measured this run); fixture csharp-block-using (grade.py, installed wheel = HEAD) -> IMPORTS 1/3, only the file-level control. Tree shape pinned with the scratch dump: namespace_declaration > body: declaration_list > using_directive; after a file-scoped `namespace X;` the using is a compilation_unit sibling (already the module - unchanged). Placement inside the namespace is StyleCop.Analyzers SA1200's default, so a codebase that follows it gets no C# IMPORTS edge at all today. Graph queries: find collect_using (:1291), impact collect_using / resolve_imports_python backward -> visit_children -> visit_namespace -> parse_file, build_dotted. LB.7d's risk text records this gap ('using directives written INSIDE a block namespace keep the namespace as from_module and stay unresolved ... reported as a gap'); no packet owns it. VERIFIER (HEAD ee4a84a): collect_using has exactly one caller (visit_children :107); tree dumps (probe/LA-r3a/verify/cs) confirm a file-scoped `namespace X;` leaves every later using a compilation_unit child (from_module already the module) and a nested `namespace A { namespace B { using C.D; } }` puts the using under B's declaration_list. Post-fix simulation: the same fixture with the two usings moved above the namespace block (probe/LA-r3a/verify/cs-sim, so from_module is the file module exactly as this packet makes it) grades IMPORTS 3/3, forbid 0 - the graph side needs no change. packets.implementation:
DESIGN (weighed): (a) graph fallback - when from_module misses module_by_qname, look the qname up as a PACKAGE and walk to its nav parent MODULE - REJECTED: a namespace PACKAGE is ONE NodeId shared by every file that declares that namespace, and merge_nav's `parent_of.extend` keeps the LAST file's MODULE, so the import would land on an arbitrary sibling file; (b) CHOSEN: the parser knows the file, so every ImportStmt carries the file's MODULE qname, whatever block it was written in. A using's C# scope is its namespace block within this file; glia's import bindings are per file, so the file module is the finest scope that exists (two blocks of one file binding one name differently - legal, vanishingly rare - resolve last-write-wins in source order, deterministic).
parsers/code/csharp/src/lib.rs (~20 LOC non-test): Acc gains `module_qname: String` (set in parse_file) and `scoped_usings: usize`. collect_using(node, src, acc) builds the three ImportStmt shapes exactly as today with `from_module: acc.module_qname.clone()`. visit_children's using arm: `if node.kind() != "compilation_unit" { acc.scoped_usings += 1; } collect_using(child, src, acc);`. LB.7d (lands first) keeps the using arm's argument as parent_qname; this packet replaces that argument with the Acc field, so the two changes do not collide.
MARKER: parse_file prints `[csharp-using] {n} block-namespace usings bound to the file module {module_qname} file={file_rel_path}` when `csharp_debug()` (a `static CSHARP_DEBUG: OnceLock<bool>` reading GLIA_CSHARP_DEBUG once, the php bind_debug_enabled precedent) and n > 0. Gated: SA1200 codebases would print it for every file.
UNIT TESTS (~45 LOC): using_inside_block_namespace_belongs_to_the_file (`namespace Shop.Controllers { using Shop.Models; using Shop.Services.Billing; class C {} }` with module qname `Controllers::UserController` -> 2 imports, both from_module `Controllers::UserController`); using_in_a_nested_block_namespace_belongs_to_the_file (`namespace A { namespace B { using C.D; } }`); file_level_and_file_scoped_usings_unchanged (compilation-unit using before and after `namespace X;` -> from_module the module qname, as HEAD); the existing using_imports test unchanged.

(1) GATE TABLE. The seven needles get VerbGate::Receiver; LA.29's two keep VerbGate::Bus (its receiver-or-import rule, unchanged); every other needle stays Open.
(2) RECEIVER. For a dotted needle the receiver is LA.29's receiver_segment(source, dot_at) (identifier before the `.`, a trailing `(...)` call skipped, leading `_ $ @` stripped). `dispatchEvent(` has no dot in the needle: the receiver is read before it only when the preceding byte is `.`; a bare `dispatchEvent(` (global call, method declaration, string) has none and is rejected.
(3) ADMIT (first match wins, recorded as Via):
  R1 Receiver - the lowercased receiver ends with one of LA.29's suffixes (bus, pubsub, emitter, events, mediator, publisher, notifications) or `dispatcher` (added here to the ONE shared suffix const, so LA.29's `publish(` / `.subscribe(` receiver rule admits `eventDispatcher.publish(..)` too: `eventDispatcher.dispatch('order.placed', e)`). Keeps bus.on / bus.emit, this.eventBus.addListener, emitter.on, @emitter.on (pyee), this.eventEmitter.emit (NestJS EventEmitter2), this.events.trigger.
  R2 Bound - the receiver identifier is bound in this file to an in-process emitter: `emitter_bindings(source)` scans (once per file, lazily) for the constructor tokens `new EventEmitter(`, `new EventEmitter<`, `new EventEmitter2(`, `new EventTarget(`, `new Emitter(`, `mitt(`, `createNanoEvents(`, and Python `EventEmitter(` / `AsyncIOEventEmitter(`; for each, walks back over spaces to `=` (not `==`, `=>`, `!=`, `<=`, `>=`), then over an optional `: Type` annotation and spaces, and records the identifier before it (a `this.` / `self.` prefix dropped). Admitted when the receiver is in that list AND (the constructor was `new EventTarget(` OR the file IMPORTS an emitter library). IMPORT means `fn imports_emitter_lib(source) -> bool`: a quoted module string that is exactly one of `events`, `node:events`, `eventemitter2`, `eventemitter3`, `mitt`, `nanoevents`, `tiny-emitter`, `@nestjs/event-emitter` AND sits in import position - the bytes before its opening quote, whitespace skipped, end with `from`, `require(`, `import(` or a bare `import` keyword (identifier-bounded) - or a Python line whose trimmed text starts `from pyee` / `import pyee`. A bare quoted word is not enough: `db.collection('events')`, `router.navigate(['events'])` or `@Output() ... 'events'` never make a file an emitter-library file. An Angular `@Output() picked = new EventEmitter<string>()` imports EventEmitter from @angular/core, which is not an emitter library, so `this.picked.emit(x)` is rejected.
  R3 Subclass - the receiver is `this` or `self` and the file declares an emitter subclass: `extends EventEmitter`, `extends EventEmitter2`, `extends Emitter` (each with R2's imports_emitter_lib) or `extends EventTarget` (no import needed), or a Python class base `(EventEmitter)` / `(AsyncIOEventEmitter)` with the pyee import.
  R4 Microservices - the needle is `.emit(` and the file names the quoted module `@nestjs/microservices` (a scoped package name, so the plain quoted-module test is enough) (ClientProxy.emit is the emitter conjugate of the @EventPattern handler eventbus.rs already mints).
  None of these -> rejected (`no_bus`). No IMPORT-only admission for these verbs: importing `events` does not make `req.on('data')` a bus.
(4) Unchanged around the gate: LA.41's malformed-literal skip, the verb fallback for an admitted occurrence with no literal (LA.29 parity: `bus.emit(name, x)` -> event_emit:emit), A2.9 broker suppression after the gate, the typed needles, anchors (the admitted site's line).

(1) `fn is_event_name(lit: &str) -> bool` - 1..=128 bytes; no control char (so no 
, , 	); the first char is alphanumeric (char::is_alphanumeric, so non-ASCII names pass) or one of `_ $ @ #`; every other char is alphanumeric or one of `_ . : / - @ $ * # +`, or a single space whose neighbours are both non-space; at least one alphanumeric char. Accepts user.created, order.placed, user:login, POST_ADDED, sensors/temp, cache.flushed, update:modelValue, order.*, `MY TOPIC` (pubsub-js, LA.29's bus_subscribe_still_handles), `some event`; rejects `, `, `, true, false),
    (`, `,
    `, `) {`, ` x`, `x  y`, `--help`, `*`, `{0}.done`, `${id}`.
(2) `fn literal_after(source: &str, at: usize) -> LiteralAt`: `source.get(at..)` (None -> Absent), trim_start (as HEAD); if the first char is not `'` or `"` -> Absent. Otherwise scan BYTES after the quote for the same quote byte; a `
` or `` or end of input first -> Malformed; else body = the slice between the two quote bytes (ASCII delimiters, so the slice is char-safe) and is_event_name(body) ? Name(body) : Malformed. Backtick literals stay Absent (HEAD behaviour).
(3) THE WALK. For a string-keyed needle with extract_name = true, the per-needle search walks occurrences in order: an occurrence first passes LA.29's gates (queue-owned, type site, declaration, bus evidence - only for its two gated needles), then literal_after; Malformed -> `bad_name += 1`, continue from `at + pattern.len()`; Name / Absent -> this is the site (Absent keeps the verb fallback). Needles with extract_name = false (EventBridge.putEvents, handle_event) keep first-occurrence behaviour. Broker suppression (A2.9) runs after, as today. The anchor is the chosen site's line, so a file whose first occurrence is malformed and a later one well formed mints the later one, anchored there.

packets.title: Const-folded queue nodes keep their owner edges: replace_queue_nodes (LA.4) takes the file path and re-runs anchor::attach over the fold's per-site anchors before LA.33's callback binding, so a folded consumer is HANDLED_BY its subscribing function and a const-topic producer is USED by its sending function exactly as a literal-topic node; the edges it re-emits carry their EVIDENCE
packets.rationale:
The chain as specced: LA.4 (W1) adds a post-cache pass `apply_queue_const_topics` (engine/src/build/grafts.rs after L0.6) that re-scans a file's queue needles with a ConstTable resolver and, when a site folds, swaps the file's queue nodes through `queues::replace_queue_nodes(fp, module_id, lang, fold)` - it removes every QUEUE_* node and its module CONTAINS edge and re-appends the fold's consumers and producers. LE.4c (W16) adds `anchors: Vec<anchor::Anchor>` to QueueNodes (one per call site) and anchors queue markers in engine/src/extract.rs through anchor::attach, which gives each node its owner edge (function USES producer, consumer HANDLED_BY function). LA.33 (W21) extends replace_queue_nodes to drop edges and refs touching a queue id the fold did not re-emit (`gone` = old ids minus new ids) and to re-bind consumer callbacks, and states the gap itself: 'LE.4c's owner edges for a folded NEW id are not re-created here (anchor::attach needs the file path, which replace_queue_nodes does not take) - reported to the orchestrator as an LE.4c / LA.4 gap'. Nothing in LA.4 / LE.4c / LA.33 passes the fold's anchors to anchor::attach, so after all three: (a) a sentinel `queue_consumer:unresolved:<fw>` that folds to `queue_consumer:<topic>` (new id) loses its HANDLED_BY - LA.33 deletes the sentinel's and nothing re-creates it; (b) a producer whose topic is a constant in a file that also names the same topic literally keeps the literal site's USES (same id survives) but never gets the constant site's USES; (c) a const-only producer (sentinel -> new id) loses its USES. The `[marker-anchor]` census (LE.4c's `(queue: q to methods, m to module)` token) would count such a folded node as `to module`.
HEAD has none of the three packets, so the owner edges are absent for every queue node. Probe fixture xcut-queue-const-anchor graded on HEAD (installed wheel): nodes 1/2 (queue_producer:orders from the literal retryOrder site; the consumer is queue_consumer:unresolved:kafka), USES 0/2, HANDLED_BY 0/1, CONTAINS 1/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1 (the consumer sentinel). Stderr at HEAD: `[queues] position sites=1 first_line=16 qname=queue_consumer:unresolved:kafka`, `[queues] position sites=1 first_line=12 qname=queue_producer:orders`, `[const] repo table: 2 bindings from 1 files (0 conflicts)`. Predicted after LA.4 + LE.4c + LA.33 without this packet: nodes 2/2, USES 1/2 (retryOrder only), HANDLED_BY 0/1, forbid 0 - the implementing agent records the real pre-fix grade on its tree first (fixture-first).
Graph queries: find emit_queue_nodes -> queues.rs:604; find attach -> anchor.rs:215 (impact --backward on attach returns nothing: its callers engine/src/extract.rs:283 and engine/src/build.rs:374 graft_rpc_markers are grep-confirmed - graft_rpc_markers is the precedent for calling attach post-cache with the path).
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs replace_queue_nodes (created by LA.4, extended by LA.33) - `(fp, module_id, lang, fold)` -> `(fp: &mut FileParse, path: &str, module_id: NodeId, lang: &str, fold: ConstFold) -> usize` (owner edges added); after the swap, LA.33's `gone` retain and before bind_consumer_callbacks: `crate::anchor::attach(fp, path, module_id, &mut anchors)` over the fold's consumer + producer anchors

parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs replace_queue_nodes - the re-appended module CONTAINS edges and the attach tail get their EVIDENCE (repo_graph_code_domain::evidence::stamp_missing with `extractor:queues` / `extractor:anchor`, the attribution LC.3a gives the same edges at extraction)

engine/src/build/grafts.rs apply_queue_const_topics (LA.4) - passes `path` (it already iterates `files`), sums the returned count into QueueConstStats.owner_edges and prints it in the `[queue-const]` marker
engine/tests/queue_const_topics.rs (LA.4) - new test folded_queue_nodes_keep_their_owner_edges
parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs #[cfg(test)] - new unit tests replace_queue_nodes_reanchors_folded_sites and const_fold_anchors_every_folded_site
packets.implementation:
DESIGN. Alternatives weighed: (a) call anchor::attach from grafts.rs after replace_queue_nodes returns (the graft_rpc_markers precedent, no signature change) - rejected: attach would then run AFTER LA.33's bind_consumer_callbacks, the reverse of the extraction order in engine/src/extract.rs (attach, then bind), so a folded file's edge list would be ordered differently from a literal file's and the one function that promises 'the fold re-emits a file's queue nodes exactly as extraction does' would no longer own the whole re-emit. (b) CHOSEN: replace_queue_nodes takes `path` and runs attach itself, in extraction order. Its only caller is apply_queue_const_topics.
queues.rs (~45 LOC). In replace_queue_nodes, before the swap: `let mut anchors: Vec<Anchor> = Vec::new(); anchors.extend(std::mem::take(&mut fold.consumers.anchors)); anchors.extend(std::mem::take(&mut fold.producers.anchors));` (consumers then producers, the append order). The swap (LA.4) and the `gone` retain (LA.33) run unchanged; the re-appended queue CONTAINS edges get `evidence::stamp_missing(&mut appended, "extractor:queues")` before they are extended into fp.edges (the stage stamp LC.3a's run_with_edges! gives them at extraction). Then: `let before = fp.edges.len(); crate::anchor::attach(fp, path, module_id, &mut anchors); evidence::stamp_missing(&mut fp.edges[before..], "extractor:anchor"); let added = fp.edges.len() - before;` and then LA.33's bind_consumer_callbacks exactly as it is. attach's own guarantees do the rest: every queue node already carries POSITION (A2.8), so no cell changes; the module CONTAINS it would add as a fallback is already present, so it is not duplicated; an owner edge that survived the swap (a literal site of a same-id node) is not emitted twice (attach dedups against fp.edges); anchors are sorted by (line, node id) inside attach, so the output order is deterministic. LE.4c's per-site anchor push in emit_queue_nodes should cover folded sites, because LA.4 records a folded site through the same site path as a literal one; CHECK it with the new queues.rs unit test `const_fold_anchors_every_folded_site` (~25 LOC): extract_queue_nodes_with_consts over the fixture's svc/bus.ts text with a resolver mapping ORDERS_TOPIC -> orders and PAYMENTS_TOPIC -> payments yields producers.anchors == [(queue_producer:orders, 8), (queue_producer:orders, 12)] and consumers.anchors == [(queue_consumer:payments, 16)] (0-indexed send / subscribe lines) and, if LE.4c put the push only on the literal-topic branch, move it to the shared site record in emit_queue_nodes (same file). Returns `added`.
engine/src/build/grafts.rs (~15 LOC). apply_queue_const_topics already iterates `files` as (path, source): pass `path` to replace_queue_nodes; QueueConstStats gains `owner_edges: usize` (sum of the returns); LA.4's marker becomes `[queue-const] folded {folded} topic sites in {files} files (unresolved={unresolved}) owner_edges={owner_edges} repo={label}` (the new token sits before ` repo=`).
TESTS. queues.rs `replace_queue_nodes_reanchors_folded_sites` (~60 LOC): a FileParse holding a MODULE, two FUNCTION nodes with POSITION spans (lines 7-9 `publishOrder`, 15-17 `listen`, the anchor.rs test-helper shape) and a sentinel QUEUE_CONSUMER `queue_consumer:unresolved:kafka` with its module CONTAINS and a HANDLED_BY -> listen; a ConstFold whose consumer is `queue_consumer:payments` (anchor line 16) and whose producer is `queue_producer:orders` (anchors lines 8 and 12, the second outside any function). After replace_queue_nodes(fp, "svc/bus.ts", module, "typescript", fold): no edge names the sentinel id; exactly one `queue_consumer:payments -HANDLED_BY-> listen`; exactly one `publishOrder -USES-> queue_producer:orders`; exactly one CONTAINS module -> each queue node; every edge touching a queue node carries exactly one EVIDENCE cell (`Evidence::of(e)` emitter extractor:anchor for USES / HANDLED_BY, extractor:queues for CONTAINS); the return value is 2. engine/tests/queue_const_topics.rs `folded_queue_nodes_keep_their_owner_edges`: generate_one over bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcut-queue-const-anchor - edges (svc::bus::publishOrder USES queue_producer:orders), (svc::bus::retryOrder USES queue_producer:orders) and (queue_consumer:payments HANDLED_BY svc::bus::listen) each exist exactly once; no node qname starts with `queue_consumer:unresolved:` or `queue_producer:unresolved:`; each of those three owner edges has `Evidence::of(e)` (LC.3a's code-domain API) with emitter == "extractor:anchor", and every CONTAINS svc::bus -> QUEUE_* edge has emitter "extractor:queues".
FIXTURE bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/xcut-queue-const-anchor (verbatim below; cross-file SCREAMING_CASE constants, one literal control).

packets.title: The parse cache is written only when it changed: ParseCache::save skips the write when the serialized bytes equal parse_cache.bin on disk, as the store already does for shards and the manifest
packets.rationale: Added mid-run 2026-09-19 at James's request (verbatim: "i think we probably should add the write only if changed thing just anyways. probs into the leap"). MEASURED on James's machine: the repo-graph MCP server (pre-leap wheel, cwd glia) had written ~1.2 TB (/proc/<pid>/io write_bytes 1,206,125,252,608) in about a day, rewriting the 21 MB `.ai/repo-graph/parse_cache.bin` about every 1.4 s (11 rewrites in 15 s, 14.8 MiB/s). The trigger is repo-graph's watcher rebuilding on read-only inotify events (LG.5a hands that off). The amplifier is glia's: `ParseCache::save` (engine/src/cache.rs) serializes and writes the whole cache on EVERY build, even when no entry changed, while the store already skips unchanged shards and an unchanged manifest (store/src/layout.rs, skip-when-unchanged) and `persist::write_self_ignore` already skips an identical `.gitignore`. An incremental build with no source change should write nothing.
entry_points: engine/src/cache.rs ParseCache::save - after `bincode::serialize`, compare with the existing `<dir>/parse_cache.bin` (length first, then bytes); when identical, skip the tmp write + rename and print the unchanged marker; otherwise keep today's per-pid tmp + atomic rename
engine/src/cache.rs mod tests - the new tests beside the existing tmp-name tests
packets.implementation: Compare against the on-disk file, not a digest remembered at load: another writer may have replaced the file since this process loaded it, and comparing with what is actually there is right in both cases (identical -> nothing to do; different -> write ours, as today). Read the existing file only when its length (std::fs::metadata) equals the new byte length, so a changed cache costs no extra read. Keep `write_self_ignore` before the comparison (it is already idempotent). Keep save best-effort: a failed read of the old file means write, never an error. Do not change the cache format, CACHE_VERSION or the serialized bytes - bincode over the BTreeMap is already deterministic (byte_identical relies on it).
packets.acceptance: New unit tests in engine/src/cache.rs: (1) save_twice_unchanged_does_not_rewrite - save a cache, record the file's inode + mtime (std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt), save the same cache again -> inode and mtime unchanged and no `parse_cache.bin.<pid>.tmp` left; (2) save_after_change_rewrites - change one entry, save -> the file's bytes equal the new serialization; (3) save_when_on_disk_differs_rewrites - overwrite the file with different bytes of the same length, save -> rewritten. `cargo test -p <engine package> --lib cache` and `--test byte_identical` green; `engine/tests/generate_many_incremental.rs` green.
